### 🐛 Describe the bug # Describe the bug Version: vLLM `0.17.1` Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-GPTQ-Int8` Hardware reproduced on: `NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090`, single GPU ## Summary I found a frontend-legal request-lifecycle bug in the resumable `streaming_update` path. The reproducer sends one live request (`req2`) and then legally updates the same request twice with `streaming_update`. While those two updates are being processed, async queue lag and shared-prefix reuse are both still active. Under that combination, vLLM rebuilds the renewed `req2` state, schedules speculative placeholder tokens for it, but the worker-side input row is no longer fully backed by real token ids. As a result, the prepared host-side input row for `req2` contains `-1` values before model execution starts. On the re-verified Qwen3 standalone run, the visible non-blocking failure is a CUDA `device-side assert` in the FlashAttention execution path. The important point is that the bad row already exists before the GPU failure. This is not a random backend crash, and it is not the same issue as the same-id placeholder-underflow bug or the older prompt-width overflow bug. ## Trigger chain 1. Submit `req0` and `req1` so the engine is already running a live mixed batch. 2. Submit `req2` as a resumable late request. 3. Send a first legal `streaming_update` for the same live `req2`. 4. Let async scheduling queue work for the current mixed batch, but do not drain all queued work yet. 5. Send a second legal `streaming_update` for the same live `req2` while shared-prefix reuse is still active. 6. vLLM rebuilds the renewed `req2`, but the worker-side row for `req2` no longer has real token ids for every placeholder-backed position. 7. The prepared host-side row already contains `-1` values. 8. When model execution consumes that row, the run fails with a CUDA `device-side assert`. ## Details ### Trigger path in code 1. The request state accepts legal streaming continuation and appends the new prompt fragment to the existing request state. ```python # vllm/v1/engine/output_processor.py def apply_streaming_update(self, update: StreamingUpdate) -> None: if self.prompt_token_ids: self.prompt_token_ids.extend(update.prompt_token_ids or ()) else: self.prompt_token_ids = update.prompt_token_ids or [] self.prompt_len = len(self.prompt_token_ids) ``` 2. In the scheduler path, resumable session handling keeps already-computed output tokens, folds them back into the same request's prompt, and then appends the new update tokens. ```python # vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py kept_output_tokens = session._all_token_ids[ session.num_prompt_tokens : num_computed_tokens ] session.prompt_token_ids.extend(kept_output_tokens) session._all_token_ids.extend(update.prompt_token_ids or ()) session.prompt_token_ids.extend(update.prompt_token_ids or ()) ``` This is why the bug is about a renewed live request, not a brand-new unrelated request. 3. Under async scheduling, vLLM adds output placeholders for each scheduled request, including speculative decode positions. ```python # vllm/v1/core/sched/async_scheduler.py cur_num_spec_tokens = len(spec_decode_tokens.get(req_id, ())) request.num_output_placeholders += 1 + cur_num_spec_tokens request.spec_token_ids = self._spec_token_placeholders ``` 4. The scheduler then exposes those placeholder-backed speculative positions in `scheduled_spec_decode_tokens`. ```python # vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py num_scheduled_spec_tokens = ( num_new_tokens + request.num_computed_tokens - request.num_tokens - request.num_output_placeholders ) if num_scheduled_spec_tokens > 0: scheduled_spec_decode_tokens[request.request_id] = spec_token_ids ``` 5. On the worker side, async scheduling constructs `prev_req_id_to_index` from the previous batch rows and appends placeholder `-1` tokens to per-request cached output state. ```python # vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py prev_req_id_to_index: dict[str, int] = {} for i, req_id in enumerate(self.input_batch.req_ids): if i in discard_req_indices_set: continue prev_req_id_to_index[req_id] = i if (req_state := self.requests.get(req_id)) is not None: req_state.output_token_ids.append(-1) self.input_batch.prev_req_id_to_index = prev_req_id_to_index ``` 6. Later, `_prepare_input_ids()` tries to reconstruct the next-step input row by mapping current request ids back to the previous batch rows and by replaying speculative positions. ```python # vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py prev_req_id_to_index = self.input_batch.prev_req_id_to_index scheduled_spec_tokens = scheduler_output.scheduled_spec_decode_tokens for req_id, cur_index in self.input_batch.req_id_to_index.items(): if (prev_index := prev_req_id_to_index.get(req_id)) is not None: draft_len = len(scheduled_spec_tokens.get(req_id, ())) sample_flattened_indices.append(flattened_index - draft_len) spec_flattened_indices.extend( range(flattened_index - draft_len + 1, flattened_index + 1) ) ``` 7. In this issue, the renewed `req2` still has placeholder-backed future positions, but the worker can no longer fully materialize every one of those positions into a real token-backed row. The host-side prepared row already carries `-1` values before execution enters the attention backend. 8. The visible failure then occurs when the model consumes that row in the FlashAttention path. ```python # vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py flash_attn_varlen_func( q=query[:num_actual_tokens], k=key_cache, v=value_cache, out=output[:num_actual_tokens], ... ) ``` The re-verified standalone run ends here with `CUDA error: device-side assert triggered`. ### Local script breakdown `repro_g11_cp64_placeholder_local.py` is a standalone local reproducer. - It reads the Qwen3 checkpoint path from `VLLM_POC_G11_MODEL` or the built-in `/path/to/qwen3` placeholder - It creates one `EngineCore` directly - It submits: - one anchor request - one overlapping peer request - one resumable late request - The late request is submitted as: - chunk 0 - first same-request `streaming_update` - second same-request `streaming_update` - It preserves async queue lag between the first and second update - It also preserves shared-prefix reuse for the late request - It writes: - `campaign.json` - `repro_config.json` - `request_history.json` - `request_states.json` - `action_log.json` - `post_run_summary.json` - `error.txt` on failure ## Local repro - Official Hugging Face repo: [Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-GPTQ-Int8](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-GPTQ-Int8) - Please download `Qwen3-0.6B-GPTQ-Int8` and run my reproduce script [repro_g11_cp64_placeholder_local.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27694875/repro_g11_cp64_placeholder_local.py) ```bash export POC_PY=/path/to/python3 export G11_LOCAL=/path/to/repro_g11_cp64_placeholder_local.py export VLLM_POC_G11_MODEL=/path/to/qwen3 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 "$POC_PY" "$G11_LOCAL" \ --model "$VLLM_POC_G11_MODEL" \ --run-name g11_cp64_placeholder_local ``` Optional blocking attribution: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 "$POC_PY" "$G11_LOCAL" \ --model "$VLLM_POC_G11_MODEL" \ --run-name g11_cp64_placeholder_blocking \ --blocking ``` ## Reproduce Environment | Item | Value | | --- | --- | | OS | Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS | | Kernel | Linux 6.5.0-35-generic | | GPU | 2 x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 | | GPU memory | 24564 MiB each | | Driver | 570.86.10 | | CUDA runtime | 12.8 (`nvidia-smi`) | | CUDA toolkit | 12.8.61 (`nvcc`) | | Python | 3.12.9 | | vLLM | 0.17.1 | | PyTorch | 2.10.0+cu128 | | transformers | 4.56.1 | | tokenizers | 0.22.0 | | flash_attn | 2.8.3 | | triton | 3.6.0 | | numpy | 2.0.2 | ## Observed result Representative traceback from the re-verified non-blocking standalone run: ```text File ".../vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py", line 724, in forward flash_attn_varlen_func( File ".../vllm/vllm_flash_attn/flash_attn_interface.py", line 300, in flash_attn_varlen_func out, softmax_lse = torch.ops._vllm_fa2_C.varlen_fwd( torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered ``` ## Root cause This is not a malformed-input bug, and it is not a random GPU-only failure. The problem is that vLLM legally continues the same live request twice through `streaming_update`, while async queued work from the earlier state is still in flight and shared-prefix reuse is still active. Under that combination, the renewed `req2` state and the worker-side input row stop agreeing with each other. In the verified run, the scheduler still treats some future positions for `req2` as valid placeholder-backed tokens, but the worker-side row that is prepared for the next model step is no longer fully backed by real token ids. That is why `-1` values are already present in the prepared host-side row before the model executes. So the real bug is in how the renewed request state, async placeholder-backed future output, and worker-side row reconstruction interact. The later CUDA `device-side assert` is the consequence of the model consuming that already-bad row. ## Attachments The attachment bundle for this report should contain: - `repro_g11_cp64_placeholder_local.py` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug]: ngram_gpu speculative decoding can propose draft tokens past max_model_len budget
signals.text:
### Environment Current `main` at commit `a8887c208f34c04c3b021cf3949ed6545d77bb01`. Tested on a Google Cloud A100 VM: - Driver: 580.126.20 - Python: 3.10.12 - vLLM: `0.20.2rc1.dev310+ga8887c208` from source/editable checkout - PyTorch: `2.11.0+cu130` - CUDA used to build PyTorch: 13.0 `python -m vllm.collect_env` excerpt: ```text ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 11.4.0-1ubuntu1~22.04.3) 11.4.0 Libc version : glibc-2.35 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.11.0+cu130 CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.10.12 (main, Mar 3 2026, 11:56:32) [GCC 11.4.0] Python platform : Linux-6.8.0-1053-gcp-x86_64-with-glibc2.35 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True GPU models and configuration : GPU 0: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB Nvidia driver version : 580.126.20 cuDNN version : 9.13.0 libraries present ============================== vLLM Info ============================== vLLM Version : 0.20.2rc1.dev310+ga8887c208 (git sha: a8887c208) vLLM Build Flags: CUDA Archs: Not Set; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled ``` ### Bug The V1 `ngram_gpu` speculative proposer can report valid draft tokens even when the target sequence has no remaining `max_model_len` budget. The CPU n-gram proposer has an explicit cap: ```python k = min(k, max_model_len - total_token) if k <= 0: return np.empty((0,), dtype=origin_tokens.dtype) ``` The GPU path computes draft validity from the kernel output and `combined_mask`, but does not also clamp by: ```python remaining = max_model_len - num_tokens_tmp position < remaining ``` ### Temporary instrumentation used I added this immediately after the `self.kernel(...)` call in `NgramProposerGPU.propose`: ```python remaining = (self.max_model_len - num_tokens_tmp).clamp(min=0, max=self.k) bad = num_valid_draft_tokens > remaining if bad.any().item(): bad_rows = torch.nonzero(bad, as_tuple=False).flatten() dump_rows = [] for row_tensor in bad_rows[:8]: row = int(row_tensor.item()) nt = int(num_tokens_tmp[row].item()) tail_start = max(0, nt - 32) dump_rows.append({ "batch_row": row, "num_tokens_no_spec": int(num_tokens_no_spec[row].item()), "valid_sampled_tokens_count": int(valid_sampled_tokens_count[row].item()), "num_tokens_tmp": nt, "remaining": int(remaining[row].item()), "draft_tokens": draft_tokens[row].detach().cpu().tolist(), "num_valid_draft_tokens": int(num_valid_draft_tokens[row].item()), "token_ids_tail": token_ids_gpu[row, tail_start:nt].detach().cpu().tolist(), "max_model_len": self.max_model_len, "k": self.k, }) print("NGRAM_GPU_MAX_MODEL_LEN_VIOLATION", dump_rows, flush=True) raise RuntimeError( "ngram_gpu proposed more draft tokens than remaining max_model_len budget" ) ``` I also logged the upstream drafter guard around `input_fits_in_drafter` in `GPUModelRunner`. ### Minimal repro script ```python from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams spec = { "method": "ngram_gpu", "num_speculative_tokens": 1, "prompt_lookup_min": 2, "prompt_lookup_max": 5, } llm = LLM( model="facebook/opt-125m", max_model_len=17, enforce_eager=True, gpu_memory_utilization=0.5, speculative_config=spec, seed=1234, ) prompt = "def f(x):
 return x + 1

" # 15 OPT tokens params = SamplingParams( temperature=0.0, max_tokens=64, ignore_eos=True, seed=1234, ) out = llm.generate([prompt], params) print(out[0].outputs[0].text) ``` ### Observed output with instrumentation ```text NGRAM_GPU_DRAFTER_GUARD max_seq_len=15 num_spec_tokens=1 effective_drafter_max_model_len=17 input_fits_in_drafter=True NGRAM_GPU_DRAFTER_GUARD max_seq_len=16 num_spec_tokens=1 effective_drafter_max_model_len=17 input_fits_in_drafter=True NGRAM_GPU_MAX_MODEL_LEN_VIOLATION [{'batch_row': 0, 'num_tokens_no_spec': 16, 'valid_sampled_tokens_count': 1, 'num_tokens_tmp': 17, 'remaining': 0, 'draft_tokens': [1437], 'num_valid_draft_tokens': 1, 'token_ids_tail': [2, 9232, 856, 1640, 1178, 3256, 50118, 1437, 1437, 1437, 671, 3023, 2055, 112, 50140, 1437, 1437], 'max_model_len': 17, 'k': 1}] RuntimeError: ngram_gpu proposed more draft tokens than remaining max_model_len budget ``` This shows `num_tokens_tmp == max_model_len == 17`, `remaining == 0`, but `num_valid_draft_tokens == 1` and `draft_tokens == [1437]`. ### CPU ngram and no-spec comparison Same prompt, same model, same `max_model_len=17`, same `num_speculative_tokens=1`, only changing the speculative method: ```text method: ngram PROMPT_TOKEN_IDS 15 OUTPUT_TOKEN_IDS 2 FINISH_REASON length TEXT_HEAD ' ' ``` No speculative decoding: ```text method: none PROMPT_TOKEN_IDS 15 OUTPUT_TOKEN_IDS 2 FINISH_REASON length TEXT_HEAD ' ' ``` Both stop cleanly at the context boundary. The invariant violation is specific to `ngram_gpu`. ### Additional note With larger settings like `max_model_len=64`, prompt length 60, and `num_speculative_tokens=4`, `ngram_gpu` also reached a CUDA device-side assert in `Indexing.cu` after the upstream guard logged `input_fits_in_drafter=False`. The reduced `k=1` instrumentation above is the cleaner repro because it catches the leaf invariant directly before that asynchronous CUDA failure path. This is distinct from GDN/Mamba n-gram speculative issues: the repro uses `facebook/opt-125m` and V1 `method="ngram_gpu"` only. ### Expected behavior `ngram_gpu` should never report more valid draft tokens than the remaining target `max_model_len` budget. It should match the CPU n-gram proposer behavior and return zero/capped draft tokens near the boundary. ### Possible fix direction Clamp/mask by remaining budget in `NgramProposerGPU.propose` or `NgramGPUKernel.forward`, for example: ```python remaining = (self.max_model_len - num_tokens_tmp).clamp(min=0, max=self.k) combined_mask &= remaining > 0 draft_tokens = torch.where( torch.arange(self.k, device=device).unsqueeze(0) < remaining.unsqueeze(1), draft_tokens, torch.full_like(draft_tokens, -1), ) num_valid_draft_tokens = torch.minimum(num_valid_draft_tokens, remaining) ``` A regression test should construct a repeated n-gram near `max_model_len` and assert GPU and CPU n-gram proposal lengths agree.

signals.title: [RFC]: Split Flashattn Forward for Prefill/Decode Separation
signals.text: ### Motivation. ## Summary Separate the attention forward computation into prefill and decode paths, using `flash_attn_varlen_func` for prefill and `flash_attn_with_kvcache` for decode tokens. ## Motivation 1. **Different access patterns**: Prefill accesses full KV sequences while decode accesses sparse KV cache entries. 2. **API optimization**: `flash_attn_with_kvcache` is optimized for block-based KV cache lookups during decode. 3. **Prefix caching**: Support explicit `cu_prefix_kv_lens` for better prefix caching strategy. ### Proposed Change. ## Detailed Design ### Data Flow ### Implementation Refer to vllm-metax: https://github.com/MetaX-MACA/vLLM-metax/blob/v0.19.0-dev/vllm_metax/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py#L1085 ### Backward Compatibility - Default behavior unchanged - New behavior enabled by `VLLM_ENABLE_FA_SPLIT_FORWARD` ## Questions for Upstream 1. Would upstream accept this split if it doesn't change behavior for existing use cases? 2. Is there interest in making this configurable? ### Feedback Period. _No response_ ### CC List. _No response_ ### Any Other Things. _No response_ ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug]: Multiple model files still trigger ImageProcessorFast DeprecationWarning post transformers v5.4 refactor
signals.text: ### What Static imports of deprecated `*ImageProcessorFast` symbols still trigger transformers `DeprecationWarning` across four model files under `vllm/model_executor/models/`. #42700 fixed the same family for `qwen3_vl.py` (one file); the other four were not covered. ### Reproduction ``` $ docker run --rm --gpus '"device=1"' --entrypoint python3 \ vllm/vllm-openai:v0.20.0 -W default -c \ "import vllm.model_executor.models.lfm2_vl" [transformers] Accessing `Lfm2VlImageProcessorFast` from `.models.lfm2_vl.image_processing_lfm2_vl`. Returning `Lfm2VlImageProcessor` instead. Behavior may be different and this alias will be removed in future versions. ``` Same form of warning fires on each of: | File | Imported symbol | Replacement (per transformers warning text) | |---|---|---| | `vllm/model_executor/models/lfm2_vl.py` | `Lfm2VlImageProcessorFast` (+ `find_closest_aspect_ratio`, `round_by_factor` from the deprecated submodule path) | `Lfm2VlImageProcessor` | | `vllm/model_executor/models/gemma3n_mm.py` | `SiglipImageProcessorFast` | `SiglipImageProcessor` | | `vllm/model_executor/models/interns1.py` | `GotOcr2ImageProcessorFast` | `GotOcr2ImageProcessor` | | `vllm/model_executor/models/cohere2_vision.py` | `Cohere2VisionImageProcessorFast` | `Cohere2VisionImageProcessor` | Sanity check the inverse: `vllm/transformers_utils/processors/{qwen_vl,glm4v}.py` define internal classes that inherit `BaseImageProcessorFast`. The same probe **does not** raise any warning for these — `BaseImageProcessorFast` is still the canonical export. So the surface is import-site only, four files. ### Background - huggingface/transformers#43514 (merged 2026-03-19, "🚨🚨 Refactor Image Processors to support different backends") dropped the `Fast` suffix for image processors and reshaped the underlying class layout. - vLLM's `requirements/common.txt` already pins around the breaking transitions (`!= 5.4.*, != 5.5.0`), but the import-site warnings on the four files above remain visible on every load. ### Question for maintainers Same as #42688's resolution — swap the imports for the un-suffixed canonical names across these four files, mirroring #42700's pattern. I'll send the follow-up PR shortly. Happy to scope it differently if there's an internal sweep planned.

signals.title: [Bug]: Forked workers retain stale CUDA primary contexts from parent process
signals.text: ## Your current environment vLLM main (latest) and v0.8.5.post1, tested on H100 multi-GPU (tp=2). ## How would you like to use vllm I'm working on integrating NVIDIA's `cuda-checkpoint` tool with vLLM for near-zero cold starts (related to RFC #34303). During multi-GPU testing, I discovered that forked worker processes retain the parent's CUDA primary context for GPU 0, even when the worker is assigned to GPU 1. ## Before submitting a new issue... - [x] I have searched existing issues - [x] I have read the relevant documentation ## Describe the bug When vLLM uses the `fork` multiprocessing method (the default on Linux), child worker processes inherit the parent's active CUDA primary contexts for **all** devices. A worker assigned to GPU 1 ends up with **two** active primary contexts: GPU 0 (inherited from parent) and GPU 1 (its own). This causes two problems: 1. **Wasted GPU memory** - the stale GPU 0 context in the GPU 1 worker holds driver-level allocations that never get freed 2. **NVIDIA cuda-checkpoint failures** - `cuda-checkpoint --action restore` fails with "invalid argument" because it tries to restore both contexts in the worker process, but the GPU 0 context is stale and cannot be restored ### Reproduction ```python # In a forked worker process assigned to GPU 1: import ctypes, torch libcuda = ctypes.CDLL("libcuda.so.1") libcuda.cuInit(0) for dev_id in range(torch.cuda.device_count()): dev = ctypes.c_int() libcuda.cuDeviceGet(ctypes.byref(dev), dev_id) flags = ctypes.c_uint() state = ctypes.c_int() libcuda.cuDevicePrimaryCtxGetState(dev, ctypes.byref(flags), ctypes.byref(state)) print(f"GPU {dev_id}: active={state.value != 0}") # Output: # GPU 0: active=True <-- STALE, inherited from parent # GPU 1: active=True <-- worker's actual device ``` ### Root cause In `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py`, `Worker.init_device()` calls `torch.accelerator.set_device_index(self.device)` to set the worker's device, but never releases inherited primary contexts from other devices. The parent process may have initialized CUDA on GPU 0 before forking, and that context persists in the child. ### Fix Call `cuDevicePrimaryCtxRelease()` for all non-assigned devices after setting the worker's device. I have a PR ready with the fix and a test. ### Impact This is a correctness issue for any external tooling that enumerates per-process CUDA contexts (cuda-checkpoint, GPU memory profilers, container checkpoint/restore). It also causes a small but unnecessary memory waste per worker process.

signals.title: [Bug]: v0.21.0 release notes claim 'DeepSeek V4: AMD/ROCm support' but stock vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.21.0 fails to bring up DeepSeek-V4-Flash on MI350X (mhc_post_tilelang → PDL is not supported); the official recipes YAML marks every AMD SKU as unsupported
signals.text: ## Your current environment The reproduction pod has been reclaimed by other workloads, so a fresh `python collect_env.py` is not available; relevant fields gathered in-pod during the run: <details> <summary>Environment (captured in-pod during the failing run)</summary> ```text Container image: vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.21.0 (official vllm-project release image) vllm: 0.21.0 (/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/__init__.py) PyTorch: 2.10.0+git8514f05 HIP runtime: 7.2.53211 Platform: ROCm 7.2.53 GPU: 8x AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950) 288 GiB HBM each (294592 MiB) 256 CUs, 160 KiB shared_memory_per_block current_platform: is_rocm()=True, is_fp8_fnuz()=False, fp8_dtype()=torch.float8_e4m3fn, capability=(9, 5) Tokenizer: deepseek_v4 (per --tokenizer-mode) Model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash (canonical HF repo, 46 shards / ~159 GB, FP4+FP8 mixed per the model card) Cluster: Kubernetes (DigitalOcean DOKS), MI350X partition. ``` </details> ## 🐛 Describe the bug ### Summary The v0.21.0 release notes list **"DeepSeek V4: AMD/ROCm support (#40871)"** under Model Support, but on the official `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.21.0` image, attempting to serve `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` on MI350X (gfx950) fails during `profile_run` in the `mhc_post_tilelang` op with a hard TVM/TileLang `LogFatal`: ``` tvm.error.InternalError: Check failed: (!mutator.has_trigger_launch_ && !mutator.has_grid_sync_) is false: PDL is not supported ``` PDL = NVIDIA Hopper's Programmatic Dependent Launch — a CUDA-only feature. The TileLang pass `MarkCudaSyncCalls` refuses an IR that emits `trigger_launch` / `grid_sync` ops when targeting AMD. The path is reached from the DSv4 model's `forward` → `torch.ops.vllm.mhc_fused_post_pre` → `mhc.py:717 mhc_post_tilelang` → TileLang JIT compile. Additionally, the canonical recipe source backing [recipes.vllm.ai](https://recipes.vllm.ai) marks **every AMD SKU as `unsupported`** for both DSv4-Pro and DSv4-Flash (see [`DeepSeek-V4-Flash.yaml`](https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/blob/main/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash.yaml) and [`DeepSeek-V4-Pro.yaml`](https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/blob/main/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro.yaml)): ```yaml hardware: h200: verified b200: verified gb200: verified b300: verified gb300: verified mi300x: unsupported mi325x: unsupported mi355x: unsupported ``` So the release notes claim AMD/ROCm support, while the official recipes — same project — say it is `unsupported`. As a user reading the release notes first, this contradiction is the actual cost: ~half a day of triage on real hardware before discovering it. There is already a merged main-branch PR that adds AMD MHC support (#41946 "[Bugfix] [ROCm] [DSV4] [Perf] Add aiter mhc support", merged 2026-05-13), but it **did not make the v0.21.0 cut** at commit `ad7125a` (`git log v0.21.0 --grep="(#41946)"` returns nothing). The remaining AMD fallbacks for the rest of the Flash variant are in **open PR #41136** (`lcskrishna/vllm:deepseekv4-rocm`, currently `state=open, mergeable_state=dirty`). ### Reproduction Launch command (adapted from the only recipe-shaped doc that exists for AMD, [`wuhuikx/recipes#433`](https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/pull/433) — unmerged PR self-labeled `[Do not merge]`; the official YAML provides no AMD command since AMD is `unsupported`). The `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` is required because `vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v4.py:1636` asserts on it: ```bash export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \ --dtype auto --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --max-num-seqs 16 --max-num-batched-tokens 1024 \ --distributed-executor-backend mp \ --trust-remote-code \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.35 \ --moe-backend triton_unfused \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --async-scheduling --enforce-eager ``` ### What works Everything up to the first forward pass succeeds: - Engine config wires up cleanly: `quantization=deepseek_v4_fp8`, `kv_cache_dtype=fp8`, `tensor_parallel_size=4`, `enforce_eager=True`, `moe_backend='triton_unfused'`, `tokenizer_mode='deepseek_v4'`. - All 4 TP workers spawn, NCCL/RCCL collectives initialize, `aiter` imports. - 46/46 safetensors shards load in 233 s (`default_loader.py:397 "Loading weights took 233.04 seconds"`). - KV cache backend registers as `fp8_ds_mla` (`deepseek_v4_attention.py:714 "Using DeepSeek's fp8_ds_mla KV cache format."`). ### What fails `gpu_worker.determine_available_memory` → `model_runner.profile_run` → dummy forward: ```text File "vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v4.py", line 1235, in forward residual, post_mix, res_mix, x = torch.ops.vllm.mhc_fused_post_pre(...) File "vllm/model_executor/layers/mhc.py", line 717, in mhc_fused_post_pre mhc_post_tilelang(...) File "tilelang/jit/__init__.py", line 465, in __call__ kernel = self.compile(*args, **kwargs) File "tilelang/engine/lower.py", line 311, in lower mod = OptimizeForTarget(mod, target) File "tilelang/engine/phase.py", line 272, in OptimizeForTarget mod = tilelang.transform.MarkCudaSyncCalls(have_pdl(target))(mod) ... tvm.error.InternalError: Check failed: (!mutator.has_trigger_launch_ && !mutator.has_grid_sync_) is false: PDL is not supported ``` All 4 workers crash identically. EngineCore then raises: ```text RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'Check failed: (!mutator.has_trigger_launch_ && !mutator.has_grid_sync_) is false: PDL is not supported' ``` No tokens are ever generated. ### Why this is a bug worth reporting (not "your hardware is unsupported") The hardware-unsupported signal exists in `recipes.vllm.ai`, but **not** in the v0.21.0 release notes, which read "DeepSeek V4: AMD/ROCm support (#40871)" — a phrase a downstream reader will reasonably interpret as "Flash on at least one MI3xx SKU runs in 0.21.0". The two sources contradict each other. Additionally, the user-facing failure is a TVM C++ `LogFatal` deep in TileLang lowering, with no actionable up-front platform check. There is no message saying "DSv4 MHC has no AMD fallback in this build; see #41136" — the user has to dig into the stack to discover that. ### Suggested fixes (any one of these would help) 1. **Reconcile the docs.** Either narrow the release-notes claim (e.g., "initial AMD/ROCm enablement landed in #40871; functional Flash support on MI3xx requires fallbacks that are still in flight in #41136 and were not all included in 0.21.0"), or — if the intent was that Pro on MI355X is actually verified — update the recipes YAMLs to reflect a `preview` / `partial` status rather than `unsupported`. 2. **Add an explicit platform check at `mhc_post_tilelang` entry** so users on ROCm get a clear error pointing to #41136 and #41946, rather than a TVM C++ check failing inside TileLang IR lowering. 3. **Consider a v0.21.1 cut that picks up #41946** (which is already merged on main but missed the 0.21.0 tag), so the gap between "release notes says supported" and "Flash runs on AMD" shrinks. ### Related - Release notes for v0.21.0: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/releases/tag/v0.21.0 - Base AMD enablement PR cited in release notes: #40871 (merged, in 0.21.0) - AMD MHC support: #41946 (merged on main 2026-05-13, **not in v0.21.0**) - Remaining AMD fallbacks for DSv4-Flash: #41136 (open, dirty) - Tracking issue for DSv4 ROCm: #41820 - Existing AMD-specific DSv4 bugs (separate failure modes, not duplicates): #41961, #41962, #41963, #41027 - NVIDIA SM12x equivalent of this MHC issue (closed via a different code path): #40991 - Recipes YAMLs claiming AMD unsupported: - https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/blob/main/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash.yaml - https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/blob/main/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro.yaml cc @hongxiayang @tjtanaa @vllmellm @lcskrishna (per the auto-cc ROCm group).

signals.title: [Feature]: Make DS layout used by default
signals.text: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch Currently vLLM uses SMM Conv state layout set as `SD` `(state_len, dim)`. Recent PR [[Kernel] Mamba support different layout for Conv state#37416](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/37416) has created support for transposed `DS` layout `(dim, state_len)`. Based on perf numbers showed in this PR `DS` layout has ~1.5x better TTFT compared to `SD` layout (perf numbers were taken from PR #37416 description Benchmark section): ``` ================================================================================ BENCHMARK SUMMARY ================================================================================ DS: ------------------------------------------------------------ TP | Req/s | Tok/s | TTFT(ms) | TPOT(ms) ------------------------------------------------------------ 1 | 20.61 | 4009.30 | 128.67 | 23.50 2 | 24.15 | 4686.47 | 119.85 | 21.18 4 | 28.48 | 5556.18 | 112.23 | 18.23 SD: ------------------------------------------------------------ TP | Req/s | Tok/s | TTFT(ms) | TPOT(ms) ------------------------------------------------------------ 1 | 20.34 | 3954.31 | 142.86 | 23.78 2 | 23.86 | 4681.23 | 161.49 | 20.92 4 | 26.63 | 5182.43 | 167.71 | 19.39 ================================================================================ ``` Since `DS` layout shows better performance it is a good reason to use it by default in vLLM because currently is is available only using `VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT =DS` env var. The problem to enable it by default is that @tdoublep commented in PR #37416: ``` > I'd probably have a preference that we just change the layout in all cases, rather than introduce a new env variable, but it looks like the new layout doesn't yet support MTP + "align" mode prefix caching, so it's OK for now. ``` So, in order to enable DS layout by default at first we need to verify if DS supports MTP + "align" mode prefix caching, and if not then add this support. ### Alternatives _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_ ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary Qwen3.5 NVFP4 disaggregated serving with NIXL fails when using heterogeneous prefill/decode parallelism: - Prefill: `4xTEP4` (`4` prefill workers, each `TP4 + expert parallel`, one 4xGB200 node per worker) - Decode: `1xDEP8` (`1` logical decode worker, `DP8 + expert parallel`, spanning two 4xGB200 nodes) - KV cache dtype: `bfloat16` - Prefix caching disabled - Async scheduling disabled - Hybrid KV cache manager explicitly enabled - SSM conv state layout set to `DS` The deployment becomes healthy, but decode NIXL handshakes fail at request time because the local decode block size is `16` and the remote prefill block size is `32`. The connector currently asserts `local_block_size % remote_block_size == 0`, which rejects this case even though the opposite direction is divisible. This makes the configuration unusable for correctness testing: GSM8K accuracy collapses because KV transfers fail and vLLM skips KV post-processing for affected requests. ## Environment - Hardware: 4xGB200 per node - Nodes used in failing run: 6 nodes - Model: `Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4` - vLLM version: `0.20.2rc1.dev354+g24337fb86.precompiled` - Dynamo: `1.2.0.dev20260429` - NIXL: `nixl-cu13==1.0.1`, `nixl==1.0.1` - CUDA base: CUDA 13 runtime ## Related upstream work I found related prior work around heterogeneous NIXL block sizes: - RFC: [[RFC]: Nixl Connector Heterogeneous BlockSize support](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/26744) - PR: [[NIXL] refine decoder side post process for heterogeneous BlockSize and kv_layout](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/30275) The RFC says support for `nP < nD` was completed, but support for `nP > nD` was dropped from scope. This bug appears to hit that unsupported direction in a Qwen3.5 hybrid/HMA configuration: prefill uses physical block size `32`, decode uses physical block size `16`, and decode-side NIXL rejects the transfer during handshake. ## Failing configuration The full resolved recipe is included in the attached log archive as `170987/logs/config.yaml`. The important bits are: ```text prefill: 4 workers, each TP4 + expert-parallel on one 4-GPU GB200 node decode: 1 logical worker, DP8 + expert-parallel across two 4-GPU GB200 nodes VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS kv-cache-dtype=bfloat16 --no-enable-prefix-caching --no-async-scheduling --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail"}' ``` Launch: ```bash srtctl apply -f recipes/qwen3.5/nvfp4/disagg/stp_prefix_off/qwen35-nvfp4-4xTEP4-1xDEP8.yaml ``` ## Expected behavior NIXL should either: - support the reciprocal block-size case where decode local block size is smaller than prefill remote block size (`16` vs `32`), or - fail during startup/health check with a clear unsupported-configuration error. It should not report the server as healthy and then fail per-request NIXL handshakes. ## Actual behavior At request time, decode workers fail NIXL handshake setup: ```text NIXL transfer failure: handshake_setup_failed AssertionError: Local block size 16 is not divisible by remote block size 32 or vice versa. ``` The compatibility hash check passes before this: ```text NIXL compatibility check passed Transfer plan: TransferTopology(tp_ratio=-4, num_kv_heads=2, local_tp=1, remote_tp=4, local_rank=0, remote_block_len=32768) ``` Then requests fail KV loading: ```text NIXL transfer failure: handshake_failed Skipping KV post-processing for failed request ... ``` ## Observed correctness impact Running GSM8K against the failing configuration returned invalid correctness: ```text Accuracy: 0.031 Invalid responses: 0.000 Total output tokens: 8192 ``` This is not a meaningful model-quality result because NIXL transfer errors are present in the decode logs. ## Log excerpt ```text (Worker_DP3_EP3 pid=349953) INFO 05-17 20:14:00 [worker.py:555] NIXL compatibility check passed (hash: 63cfb9d5c28916a5ccc703d83c44c6dec2009cdbaf85edbe0f9cec80e5762d81) (Worker_DP3_EP3 pid=349953) INFO 05-17 20:14:00 [worker.py:1301] Transfer plan: TransferTopology(tp_ratio=-4, num_kv_heads=2, local_tp=1, remote_tp=4, local_rank=0, remote_block_len=32768) (Worker_DP3_EP3 pid=349953) ERROR 05-17 20:14:00 [worker.py:735] NIXL transfer failure: handshake_setup_failed | Context: {'failure_type': 'handshake_setup_failed', 'request_id': None, 'engine_id': '6ff14cc5-a32c-46c9-80ed-801031f38e11_dp0', 'remote_engine_id': '944cb3df-ccb0-4860-9fae-15ec5c53a9ae'} Traceback (most recent call last): File "/opt/vllm/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/worker.py", line 733, in done_callback self._remote_agents[eid] = f.result() File "/usr/lib/python3.12/concurrent/futures/_base.py", line 449, in result return self.__get_result() File "/usr/lib/python3.12/concurrent/futures/_base.py", line 401, in __get_result raise self._exception File "/usr/lib/python3.12/concurrent/futures/thread.py", line 58, in run result = self.fn(*self.args, **self.kwargs) File "/opt/vllm/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/worker.py", line 581, in _nixl_handshake remote_agent_name = self.add_remote_agent( File "/opt/vllm/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/worker.py", line 1320, in add_remote_agent block_size_ratio = transfer_topo.block_size_ratio(nixl_agent_meta.block_size) File "/opt/vllm/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/utils.py", line 519, in block_size_ratio assert self.block_size % remote_block_size == 0, ( AssertionError: Local block size 16 is not divisible by remote block size 32 or vice versa. (Worker_DP3_EP3 pid=349953) WARNING 05-17 20:14:00 [worker.py:1735] Skipping KV post-processing for failed request 5a4c1f4d-e725-40c4-944f-6c0d0584f627-b6ed42d1 ``` Full logs: [170987.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27906144/170987.zip) ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

On the first day, the trains travel for two days. signals.title: [SM120] _dummy_sampler_run hangs indefinitely on RTX 5090 due to top_k=vocab_size-1 triggering an SM120-broken top-k masking kernel (one-line fix)
signals.text: ### Summary On physical RTX 5090 hardware (SM120 / compute_120f), `vllm serve` hangs indefinitely during engine startup. The hang is in `_dummy_sampler_run` (called from `profile_run` → `_initialize_kv_caches`) when it invokes the sampler with `top_k = logits.size(1) - 1` (i.e. `vocab_size - 1`, which is **151935** for `Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct`). Real production sampling uses small `top_k` values (e.g. 40, 50) and does not hang. Substituting a small `top_k` in the dummy run resolves the startup hang with no functional regression — the dummy sampler exists only for KV-cache memory profiling, where realistic top_k values give an identical memory footprint. ### One-line proposed fix `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py`, in `_dummy_sampler_run`: ```diff - top_k=dummy_tensors(logits.size(1) - 1), + top_k=dummy_tensors(50), ``` (or any small constant in the typical-production range, e.g. 20–100.) I'd be glad to send a PR. Wanted to surface the diagnosis first in case there's a different preferred remediation (e.g. detect SM120 and short-circuit, or fix the underlying kernel). ### Diagnostic evidence (py-spy, captured 2026-05-17 on a real RTX 5090) ``` Thread MainThread (active): "VLLM::EngineCore" apply_top_k_top_p_triton (vllm/v1/sample/ops/topk_topp_triton.py:1000) apply_top_k_top_p (vllm/v1/sample/ops/topk_topp_sampler.py:252) forward_native (vllm/v1/sample/ops/topk_topp_sampler.py:106) sample (vllm/v1/sample/sampler.py:276) forward (vllm/v1/sample/sampler.py:97) _dummy_sampler_run (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:5663) profile_run (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:5855) determine_available_memory (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py:370) _initialize_kv_caches (vllm/v1/engine/core.py:250) ``` `py-spy dump --native` shows the host thread is stuck inside `cuLaunchKernel → clock_gettime` — a `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` sync poll waiting for a GPU kernel that **never returns**. The process sits at 100% CPU, GPU at 0% util, allocated memory ~7128 MiB, observed for >9 hours before manual `SIGTERM` cleanup. **The same hang reproduces with `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=1`**: ``` top_k_mask_logits (flashinfer/sampling.py:564) top_k_mask_logits (flashinfer/sampling.py:1820) top_k_top_p_sampling_from_logits (flashinfer/sampling.py:1414) flashinfer_sample (vllm/v1/sample/ops/topk_topp_sampler.py:391) forward_cuda (vllm/v1/sample/ops/topk_topp_sampler.py:140) sample (vllm/v1/sample/sampler.py:276) _dummy_sampler_run (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:5663) ... ``` So **both the Triton-based and the FlashInfer-based top-k masking kernels hang for this `top_k` value on SM120.** Switching between the two doesn't help; the bug appears to be specific to the codegen/scheduling these kernels emit when `top_k` approaches `vocab_size`. ### Verified workaround I monkey-patched `_dummy_sampler_run` to substitute `top_k=50` into the dummy `SamplingMetadata` (via a `.pth` injection in the venv's site-packages, gated on an env var so it's opt-in). With the patch active, `vllm serve` reaches `Application startup complete` in ~5 seconds. No regressions observed in subsequent inference behavior (other independent SM120 issues exist; see "Other notes" below). ### Why the dummy-run argument is the worst case for these kernels `_dummy_sampler_run` at `gpu_model_runner.py` line 5648 (vLLM 0.20.1) creates: ```python dummy_metadata = SamplingMetadata( temperature=dummy_tensors(0.5), all_greedy=False, all_random=False, top_p=dummy_tensors(0.9), top_k=dummy_tensors(logits.size(1) - 1), # <-- vocab_size - 1 ... ) ``` `logits.size(1)` is the model's vocab size. For Qwen2.5-3B this is 151,936, so `top_k` becomes 151,935 — essentially "keep top-151,935 of 151,936". This is presumably intended as a worst-case argument for memory profiling, but it exercises a kernel codegen path that doesn't terminate on SM120 in either implementation. Real production requests pass per-call top_k from the SamplingParams (typically ≤ 100). Substituting a realistic value in the dummy run keeps the memory-profiling intent intact while avoiding the buggy code path. ### Hardware and software | Item | Value | |---|---| | GPU | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (SM120 / compute_120f, 32 GB VRAM) | | OS | Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, kernel 6.17.0-22-generic | | NVIDIA driver | 595.58.03 (open kernel modules) | | CUDA toolkit | 13.2 | | torch | 2.11.0+cu130 | | vllm | 0.20.1 (PyPI wheel) | | flashinfer-python | 0.6.11 (PyPI wheel, JIT-only) | | Env | `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1`, `--attention-backend flashinfer` | Not WSL2, not DGX Spark / SM121 — physical bare-metal RTX 5090. ### Other notes (not blocking this fix) After applying the workaround, two additional SM120 hangs become visible later in the lifecycle: 1. With `--enforce-eager`: first inference request hangs in `default_unquantized_gemm` at `vllm/model_executor/layers/utils.py:98` (the lm-head matmul). Same shape: kernel launched, host blocks on CLB=1 sync, GPU never returns. 2. With `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`: weight loading stalls and the GPU enters `[requires reset]` at 6752 MiB allocated. These appear to be independent kernel-scheduling issues on SM120 affecting different kernel families. The dummy_sampler fix is independent and worth landing on its own; the others I plan to file separately (or comment on existing trackers) once I have similar diagnostic evidence. ### Reproduction Any vLLM 0.20.1 (likely 0.21.x too — not retested with the fix) startup on an RTX 5090 with default sampling settings: ``` CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 \ vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct \ --enforce-eager \ --attention-backend flashinfer \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \ --max-model-len 2048 \ --port 8000 ``` Hangs indefinitely at `profile_run` step. With `top_k=50` substituted in `_dummy_sampler_run`, reaches `Application startup complete` in ~5 seconds. ### Offer Reliable RTX 5090 reproducer available. Happy to test the official patch (or any alternative) on this hardware with overnight turnaround.

signals.title: [Feature]: Fuse QK Norm + mRoPE + KV cache write + FP8 quant
signals.text: #### Purpose For the QK-RMSNorm + mRoPE models (such as Qwen3-VL), the operations for Q/K RMSNorm, mRoPE, and the KV cache write with FP8 quantization currently run as separate kernels. This results in intermediate global memory round-trips and multiple kernel launches. This PR introduces a kernel fusion that combines these operations into a single fused CUDA kernel. This new kernel will handle Q/K RMSNorm, mRoPE, KV cache writing, and per-tensor FP8 quantization, all in a single op. As part of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/36066 #### Additional context _No response_ #### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug]: thinking_token_budget forces reasoning_end tokens into the middle of tool-call arguments — ThinkingBudgetStateHolder doesn't treat <tool_call> as implicit reasoning end (Qwen3.5+)
signals.text:
### Your current environment - vLLM **0.22.0** (OpenAI-compatible server), `/v1/responses` with `stream: true` - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8`, `max_model_len` 262144 - `--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder`, `--reasoning-parser qwen3` - `--reasoning-config '{"reasoning_start_str": "<think>", "reasoning_end_str": "I have to give the solution based on the reasoning directly now.</think>"}'` - Requests carry a small `thinking_token_budget` (~256 tokens; in our deployment mapped from `reasoning: {"effort": "minimal"}` by a local patch — see "Reproducing on stock vLLM" below) - Plain httpx client, raw SSE captured (no SDK/proxy in between) ### 🐛 Describe the bug > **Note (edited):** this issue originally blamed the Responses API streaming layer. Further differential experiments isolated the real root cause: **thinking-token-budget forcing corrupts the generated token stream itself**. The original observations below are unchanged and remain valid — they are downstream symptoms. Title and analysis updated accordingly. **Root cause: `ThinkingBudgetStateHolder` and `Qwen3ReasoningParser` disagree on what ends reasoning.** - `Qwen3ReasoningParser` treats `<tool_call>` as an **implicit end of reasoning** — Qwen3.5+ models start tool calls inside the `<think>` block without closing `</think>` first (documented in the parser's docstring, handled in `is_reasoning_end` / `is_reasoning_end_streaming`). - `ThinkingBudgetStateHolder` (`vllm/v1/sample/thinking_budget_state.py`) only tracks the **literal** `reasoning_start/end_token_ids` sequences. It does not know about the implicit end. So when the model starts a tool call inside `<think>`: 1. The tool parser correctly begins streaming `function_call_arguments.delta` (implicit reasoning end). 2. The budget tracker still believes it is in think mode — the tool-call argument tokens keep counting against the thinking budget. 3. The budget runs out **mid-JSON**, and the holder force-injects `reasoning_end_token_ids` via logit masking — right into the middle of the arguments. 4. The model "recovers" after the forced `</think>` and re-emits a fresh `<tool_call>`, which lands inside the previous call's argument string. The injected sentence visible in all corrupted arguments below ("I have to give the solution based on the reasoning directly now.") is **not model-emitted text — it is our configured `reasoning_end_str`, force-sampled by the budget holder**. With the default single-token `</think>` end string the corruption would still occur, just less visually obvious. All corruption modes we observed are slices of this one corrupted token stream, cut differently by the streaming and the final parser: **1. Forced end-string + chat-template tokens injected into `arguments`** (stream and final garbled differently): ``` streamed: {"file_id": 1014, "number_of_pagesI have to give the solution based on the reasoning directly now.</think": "
<tool_call>
<function=read_document>", "file_id" final: {"file_id": 1471, "number_of_pagesI have to give the solution based on the reasoning directly now.</think": "
<tool_cal ``` **2. Streamed deltas truncated mid-JSON** (stream stops right after a number/bracket — incremental-parser flush boundary), final object corrupted differently: ``` streamed: {"file_id": 51, "start_index": 3 final: {"file_id": 51, "start_index": 3, "number_of_pages": "I have to give the solution based on the reasoning directly now.</ ``` ``` streamed: {"folder_ids": [] final: {"folder_ids": [], "keywords": "["COODE", "Projekt", "ZeI have to give the solution based on the reasoning directly ``` **3. Argument deltas routed to the wrong call (off-by-one):** after such a desync, the deltas attributed to call N+1 contained the arguments of call N; call N+1's real arguments only appeared in the final response object. The affected `function_call` items report `status: "completed"` — there is no error signal at all. ### Differential evidence Same server, same model, same prompts/tools, raw httpx SSE against `/v1/responses`: | Configuration | Thinking | Budget forcing | Corrupted runs | |---|---|---|---| | `effort: "minimal"` (→ budget ~256) | on | **fires mid-args** | **3 / 4** | | `effort: "high"` (→ large budget) | on | never reached | 0 / 8 | | no `reasoning` field | off | n/a | 0 / 12 | | Chat Completions, same workload (no budget set on that path) | on | n/a | 0 / 48 | Thinking itself is harmless (`high` is clean). Only the combination *small thinking budget + tool call started inside `<think>`* corrupts. This also explains the earlier "Responses API only" observation: in our deployment only the Responses path sets a budget — the API itself was never the culprit. We additionally confirmed the budget arithmetic in the forensics: tool-call argument tokens count toward the remaining thinking budget (injection point ≈ configured budget measured from `<think>`, including the partial JSON). ### Impact Agent loops that accumulate argument deltas (the documented streaming pattern) persist truncated/garbage arguments into the conversation history. The next request containing that `function_call` item is then rejected by vLLM itself with `400 {"error":{"message":"Expecting ',' delimiter: ..."}}` — the conversation is permanently poisoned. The off-by-one variant silently executes tools with the *previous call's* arguments. In production (HR document assistant, ~5400 tool calls) we measured **~0.5 % of all tool calls** corrupted this way. ### Suggested fix Make the budget holder consistent with the reasoning parser: in `ThinkingBudgetStateHolder._update_think_state`, treat the `<tool_call>` token id as an implicit reasoning end (set `in_think = False`, stop forcing), mirroring `Qwen3ReasoningParser.is_reasoning_end`. Forcing an end-of-thinking sequence into the middle of a tool call can never produce valid output. ### Reproducing on stock vLLM Stock vLLM does not map `reasoning.effort` to a thinking budget (that mapping is a local patch on our Responses path). Upstream, the same forcing path is reachable directly: Chat Completions / sampling params with `thinking_token_budget` set low (e.g. 200–300), `--reasoning-parser qwen3`, `--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder`, a Qwen3.5+/3.6 model and a tool-use prompt that makes the model start a tool call inside `<think>`. Our repro loop (agent-style document-search conversations, German HR questions) triggers it in ~75 % of runs at budget ~256. <details> <summary>repro.py (our /v1/responses harness — adapt the budget mechanism as described above)</summary> ```python import asyncio, json, os, sys import httpx BASE = os.environ["VLLM_BASE_URL"] # e.g. https://host/v1 KEY = os.environ["VLLM_API_KEY"] MODEL = os.environ["VLLM_MODEL"] # e.g. Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 QUESTIONS = [ "Wo finde ich die RHOME-Plattform für Workation-Anträge?", "Wie hoch ist das Weiterbildungsbudget pro Jahr?", "Welche Feiertage gelten dieses Jahr und wie beantrage ich Urlaub?", "Wie erfasse ich meine Tätigkeiten im COODE-Projekt?", ] INSTRUCTIONS = ("You are an HR assistant for employees. Always ground your answers in " "the shared documents: search first, then read the relevant documents. " "Answer in German.") TOOLS = [ {"type": "function", "name": "search", "description": "Search shared documents by keywords. Returns matching files with ids.", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": { "folder_ids": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "integer"}}, "keywords": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}, "top_k": {"type": "integer"}}, "required": ["folder_ids", "keywords", "top_k"]}}, {"type": "function", "name": "read_document", "description": "Read a page range of a document by file id.", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": { "file_id": {"type": "integer"}, "start_index": {"type": "integer"}, "number_of_pages": {"type": "integer"}}, "required": ["file_id", "start_index", "number_of_pages"]}}, ] def tool_result(name): if name == "search": return ("Treffer:
- file_id 51: Company FAQ.pdf
- file_id 1012: Weiterbildungsrichtlinie.pdf
" "- file_id 1014: Urlaubsrichtlinien.pdf
- file_id 1471: Feiertagskalender.pdf
" "Für Details bitte die relevanten Dokumente lesen.") return ("Seiten gelesen: Die Beantragung erfolgt über das HR-Portal. Details stehen in den " "weiteren Abschnitten; siehe auch die anderen Dokumente für verwandte Richtlinien.") async def turn(client, input_items): body = {"model": MODEL, "input": input_items, "instructions": INSTRUCTIONS, "reasoning": {"effort": "minimal", "summary": "auto"}, "tools": TOOLS, "stream": True, "max_output_tokens": 8192} order, streamed, final = [], {}, None async with client.stream("POST", "/responses", json=body) as resp: resp.raise_for_status() et = None async for line in resp.aiter_lines(): if line.startswith("event: "): et = line[7:] elif line.startswith("data: ") and et: d = json.loads(line[6:]) if et == "response.output_item.added" and d["item"].get("type") == "function_call": order.append(d["item"]["id"]); streamed[d["item"]["id"]] = d["item"].get("arguments") or "" elif et == "response.function_call_arguments.delta" and d.get("item_id") in streamed: streamed[d["item_id"]] += d.get("delta") or "" elif et == "response.completed": final = d["response"] calls = [i for i in (final.get("output") or []) if i.get("type") == "function_call"] bad = False for pos, item in enumerate(calls): s = streamed.get(order[pos], "") if pos < len(order) else "" f = item.get("arguments") or "" if s != f and (final.get("incomplete_details") or {}).get("reason") != "max_output_tokens": print(f"MISMATCH {item.get('name')}
 streamed: {s[:120]!r}
 final: {f[:120]!r}") bad = True return final, calls, bad async def run(client, q): items = [{"type": "message", "role": "user", "content": [{"type": "input_text", "text": q}]}] for _ in range(6): final, calls, bad = await turn(client, items) if bad: return True if not calls: return False items.extend(final.get("output") or []) for c in calls: items.append({"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": c["call_id"], "output": tool_result(c["name"])}) return False async def main(): async with httpx.AsyncClient(base_url=BASE, timeout=180, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {KEY}"}) as client: for i in range(int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 8): hit = await run(client, QUESTIONS[i % len(QUESTIONS)]) print(f"run {i}: {'HIT' if hit else 'clean'}") if hit: sys.exit(1) asyncio.run(main()) ``` </details> ### Secondary findings (Responses API streaming, observed along the way) - On a `max_output_tokens` cutoff mid-arguments, `function_call_arguments.done` / `output_item.done` carry only the flushed prefix (e.g. `"{"`) with `status: "completed"`, while the final `response.completed` object contains longer (auto-closed) arguments — stream consumers and final-object consumers see different data, with no error signal. - `item.id` and `call_id` differ between streamed events (`call_xxx`) and the final response object (`chatcmpl-tool-xxx`), so the two can only be correlated positionally. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug]: Hybrid-model prefix caching silently drops to 0% when the align-mode Mamba checkpoint lands in request-unique tokens
signals.text: ### Summary For hybrid Mamba/attention models (e.g. the Qwen3.5 GDN family), `mamba_cache_mode="align"` — the only prefix-caching mode these models support ("all" falls back to it) — retains, per request, only the Mamba state checkpoint at the **last block boundary before the prompt ends**. Whether *any* cross-request prefix-cache reuse happens therefore depends on whether that single position lands inside the workload's shared prefix or in the request-unique part of the prompt. When it lands in unique tokens, the Mamba group never matches, `HybridKVCacheCoordinator` intersects per-group hits, and **all** reuse — including attention blocks that matched perfectly — drops to exactly 0%, with no warning and nothing in metrics to distinguish this from "requests simply don't share prefixes". A 100-token shift in prompt composition flips this on stock main: | workload (shared prefix / unique suffix, ~2200-token prompts) | checkpoint position (block_size 528) | prefix-cache hits | mean TTFT | |---|---|---|---| | 1600 / 600 | 1584 — inside shared prefix | 52/64 requests | 433 ms | | 1500 / 700 | 1584, 2112 — both in unique region | **0/64** | **905 ms** | (Qwen3.5-4B, main @ 16282a9c4, single GPU, `--enforce-eager`, concurrency 1. Hit positions verified with instrumentation in `MambaManager.find_longest_cache_hit` — the healthy case hits exactly at block index 2 = boundary 1584, as the arithmetic predicts.) ### Reproduction ```bash vllm serve <Qwen3.5-4B-class hybrid> --max-model-len 8192 --enable-prefix-caching --enforce-eager # Case A (healthy): shared prefix 1600, unique suffix 600 vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model <model> --dataset-name prefix_repetition \ --prefix-repetition-prefix-len 1600 --prefix-repetition-suffix-len 600 \ --prefix-repetition-num-prefixes 8 --prefix-repetition-output-len 64 \ --num-prompts 64 --max-concurrency 1 # Case B (0% hits): identical except --prefix-repetition-prefix-len 1500 --prefix-repetition-suffix-len 700 ``` Compare `vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total / vllm:prefix_cache_queries_total` and TTFT. The trigger condition is `floor((prompt_len-1)/block_size)*block_size > shared_prefix_len`, with the platform-aligned block size (528 for Qwen3.5-4B at bf16/TP1, up to 2096 for 122B/397B). Full methodology, instrumentation, and traces: https://gist.github.com/Sahil170595/8ed465122d42c2d956bba3a83e61c556 ### Root cause 1. In align mode, `MambaManager.allocate_new_blocks` gives a request real blocks only at/near the last aligned boundary; earlier prompt positions are null blocks (Mamba state is O(1) per request — only the running state exists). 2. `BlockPool.cache_full_blocks` skips null blocks when registering block hashes (the null-skip comment in `block_pool.py` explicitly mentions Mamba align mode). Net effect: per request, only ~1–2 Mamba block hashes ever enter the prefix cache, at geometry-determined positions. 3. `MambaManager.find_longest_cache_hit` already searches right-to-left for *any* single cached boundary block — the lookup handles sparse checkpoints fine. The gap is purely registration/retention coverage. 4. `HybridKVCacheCoordinator` requires every group to hit, so a Mamba miss vetoes the attention groups' matches entirely. ### Who is affected Any hybrid GDN/Mamba deployment with shared-prefix traffic (RAG system prompts, agentic loops, multi-turn chat) — i.e. the workloads prefix caching exists for. The failure is binary per (prompt_len, shared_prefix_len, block_size), so real mixed traffic sees some fraction of requests permanently missing. Larger models are worse off: block_size grows with the Mamba state (528 → 2096 across the Qwen3.5 family), so checkpoint spacing gets coarser exactly where prefill is most expensive. Block-size-changing work like #35703 shifts the checkpoint position and can flip a workload between healthy and zero — that's how this was found: what looked like an `attn_pack_size=4` regression in my benchmarks there (block 144 → checkpoint at 2016, 16 tokens past a 2000-token shared prefix → 0% at concurrency 1) was this main-branch behavior, not the PR. ### Possible fix directions - **(a) Retain K checkpoints per request**, spread across the prompt (positions rounded to block boundaries), K configurable with a small default (2–4). Memory cost: (K−1) extra Mamba pages per request — ~2–8 MiB/request for Qwen3.5-4B, bounded and predictable. Lookup needs no changes (it already takes the rightmost cached boundary). - **(b) Checkpoint at globally fixed positions** (every M tokens) so requests sharing a prefix share checkpoint positions regardless of total length — better hit alignment, slightly more invasive in the align copy machinery. - **(c) At minimum, observability**: a counter for "attention-side prefix match vetoed by missing Mamba checkpoint", so operators can see the loss. Happy to implement whichever direction maintainers prefer — (a) looks contained (allocation + the existing align boundary-copy machinery; registration follows existing `cache_full_blocks` paths). ### Related - #35703 (attn-pack-size — interacts by moving the checkpoint position; follow-up comment there) - #37121 (hybrid KV cache accounting) ### Disclosure Investigated and written with AI assistance (Anthropic Claude, Fable/Mythos 5) under my direction; all findings reproduced and reviewed by me.

signals.title: [Bug]: Qwen3-VL video prompt expansion drops outer <|vision_start|>/<|vision_end|> wrapper, mismatching HuggingFace processor
signals.text:
### 🐛 Describe the bug For **Qwen3-VL** video inputs, vLLM's multimodal prompt replacement produces a different `prompt_token_ids` sequence than the official HuggingFace `Qwen3VLProcessor`: 1. **2 fewer tokens** (e.g. 2065 vs 2067 in the token-only repro below). 2. **Different token order** at the start of the video block: - **HF (expected):** `...user
<|vision_start|><0.3 seconds>...` - **vLLM (current):** `...user
<0.3 seconds><|vision_start|>...` The mismatch persists all the way into model `forward` — `prompt_token_ids` are not rewritten after the multimodal processor. ### Root cause HuggingFace expands video in **two steps**: 1. The official Qwen3-VL chat template renders video as `<|vision_start|><|video_pad|><|vision_end|>` ([`Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct` `chat_template.json`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct/blob/main/chat_template.json)). 2. `Qwen3VLProcessor` only replaces the **inner** `<|video_pad|>` token via `get_text_with_replacements()`, keeping the outer wrapper intact ([`processing_utils.py` L862–863, transformers `v5.12.0`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v5.12.0/src/transformers/processing_utils.py#L862-L863)). 3. `replace_video_token()` expands each frame as `timestamp + <|vision_start|> + pad*N + <|vision_end|>` ([`modular_qwen3_vl.py` L1137–1140, transformers `v5.12.0`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v5.12.0/src/transformers/models/qwen3_vl/modular_qwen3_vl.py#L1137-L1140)). **Final HF sequence:** ``` <|vision_start|> + [per-frame: <t> + <|vision_start|> + pads + <|vision_end|>] + <|vision_end|> ``` In vLLM, **image** correctly replaces only `hf_processor.image_token` (`<|image_pad|>`), but **video** replaces the **entire** string `<|vision_start|><|video_pad|><|vision_end|>` with the per-frame expansion, which **consumes the outer wrapper**: - Image target (correct): [`qwen3_vl.py` L1423, vLLM `v0.23.0`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.23.0/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_vl.py#L1423) - Video target (bug): [`qwen3_vl.py` L1430, vLLM `v0.23.0`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.23.0/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_vl.py#L1430) - `get_video_repl()` builds per-frame tokens without re-adding an outer wrapper: [`qwen3_vl.py` L1481–1486, vLLM `v0.23.0`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.23.0/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_vl.py#L1481-L1486) This is inconsistent with both HuggingFace and vLLM's own image handling in the same file. ### Expected behavior `prompt_token_ids` from vLLM's multimodal processor should match HuggingFace `processor.apply_chat_template(..., tokenize=True)` for the same prompt and video. ### Actual behavior | | Outer wrapper | First tokens after `user
` | Length (sample) | |---|---|---|---| | HuggingFace | preserved | `<|vision_start|><0.3 seconds>...` | 2066 | | vLLM | dropped | `<0.3 seconds><|vision_start|>...` | 2064 | ### Environment - vLLM: `0.23.0` - transformers: `5.12.0` - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct` ### Steps / script to reproduce ```bash pip install "vllm==0.19.1" "transformers==5.12.0" python repro_qwen3vl_video_prompt_mismatch.py ``` <details> <summary>repro_qwen3vl_video_prompt_mismatch.py</summary> ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Reproduce Qwen3-VL video prompt_token_ids mismatch: vLLM vs HuggingFace.""" import argparse VIDEO_PLACEHOLDER = '<|vision_start|><|video_pad|><|vision_end|>' def _replace_first_subseq(ids, target, replacement): for i in range(len(ids) - len(target) + 1): if ids[i:i + len(target)] == target: return ids[:i] + replacement + ids[i + len(target):] raise ValueError(f'target subsequence not found: {target}') def main(): parser = argparse.ArgumentParser() parser.add_argument('--model', default='Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct') parser.add_argument('--timestamp', type=float, default=0.3) parser.add_argument('--tokens-per-frame', type=int, default=2048) args = parser.parse_args() from transformers import AutoProcessor from vllm.model_executor.models.qwen3_vl import Qwen3VLMultiModalProcessor messages = [{ 'role': 'user', 'content': [ {'type': 'video', 'video': 'dummy.mp4'}, {'type': 'text', 'text': 'describe the video.'}, ], }] processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(args.model, trust_remote_code=True) tokenizer = processor.tokenizer prompt_text = processor.apply_chat_template( messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=False, ) prompt_token_ids = tokenizer.encode(prompt_text, add_special_tokens=False) hf_frame_text = ( f'<{args.timestamp:.1f} seconds>' + '<|vision_start|>' + '<|video_pad|>' * args.tokens_per_frame + '<|vision_end|>' ) hf_ids = tokenizer.encode( prompt_text.replace('<|video_pad|>', hf_frame_text, 1), add_special_tokens=False, ) vision_start_id = tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids('<|vision_start|>') vision_end_id = tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids('<|vision_end|>') video_id = tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids('<|video_pad|>') vllm_repl = Qwen3VLMultiModalProcessor.get_video_repl( tokens_per_frame=[args.tokens_per_frame], timestamps=[args.timestamp], tokenizer=tokenizer, vision_start_token_id=vision_start_id, vision_end_token_id=vision_end_id, video_token_id=video_id, select_token_id=True, ).full target_ids = tokenizer.encode(VIDEO_PLACEHOLDER, add_special_tokens=False) vllm_ids = _replace_first_subseq(prompt_token_ids, target_ids, vllm_repl) print(f'HF len={len(hf_ids)}, vLLM len={len(vllm_ids)}, diff={len(hf_ids)-len(vllm_ids)}') print('HF :', tokenizer.decode(hf_ids[:10])) print('vLLM:', tokenizer.decode(vllm_ids[:10])) assert hf_ids == vllm_ids if __name__ == '__main__': main() ``` </details> **Expected output (current bug):** ``` HF len=2066, vLLM len=2064, diff=2 HF : <|im_start|>user <|vision_start|><0.3 seconds> vLLM: <|im_start|>user <0.3 seconds><|vision_start|> AssertionError ``` ### Suggested fix Align video handling with image handling and HuggingFace: **Option A (preferred, mirrors HF):** Change video `PromptReplacement.target` from `"<|vision_start|><|video_pad|><|vision_end|>"` to `hf_processor.video_token` (`"<|video_pad|>"`) only, so the outer `<|vision_start|>` / `<|vision_end|>` from the chat template are preserved. **Option B:** Keep the full-string target but wrap `get_video_repl()` output with outer `vision_start_token_id` and `vision_end_token_id`. ### Impact Training frameworks (GRPO/RLHF) that align rollout `prompt_token_ids` with HuggingFace training inputs will see a systematic 2-token offset and reordered timestamp/vision markers for every Qwen3-VL video request. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug]: Partial LoRA on Qwen3.5/Qwen3.6 GatedDeltaNet (in_proj_qkv without in_proj_z) crashes in expand_packed_lora — regression from #37912
signals.text: ### Your current environment <details> <summary>Environment</summary> ``` vLLM version: 0.24.0 (latest; also reproduced on current main) Model: Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B (runs through the shared Qwen3.5 code path -> Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration; multimodal GDN hybrid) OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64) Python: 3.12.3 torch: 2.11.0+cu130 CUDA: 13.0 (runtime 13.0.88), driver 570.124.06 GPU: 1x NVIDIA H200 (Hopper, SM 9.0) FlashInfer: 0.6.12 transformers: 5.13.0 ``` Serve command that triggers it: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B --reasoning-parser qwen3 --enable-lora \ --lora-modules my_lora=<adapter targeting q_proj,k_proj,v_proj,in_proj_qkv> \ --mm-processor-kwargs '{"max_pixels": 262144}' --enforce-eager ``` Known-good: v0.20.0 loads this adapter (verified on the same H200 box, torch 2.11.0+cu130, FlashInfer 0.6.8.post1). Crash starts at v0.21.0 — the release that first contains #37912 (commit `48698b1b9`) — and persists through v0.24.0 and current `main`. </details> ### 🐛 Describe the bug Loading a LoRA adapter that targets **only a subset** of a GatedDeltaNet packed projection group on Qwen3.5/Qwen3.6 crashes at adapter-activation time. Concretely: an adapter that adapts `in_proj_qkv` but **not** `in_proj_z`. **Traceback (vLLM 0.24.0, trimmed to the relevant frames):** ``` (EngineCore) ERROR [core.py:1449] Invocation of add_lora method failed (EngineCore) ERROR [core.py:1449] Traceback (most recent call last): (EngineCore) ERROR [core.py:1449] File ".../vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 825, in add_lora (EngineCore) ERROR [core.py:1449] return self.model_executor.add_lora(lora_request) (EngineCore) ERROR [core.py:1449] File ".../vllm/v1/worker/lora_model_runner_mixin.py", line 276, in add_lora (EngineCore) ERROR [core.py:1449] return self.lora_manager.add_adapter(lora_request) (EngineCore) ERROR [core.py:1449] File ".../vllm/lora/worker_manager.py", line 314, in add_adapter (EngineCore) ERROR [core.py:1449] self._adapter_manager.activate_adapter(lora_request.lora_int_id) (EngineCore) ERROR [core.py:1449] File ".../vllm/lora/model_manager.py", line 325, in activate_adapter (EngineCore) ERROR [core.py:1449] module.set_lora( (EngineCore) ERROR [core.py:1449] File ".../vllm/lora/layers/column_parallel_linear.py", line 314, in set_lora (EngineCore) ERROR [core.py:1449] lora_a, lora_b = self.expand_packed_lora(lora_a, lora_b) (EngineCore) ERROR [core.py:1449] File ".../vllm/lora/layers/column_parallel_linear.py", line 280, in expand_packed_lora (EngineCore) ERROR [core.py:1449] b_rows, cu_rows, covered = b_i.shape[0], 0, 0 (EngineCore) ERROR [core.py:1449] AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'shape' ``` Surfaces to the API server as: ``` ValueError: Call to add_lora method failed: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'shape' ``` ### Root cause `packed_modules_mapping` for Qwen3.5 declares the GDN input projection as a 2-member group mapped onto a 4-slice fused `MergedColumnParallelLinear`: ```python # vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_5.py "in_proj_qkvz": ["in_proj_qkv", "in_proj_z"], # in_proj_qkv -> slices (0,1,2), in_proj_z -> slice 3 "in_proj_ba": ["in_proj_b", "in_proj_a"], ``` When an adapter provides fewer group members than there are slices, `set_lora` routes through `expand_packed_lora`, which dereferences each entry unconditionally: ```python for a_i, b_i in zip(lora_a, lora_b): b_rows, cu_rows, covered = b_i.shape[0], 0, 0 # crashes when b_i is None ``` If a group member is absent from the adapter (here `in_proj_z`), its entry is `None`, and `b_i.shape[0]` raises. The rest of the packed-LoRA pipeline already tolerates unadapted slices: the sibling method `slice_lora_b` and the downstream stacking loop in `set_lora` both guard `None`. `expand_packed_lora` is the only step missing the guard. A `None` entry should mean "this group member is not adapted; leave its slice(s) at base weights." ### Regression: introduced by #37912 This worked on v0.20.0, which built `in_proj_qkv` and `in_proj_z` as **separate modules** under LoRA (`create_in_proj_qkvz`) so they could be adapted independently. PR #37912 ("[Bugfix] Fuse Qwen3.5 in_qkvz_proj forwarding with LoRA enabled") unified them back into the fused `in_proj_qkvz` layer and added the `expand_packed_lora` helper — a reasonable simplification — but the new helper didn't carry over the `None`-tolerance, so partial groups now crash instead of being supported. ### Minimal repro PEFT adapter targeting GDN qkv (and full-attention q/k/v) but **not** z: ```json { "target_modules": "model\\.language_model\\..*\\.(q_proj|k_proj|v_proj|in_proj_qkv)" } ``` Per-layer keys present: `linear_attn.in_proj_qkv.lora_A/lora_B` Per-layer keys **absent**: `linear_attn.in_proj_z.lora_A/lora_B` ```bash vllm serve <Qwen3.5-or-3.6-model> --enable-lora --lora-modules my=/path/to/adapter # -> crashes in expand_packed_lora on first adapter activation ``` ### Proposed fix Make `expand_packed_lora` skip `None` group members, emitting `None` placeholders for the slice(s) they cover so subsequent groups stay aligned and those slices are left at base weights — matching the `None`-tolerance already in `slice_lora_b` and the `set_lora` stacking loop. This restores partial-group support inside the current fused architecture without reverting the #37912 split. `expand_packed_lora` is only reached for the `in_proj_qkvz` group (2 members → 4 slices); every other packed group (`qkv_proj`, `gate_up_proj`, `in_proj_ba`) has `len(lora_b) == n_slices` and takes the normal, already-`None`-tolerant path. In `in_proj_qkvz` the only multi-slice member (`in_proj_qkv`, Q+K+V) leads and the only optional member (`in_proj_z`) trails, so a `None` member covers exactly the remaining slices. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
