signals.title: [Bug]: Token truncation leaves stale Request.block_hashes and can cause incorrect KV cache hits
signals.text: ### Your current environment <details> <summary>Environment</summary> Not environment-dependent: this is a code-level invariant break in the scheduler / prefix-hashing path, reproduced against `main` @ `f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1` with the pure-Python script below (no GPU required). </details> ### 🐛 Describe the bug **Summary.** When a request's tokens are truncated in place while `Request.block_hashes` is not, the retained hashes keep fingerprinting the replaced tokens. Prefix-cache, event, and offload consumers treat these hashes as authoritative identities, so the prefix cache can serve KV under a wrong identity: a later request whose prefix matches the OLD tokens gets a cache hit on KV computed from the NEW tokens — silently incorrect output — while the NEW token sequence misses blocks that are actually resident. The trigger reproduced deterministically below is the resumable streaming session path; the Mooncake/NIXL token-pop paths can violate the same invariant when the popped token is already hash-covered (see Related work). **Root cause** (permalinks pinned to `main` @ `f25953cc5`): 1. `Scheduler._update_request_as_session` discards the last sampled token(s) by truncating `_all_token_ids` past `num_computed_tokens` on the live `Request`, then extends it with the next input chunk and calls `update_block_hashes()` ([`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:1282-1314`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L1282-L1314)). 2. `Request.update_block_hashes` only appends ([`vllm/v1/request.py:244-260`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/request.py#L244-L260)); nothing in the tree ever truncates `request.block_hashes`. 3. The block hasher resumes from `start_token_idx = len(request.block_hashes) * hash_block_size` ([`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:691-748`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py#L691-L748)), so a block whose hash already exists is never recomputed. If a discarded sampled token had completed a hash block (for a single discarded token: `num_computed_tokens % hash_block_size == hash_block_size - 1`), the hash chained over the now-replaced token persists, and all later hashes chain from it. **Deterministic reproduction** (mirrors the statements `_update_request_as_session` executes at `scheduler.py:1293-1314`): ```python from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams from vllm.utils.hashing import sha256 from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils import get_request_block_hasher, init_none_hash from vllm.v1.request import Request init_none_hash(sha256) hash_block_size = 4 req = Request( request_id="session", prompt_token_ids=[1, 2, 3], sampling_params=SamplingParams(), pooling_params=None, block_hasher=get_request_block_hasher(hash_block_size, sha256), resumable=True, ) req.append_output_token_ids(99) # completes hash block [1, 2, 3, 99] assert len(req.block_hashes) == 1 stale_hash = req.block_hashes[0] req.num_computed_tokens = 3 # sampled token 99 was never computed # --- what _update_request_as_session runs for the next streaming chunk [4] --- del req._all_token_ids[req.num_computed_tokens :] # scheduler.py:1297 req._output_token_ids.clear() # scheduler.py:1298 req._all_token_ids.append(4) # next input chunk req.update_block_hashes() # scheduler.py:1314 assert list(req.all_token_ids) == [1, 2, 3, 4] # block_hashes[0] still fingerprints [1, 2, 3, 99]: the hasher resumes at # len(request.block_hashes) * hash_block_size == 4 and never revisits block 0. assert req.block_hashes[0] == stale_hash # Explicit identity check: the retained hash is the OLD sequence's, not the new one's. import vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils as kcu assert req.block_hashes[0] == kcu.hash_block_tokens(sha256, kcu.NONE_HASH, [1, 2, 3, 99]) assert req.block_hashes[0] != kcu.hash_block_tokens(sha256, kcu.NONE_HASH, [1, 2, 3, 4]) ``` **Consequence (source derivation; the wrong cross-request hit requires prefix caching to be enabled).** At session-update time the boundary block has not yet been cached as a full block (its last token was never computed). The corruption lands when the resumed session is next scheduled: `allocate_slots()` commits the block under `request.block_hashes[0]` — the identity of `[1, 2, 3, 99]` — **before** the forward pass runs; the insertion chain is [`kv_cache_manager.py:493-503`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py#L493-L503) -> [`kv_cache_coordinator.py:283-287`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py#L283-L287) -> [`single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:443-450`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py#L443-L450) -> the insertion at [`block_pool.py:280-297`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py#L280-L297) (fine-grained hash-block configurations go through the partial-block callers at [`single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:787`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py#L787) / [`:1674`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py#L1674) into [`block_pool.py:490-512`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py#L490-L512)); the subsequent forward then writes the KV computed from `[1, 2, 3, 4]` into that block. On lookup, `get_computed_blocks` matches `request.block_hashes` under the `num_tokens - 1` cap ([`kv_cache_manager.py:237-241`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py#L237-L241)) and resolves cached blocks via [`block_pool.py:198-223`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py#L198-L223): a later request continuing past that block with actual prefix `[1, 2, 3, 99, …]` (it must extend beyond the block because of the `num_tokens - 1` cap, so an exactly-four-token request does not hit) computes that same hash and gets the block — a prefix-cache hit on KV computed from different tokens, i.e. silently wrong output — while a later `[1, 2, 3, 4, …]` request computes a hash absent from the map and misses a resident block. The stale identities also flow into KV cache events (`BlockStored` payloads are emitted from the same pool paths, e.g. [`block_pool.py:331`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py#L331) and [`:527-528`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py#L527-L528)) and into offload keys (the offloading connector derives `OffloadKey`s from `request.block_hashes` in `update_offload_keys`, [`offloading/scheduler.py:306-316`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py#L306-L316)), so external indexers and offloaded copies inherit the wrong fingerprints. (The script pins the request-side invariant break; the pool-side consequence is derived from the cited paths — no end-to-end wrong-output run is included here.) **Candidate fix direction (text-only; see limitations).** In `_update_request_as_session`, invalidate hashes past the kept prefix before extending — `del session.block_hashes[num_computed_tokens // self.hash_block_size :]` (the scheduler holds `hash_block_size`): hashes of blocks fully inside `[0, num_computed_tokens)` remain valid, and the resumed hasher recomputes the boundary block. On this path that is also sufficient for the pool side, because the boundary block was never cached as a full block. Two limitations to be explicit about: (i) this is correct for **text-only** requests — with multimodal inputs the incremental hasher restarts its feature scan from the last MM feature in the request's current list — including newly appended ones (`curr_mm_idx = -1`) — not from the first feature overlapping the recomputed range ([`kv_cache_utils.py:713-748`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py#L713-L748)), so deleting the hash suffix alone can still yield wrong hashes — when the suffix recomputation starts from a non-zero boundary and the recomputed range overlaps earlier MM features while a later feature exists in the current list (confirmed by fresh-vs-incremental hash comparison for such cases; deleting all hashes and recomputing from token 0 does not hit this); covering multimodal requires also rewinding the MM scan start plus regression tests, or scoping the streaming fix to text-only sessions; (ii) a general fix for truncating already-computed tokens would additionally have to keep the `BlockPool` side consistent (`KVCacheBlock` block-hash state and the `cached_block_hash_to_block` mapping). Both are out of scope for the minimal fix here. I'm happy to send a fix PR for the text-only path unless the streaming-sessions folks would rather take it. **Related work (checked, not duplicates).** - #43372 (open) adds an explicit per-session KV-cache truncation API and clears `Request.block_hashes` on that new path; it does not touch `_update_request_as_session`, and clearing the request-side list alone does not cover the pool side for already-computed truncated tokens. Related — neither a duplicate nor a complete fix precedent. - Adjacent paths that can violate the same invariant (not reproduced end-to-end; should not block this fix): the Mooncake and NIXL connector token-pop paths for hybrid/Mamba models — NIXL's `_truncate_mamba_request_for_prefill` ([`nixl/base_scheduler.py:341-365`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_scheduler.py#L341-L365)) and the Mooncake connector's last-token pop ([`mooncake/mooncake_connector.py:701-707`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py#L701-L707)) — can leave stale `block_hashes` when the removed token is already covered by a computed hash (e.g. the pre-pop length lands exactly on a hash boundary). They warrant separate fixes/audits. cc @joshuadeng (streaming sessions, #28973) @Alex-ai-future (#48596) AI assistance was used in preparing this report; the reproduction script was verified against `main` @ `f25953cc5`. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug]: fuse_norm_quant/fuse_act_quant custom fusions produce garbled token output on SM120 (GB10) for DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731
signals.text: ### Your current environment - **Hardware**: 2× NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark), one GPU per node, 2-node cluster joined via Ray (TCP/RoCE interconnect) - **Compute Capability**: SM121 (12.1), `aarch64` - **vLLM**: 0.26.0 (PyPI release) - **torch**: 2.11.0+cu130 - **CUDA**: 13.0 - **Distributed executor**: `ray`, `--tensor-parallel-size 2` (one GPU per node), `--enable-expert-parallel` ### Model ``` deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 ``` ### 🐛 Describe the bug The default-enabled custom fusion passes `fuse_norm_quant` / `fuse_act_quant` (see `vllm/config/compilation.py`, logged at startup as `Enabled custom fusions: norm_quant, act_quant`) produce corrupted/garbled token output on SM120 (GB10) for this model, **even under greedy decoding**. Disabling both via `--compilation-config` restores fluent, grammatically well-formed output for the identical prompt and sampling parameters. We independently ruled out chat-template/prompt-encoding as the cause (verified via `/tokenize` that the prompt's special tokens resolve to the exact expected IDs) and ruled out sampling randomness (reproduced identically at `temperature=0`). This was tested after already working around the `--load_format fastsafetensors` weight-loading bug reported separately (#50772) — i.e. weight loading itself was confirmed correct going into this test. ### Launch command (bugged — default fusion behavior) ```bash vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --trust-remote-code \ --max-model-len 262144 \ --distributed-executor-backend ray \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --block-size 256 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 ``` ### Repro Prompt (raw `/v1/completions`, DeepSeek-V4's own chat-mode encoding, `add_special_tokens=false`, `temperature=0`): ``` <｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜User｜>Repeat this exact word back to me: BANANA<｜Assistant｜></think> ``` **With default fusions enabled** (greedy, `temperature=0`): ``` * 501 ...eti~and.## 202 ``` **With `--compilation-config '{"pass_config": {"fuse_norm_quant": false, "fuse_act_quant": false}}'`** (identical prompt/params): ``` *#ifndef BOOST_MP11_DETAIL_MP_COUNT_HPP_INCLUDED ``` (Still doesn't answer the actual instruction — that appears to be a separate, not-yet-isolated issue, possibly related to the SM120 sparse-MLA decode kernel gaps discussed in #50720 — but the output is now well-formed rather than token salad, confirming the fusion kernels were introducing the garbling.) ### Expected behavior The `norm_quant`/`act_quant` fused kernels should be numerically equivalent to the unfused path on SM120, or should be disabled by default on architectures where they haven't been validated. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the documentation page, which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug `MooncakeStoreConnector` tracks asynchronous store jobs only by `req_id`. When a request is preempted, its tracking state can be deleted while old queued or active store jobs still exist. If the same `req_id` is subsequently tracked again, completions from the old lifecycle decrement the counter of the new lifecycle. This is a request-ID ABA problem across request tracking generations. Observed lifecycle: 1. A store job for `req_id=X` in generation N is queued or becomes active. 2. The request is preempted and the worker-side tracking entry for `X` is deleted. 3. The same `req_id=X` is subsequently tracked again for a newer generation, creating a fresh counter. 4. A stale job from an older generation completes and decrements the counter belonging to the newer generation. 5. With multiple stale completions, the new counter can reach zero prematurely and then become negative. 6. In the observed failure, the counter became negative before the completion scan, so the real jobs of the current generation could no longer restore the expected zero state. 7. `finished_sending` was therefore never emitted for the affected request. 8. Finished requests retained KV blocks, eventually causing persistent KV starvation and a `running=0, waiting>0` livelock. ### Root cause The following worker state is keyed only by reusable `req_id`: - `stored_requests` - `_saved_offset` - `_skip_store_requests` - `finished_store_req` `dec_stored_request(req_id)` does not verify that the completing job belongs to the currently tracked request generation. Preemption removes the bare-`req_id` tracking state, but does not associate already queued or active jobs with the lifecycle that created them. An active old job can therefore complete after deletion, and a queued old job can also become indistinguishable from a new job if the same `req_id` is tracked again before it executes. The current `main` branch still appears to have the same lifecycle pattern in: [`worker.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/worker.py) Relevant methods and fields include: - `KVCacheStoreSendingThread.stored_requests` - `add_stored_request` - `dec_stored_request` - `delete_finished_stored_request` - `MooncakeStoreWorker.finished_store_req` - `_get_and_clear_finished_sending` I reproduced the bug on v0.25.0 and v0.26.0. I have not yet rerun the full GPU reproduction against the latest `main`, but the same bare-request-ID bookkeeping pattern is still present. ### Related work I searched existing vLLM issues and PRs and did not find an issue or PR covering the same cross-generation aliasing. The closest related work is: - [PR #43281](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43281) preserves and resets the scheduler-side `RequestTracker` after preemption. This issue is in worker-side asynchronous store-job accounting below that tracker. - [PR #43742](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43742) ensures the `stored_requests[req_id]` counter is decremented after a failed store. It addresses a missing decrement; this issue is a decrement applied to the wrong request generation. - [PR #43371](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43371) prevents conflicting save/load work from being co-queued for one request, but does not distinguish an old store job from a newer lifecycle with the same ID. - [Issue #43226](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43226) and [Issue #46240](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/46240) / [PR #46304](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46304) concern stale completions for an absent or aborted request. Here the bare `req_id` exists again and represents a newer lifecycle, so an existence check cannot reject the stale completion. - [PR #51595](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51595) aggregates asynchronous completions with a per-request counter, but does not add a request-generation identity. - [PR #49796](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49796) rejects a duplicate client-controlled Mooncake `transfer_id` and cleans up transfer resources. That transfer-layer ID collision is distinct from reuse of a vLLM `req_id` after preemption and a stale store job decrementing the current generation of `stored_requests`. The distinguishing condition is therefore not merely a late completion after preemption. It is an old worker job mutating a newly tracked lifecycle that reuses the same request ID. ### Evidence With a 1-replica x TP2, 96-trajectory workload, lifecycle diagnostics recorded: - 1,128 deletes while store jobs were pending - 336 stale-job generation mismatches - 221 counter-underflow events - negative counters on both TP ranks - no outstanding synchronous store I/O - no missing receive completions - all retained KV blocks accounted for by finished requests A captured transition was: ```text req_id=X job_epoch=3 current_epoch=4 counter_before=0 counter_after=-1 stale_epoch=True ``` The run subsequently stabilized at: ```text running=0 waiting=42 scheduled_tokens=0 free_blocks=883 ``` Both store workers had empty queues and no active I/O at that point, while finished requests still owned all 11,267 referenced KV blocks. Here, "generation" / "epoch" refers to the request-lifecycle identity used in my diagnostics and proposed fix. ### Expected behavior A queued or active store job must only modify the tracking generation to which it belonged when it was enqueued. A stale completion must not decrement the counter, update saved offsets, publish KV events, or complete a newer request generation. ### Proposed fix Assign a monotonically increasing epoch to every request tracking generation: - Bind each queued store job to `(req_id, epoch)`. - Atomically increment the counter and enqueue the epoch-tagged job. - Validate the epoch before I/O and before processing completion. - Ignore stale completions without modifying the current counter. - Scope saved offsets, pressure state, KV events, deferred-finished state, and deletion to the same epoch. - Emit `finished_sending` only when the matching generation reaches zero. ### Fix status I have a local epoch-based fix with deterministic lifecycle tests. In local validation, the patched worker no longer exhibited counter underflow or the resulting KV starvation. I can submit a PR against `main`. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Feature][DSpark]: Enable varlen for Qwen 3.x (GDN)
signals.text: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch Adaptive verification has a firm requirement that the attention backend must not use the CPU-side query lengths as a source-of-truth, instead using the gpu tensors (so that we can run the confidence-based assignment on the GPU without synchronizing the CPU). Additionally, kernels must be able to support decode batches where requests have different query lengths per request. Currently, it is not clear if our various GDN decode kernels are compatible with varlen execution. We should audit the flashinfer and/or triton GDN decode kernels and check if we can run decode with a ragged batch. If it's feasible, we should wire it up, validate correctness, evaluate performance, and merge support. signals.title: [Bug]: draft_model speculative decoding crashes at init under TP>1 when draft hidden_size > target (TRT-LLM fused allreduce+RMSNorm workspace sized from target only)
signals.text: ### Summary With `draft_model` speculative decoding under tensor parallelism (`TP>1`), the engine crashes at init when the **draft model's `hidden_size` is larger than the target model's**. The `fuse_allreduce_rms` compilation pass builds the FlashInfer TRT-LLM fused allreduce+RMSNorm workspace with a token budget derived from the **target** model's `hidden_size` only. When the draft model then runs its own forward under TP, its larger `hidden_size` overflows that workspace and `check_trtllm_allreduce_fusion_workspace_metadata` raises, aborting startup. `draft_hidden < target_hidden` and `TP=1` both work; the crash is specific to **`draft_hidden > target_hidden` AND `TP>1`**. ### Environment - vLLM `v0.27.1`, V1 engine, `dtype=torch.bfloat16` - 2×H100 PCIe (80GB), `tensor_parallel_size=2` - `compilation_config.pass_config.fuse_allreduce_rms: True` (default), FlashInfer allreduce backend - Full raw server logs for all arms (`collect_env` included): https://github.com/seongyun1104/depthchart/tree/39b1557/draft_model_tp_bug ### Reproduction | Arm | target (TP) | draft | draft_hidden vs target_hidden | result | |-----|-------------|-------|-------------------------------|--------| | A | Qwen3-30B-A3B (**TP=1**) | Qwen3-4B | **2560 > 2048** | OK (acceptance 83.8%, normal) | | B | Qwen3-30B-A3B (**TP=2**) | Qwen3-4B | **2560 > 2048** | **CRASH** at init | | C | Qwen3-30B-A3B (TP=2) | Qwen3-0.6B | 1024 < 2048 | OK (acceptance 73.1%, coherent) | Arm A vs B isolates the trigger to **`TP>1`**: same `draft_hidden > target_hidden` pair, only the parallelism differs. Arm C shows the same TP=2 target is fine when `draft_hidden < target_hidden`. Arm B command (greedy): ``` vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --override-generation-config '{"do_sample": false}' \ --speculative-config '{"method": "draft_model", "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-4B", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}' ``` (Qwen3-4B `hidden_size=2560` as draft; Qwen3-30B-A3B `hidden_size=2048` as target.) ### Traceback (arm B, verbatim) ``` File ".../vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/allreduce_rms_fusion.py", line 265, in call_trtllm_fused_allreduce_norm ... check_trtllm_allreduce_fusion_workspace_metadata( File ".../flashinfer/comm/trtllm_ar.py", line 1026, in check_trtllm_allreduce_fusion_workspace_metadata raise ValueError(error_msg) ValueError: Workspace validation failed: - token_num (8192) * hidden_dim (2560) exceeds workspace max_token_num (8192) * hidden_dim (2048). This may cause Illegal Memory Access. ``` `hidden_dim (2560)` is the draft (Qwen3-4B); the workspace budget `hidden_dim (2048)` is the target (Qwen3-30B-A3B). ### Where it comes from The fused-allreduce workspace token budget is `max_token_num = max_size // (hidden_dim * element_size)`, and `hidden_dim` is taken from the target model config in the pass. The draft model's forward under TP issues the same fused allreduce with its own (larger) `hidden_size`, exceeding the target-sized budget. Note (not a proposed fix): patching the pass `__init__` to use `max(target_hidden, draft_hidden)` did **not** resolve it — the run still reports `hidden_dim (2048)` in the validation error, so the workspace metadata that is actually checked is created upstream of that pass field. A correct fix has to reach the workspace **creation** site so its stored `hidden_dim` accounts for the draft model. ### Relationship to #50877 / #50932 Same theme (FlashInfer allreduce workspace/buffer under a draft model that adds allreduce traffic), but a **distinct backend**: - #50877 / PR #50932 — the **MNNVL** path (`trtllm_mnnvl_ar`, Lamport buffer rotation); #50932 touches `flashinfer_all_reduce.py` / `fused_allreduce_gemma_rms_norm.py` and adds an `is_buffer_size_sufficient` admission guard. - This report — the **TRT-LLM fused allreduce+RMSNorm** compilation-pass path (`allreduce_rms_fusion.py` → `flashinfer/comm/trtllm_ar.py`), which #50932 does not touch. Filing separately so the TRT-LLM path is tracked; happy to fold into #50877 if maintainers prefer a single tracking issue.

signals.title: [Feature][DSpark]: Improve Adaptive DSpark Online Profiling
signals.text: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch The initial version does profiling at startup to estimate the verification step time by replaying the recorded CUDA graphs. This is known to have some drift, especially at higher batch sizes. Here are my results from initial study: We want to extend this to fully online profiling. However, there are some challenges that make this tricky: - Online profiling may lead to "dead spots": one-time latency spikes make a certain batch size appear unattractive, leading to the adaptive verifier to never select that batch size, which leads to negative feedback and stale data limiting our range of profiled values. Generally there is an "exploration vs exploitation" problem here, as well as a requirement for some way to detect and eliminate outliers (such as those caused by JIT compilation). - Variable sequence lengths make it hard to measure a single reliable estimate of execution time for a given number of tokens. In practice we will want some way to account for this: either tracking measured points in 2D (num_tokens, max_seq_len or mean_seq_len), or estimating the overhead added per-token of KV reads We should do a more comprehensive study on the drift across models, batch sizes, and sequence lengths. Then, we should design a fully-online solution that addresses the shortcomings, and evaluate the performance gain. We should also evaluate the "oracle" speedup with perfect timing prediction (retrospectively) to assess how much performance can be gained

signals.title: [CI Failure][Anthropic] /v1/messages returns 500 when stop_sequences has more than 4 items
signals.text: ### Your current environment Observed in vLLM Buildkite CI while running PR #48215. ### Describe the bug The stateless OpenAPI Schemathesis test for `POST /v1/messages` can generate an Anthropic request containing more than four `stop_sequences`. The Anthropic request schema accepts the payload, but converting it to `ChatCompletionRequest` raises a Pydantic validation error because the OpenAI `stop` field permits at most four items. The validation exception is exposed as an HTTP 500 response, so the schema test reports a server error: ```text SUBFAILED entrypoints/openai/test_openai_schema.py::test_openapi_stateless[POST /v1/messages] schemathesis.core.failures.ServerError: Server error [500] Internal Server Error: 2 validation errors for ChatCompletionRequest stop.str Input should be a valid string [type=string_type, input_type=list] stop.list[str] List should have at most 4 items after validation, not 6 ``` The generated request contained six values: ```json { "stop_sequences": ["sequence-1", "sequence-2", "", "sequence-4", "sequence-5", "sequence-6"] } ``` This appears to be a mismatch between the `/v1/messages` OpenAPI request schema and the constraints applied during Anthropic-to-OpenAI request conversion. ### Expected behavior The OpenAPI schema should constrain `stop_sequences` to the supported maximum, or the conversion validation error should be returned as a client error (4xx). Invalid user input should not result in HTTP 500. ### Additional context - Failing test: `entrypoints/openai/test_openai_schema.py::test_openapi_stateless[POST /v1/messages]` - CI build: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/83486 - Encountered while testing https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48215; that PR changes Ultravox/Whisper model code and appears unrelated to the Anthropic entrypoint. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] I searched existing issues and PRs for `test_openapi_stateless`, `/v1/messages`, `stop_sequences`, and the Pydantic maximum-length error. I found related entrypoint/schema issues, but no issue covering this specific failure.

signals.title: RFC: Kimi K3 MoonEP integration roadmap
signals.text: ## Motivation Track the **MoonEP integration** item under Large-scale Serving in #50001 as a small set of independently reviewable PRs. MoonEP (https://github.com/MoonshotAI/MoonEP) is the balanced EP communication library used by Kimi K3: dynamic redundant experts keep every EP rank at exactly `S × K` tokens regardless of router skew, with static shapes and zero-copy dispatch/combine. ## Proposed change - [ ] **BF16 end-to-end integration: backend, dispatch/combine, experts, FusedMoE wiring** — #52101 `"moonep"` `All2AllBackend` + system-compat probe, `MoonEPAll2AllManager`, `MoonEPPrepareAndFinalize` (pad → dispatch → `prefetch_weight` → combine, plan stashed between prepare/finalize), `MoonEPExperts` (`torch._grouped_mm` × 3 over `cu_seqlens[E+B]`), `UnquantizedMoeBackend.MOONEP` + `[E+B]` weight-layout wiring in `FusedMoE` (load-time all-gather of local experts into global order, contiguous gate/up/down tensors), multi-GPU pytest under `tests/kernels/moe/`. Per reviewer request the experts and engine wiring were folded into this PR rather than split out. Validated: kernel test 16/16 on GB300; `vllm serve` OLMoE-1B-7B DP=4/EP=4 eager, greedy output vs. `allgather_reducescatter` baseline 10/16 token-identical, remainder bf16 tie-break flips, mean |Δlogprob| 0.011. - [ ] **MoonEP build / commit pin in `tools/ep_kernels`** — PR TBD MoonEP has no releases or PyPI wheel; pin a commit hash in `install_python_libraries.sh` the same way DeepEP is handled (deferred from #52101 at reviewer request). - [ ] **Tuned grouped GEMM over `cu_seqlens`** — PR TBD Replace `torch._grouped_mm` if profiling shows it limiting on Blackwell; DeepGEMM contiguous-layout kernels are the natural fit for the FP8 path below. - [ ] **Benchmarks** — PR TBD Dispatch/combine benchmark vs `deepep_*` backends under `benchmarks/kernels/`, sweeping router imbalance; e2e eval on Qwen3-30B-A3B once capacity allows. - [ ] **Sharded symmetric-memory expert weight ownership** — PR TBD Replace per-rank weight replication with MoonEP's production layout: one contiguous VMM tensor per projection where rows `[0, E)` alias each home rank's parameter memory. Memory-viability requirement for Kimi-K3 scale. Design question: allocate expert weights inside the MoonEP buffer before weight loading vs. post-load remap. - [ ] **CUDA graph support** — PR TBD MoonEP's fully static `NvS` shapes should make capture tractable. - [ ] **Quantized dispatch + weights (fp8 first)** — PR TBD Kimi-K3-scale serving will not be BF16; needs MoonEP-side support scoping as well. - [ ] **EPLB interaction** — PR TBD MoonEP's dynamic redundant experts overlap with the EPLB item in the same #50001 section; define compose-or-exclude semantics. - [ ] **Async / DBO support** — PR TBD `async_finish=True` + MoonEP's comm stream for prepare_async/finalize_async and dual-batch overlap. ## Scope This issue is a tracking RFC only. Each item should remain independently reviewable. The first four items establish a correctness-first BF16/eager path; the sharded weight-ownership and EPLB items carry the design decisions where maintainer input is requested before implementation.

signals.title: [Bug]: sparse_mla_attention forward_mha falls through to unimplemented base class under low max-num-batched-tokens, surfaces as scheduler KeyError
signals.text: ## Environment - vLLM: v0.27.0, source-built with #51538's two commits (`47f6574`, `db39e67`) applied - Model: GLM-5.2 (compressed-tensors WNA16 Int4-Int8), `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` - Hardware: 4x DGX Spark GB10 (sm_121, capability 12), TP=4, `mp` executor - Attention backend: `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120` (the only one that supports this hardware capability plus a sparse indexer, see below) - Speculative decoding: MTP, `num_speculative_tokens=2` - Relevant flags: `--max-model-len 64000 --kv-cache-memory-bytes 4294967296 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.70 --max-num-seqs 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"NONE"}'` Found while narrowing a separate concurrent-load hang (vllm-project/vllm#51921) under a reduced-memory diagnostic configuration. Not the same bug as #51921: confirmed by reverting only `--max-num-batched-tokens` from 2048 to production's 8192 with everything else identical, this crash disappears and the original silent hang (#51921) returns instead. ## Bug description Sending a long prompt (20000 tokens) under `--max-num-batched-tokens 2048` crashes the engine reproducibly (2/2 runs, exact same crash site both times): ``` File "vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py", line 1761, in update_from_output req_index = model_runner_output.req_id_to_index[req_id] KeyError: 'chatcmpl-<per-request id>' ``` This is downstream of the real failure. All four TP ranks (the scheduler's own rank 0 worker included) hit an identical `NotImplementedError` at the same timestamp: ``` File "vllm/v1/attention/backend.py", line 1052, in forward_mha raise NotImplementedError ``` ## Root cause `vllm/v1/attention/backend.py`'s `MLAAttentionImpl.forward_mha` is a non-abstract base-class method that defaults to `raise NotImplementedError`, meant to be overridden by backends that support MHA-style prefill. `sparse_mla_attention.py`'s override contains: ```python if force_dense or (prefill_max_seq_len <= topk_tokens and not force_masked): return super().forward_mha(...) # the unimplemented base-class path ``` Under chunked prefill with `max-num-batched-tokens=2048`, a 20000-token prompt gets split into chunks no larger than 2048 tokens. If `topk_tokens` (the sparse indexer's per-request top-k budget) is >= 2048, every chunk satisfies `prefill_max_seq_len <= topk_tokens`, permanently routing into the unimplemented path instead of the working masked-MHA implementation a few lines below it. Since all four ranks are running the identical batch shape, they hit this simultaneously. Workers die before producing output; the scheduler's `req_id_to_index` `KeyError` on rank 0 is a consequence of that, not an independent bug, `req_id_to_index` has no guard anywhere against a request going missing because upstream compute failed. ## Reproduction 1. TP=4, GLM-5.2 (or any model on the `sparse_mla_attention.py` code path with a small enough `topk_tokens`), `--max-num-batched-tokens` set low enough that a long prompt's chunk size can be <= `topk_tokens`. 2. Send a prompt whose length exceeds `max-num-batched-tokens`, so chunked prefill kicks in. 3. Every rank raises `NotImplementedError` in `forward_mha` at the same moment; the API returns `500` for all in-flight requests. ## Suggested fix Either implement `forward_mha` in the base class (or raise a clear, catchable, user-facing error instead of a bare `NotImplementedError` that surfaces as an unrelated scheduler `KeyError`), or have `sparse_mla_attention.py`'s branch condition account for cases where the base class path is genuinely unimplemented rather than routing into it unconditionally. Happy to provide full four-rank tracebacks and the exact launch config if useful.
signals.author: joesinvestments

signals.title: [Feature]: Restore length-based speculation skip (speculative max_model_len) or per-request speculative decoding control in V1
signals.text: ## 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch In V0, `--speculative-max-model-len` allowed sequences longer than a threshold to automatically skip speculation (documented in v0.6.x spec_decode docs). In V1, the config plumbing survives — `SpeculativeConfig.max_model_len` is still accepted and `_maybe_override_draft_max_model_len()` still overrides `draft_model_config.max_model_len` (its docstring even says "mainly used for testing that sequences can skip speculation") — but we could not find any runtime consumer under `vllm/v1/`, and empirically the field is a no-op. **Repro (vLLM 0.26.0, DGX Spark GB10, Qwen3.6-27B NVFP4 target + DFlash drafter):** ``` --speculative-config '{"method": "dflash", "model": "z-lab/Qwen3.6-27B-DFlash", "num_speculative_tokens": 10, "max_model_len": 12288}' ``` - Config validation accepts the field, engine boots normally. - A 19,853-token prompt still drafts normally (spec_decode_num_drafts_total +149 for a 150-token completion) — no skip. ## Use case Mixed workloads on a single engine: interactive short prompts get a real speculation win (we measure 1.6–1.8× decode with EAGLE-3/DFlash), but long-document summarization (20K–73K Chinese meeting transcripts) collapses to 5–8% acceptance, making speculation net-negative (decode drops below the no-spec baseline). With no per-request toggle in V1 and the dynamic schedule (`num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size`) keyed on batch size only, there is currently no way to keep speculation for short requests while disabling it for long ones on one engine — and unified-memory hardware (GB10 128GB) cannot co-load a second engine as a workaround. ## Ask Either: 1. Re-implement the V0 behavior: proposers skip drafting when the sequence exceeds the draft model's effective `max_model_len`, or 2. Expose a per-request control (e.g. a SamplingParams / request-level field to disable speculation), or 3. A length-keyed variant of the dynamic speculative schedule. Related: RFC #36657 (Dynamic Speculation Length / confidence-based early exit) addresses the per-step dimension but not the per-request/length dimension. ## Alternatives - Dual serve profiles routed by input length — not viable on unified-memory single-GPU hosts (cannot co-load two large models). - Batch-size-keyed dynamic schedule — wrong dimension for bs=1 long jobs. - Patching the sealed vendor image — not sustainable.

signals.title: [Feature]: Native SM120 backend for Quark/OCP MXFP6 (Dense and Qwen3.5 MoE)
signals.text: This issue tracks an optional native SM120 execution path for vLLM’s existing Quark/OCP MXFP6 support, while retaining software emulation as the fallback. ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch vLLM can load OCP MXFP6 checkpoints through Quark, but CUDA execution currently uses software emulation. PR [#21166](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/21166) added the format and emulation support and left native OCP MX kernels as follow-up work. We built [mxfp6-sm120](https://github.com/Nekofish-L/mxfp6_sm120), a BSD-licensed PyTorch CUDA extension for native OCP W6A8 execution on NVIDIA SM120. It keeps weights in packed MXFP6 E3M2 with UE8M0 scales, quantizes FP16/BF16 activations to MXFP8 E4M3 at runtime, and accumulates in FP32. The current implementation includes: - a general Dense GEMM operator; - a Qwen3.5 routed-MoE path covering routing, W1, activation processing, W2, shared-expert combine, and final reduction; - persistent workspaces and CUDA Graph replay for the tested execution paths. A public vLLM v0.25.1 reproducer loads and serves Qwen3.5-27B and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on two RTX 5090 GPUs with tensor parallel size 2. Compared with the corresponding official FP8 checkpoints, MXFP6 improved output throughput by 9.11% for Qwen3.5-27B and 16.95% for Qwen3.5-35B-A3B. This issue documents the working implementation and measured scope. If this evidence is not yet sufficient to evaluate an upstream contribution, we can add targeted correctness coverage, workloads, hardware configurations, or fallback tests. ### Alternatives The existing Quark software-emulation path remains a functional fallback, but it does not execute the packed weights with native SM120 MX instructions. The repository also contains a narrowly versioned vLLM compatibility patch. That patch demonstrates end-to-end integration for the two tested models; it is not proposed as an upstream patch. ### Additional context #### Public end-to-end results The public reproduction uses vLLM v0.25.1, two PIX-connected RTX 5090 GPUs, tensor parallel size 2, and four fresh service lifecycles in FP8/MXFP6/MXFP6/FP8 order. | Model and workload | FP8 output tok/s | MXFP6 output tok/s | Gain | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Qwen3.5-27B, 3000 input / 1000 output, c32 | 1229.90 | 1341.97 | **+9.11%** | | Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, public `random-mm`, c4 | 678.37 | 793.33 | **+16.95%** | Standalone measurements report a 1.633x geometric-mean speedup over vLLM block-FP8 for the five measured Qwen3.5-27B Dense shapes, and 1.278x over the vLLM FP8 MoE path for the complete Qwen3.5-35B-A3B TP2 MoE layer at B16-B96. Operator, layer, and service results have different measurement boundaries and are not additive. #### Internal runtime reference We also measured the package with an internally optimized vLLM 0.25.1 stack: 22.44% higher output throughput for Qwen3.5-27B and 13.58% for Qwen3.5-35B-A3B. On the 35B-A3B workload, 742 greedy reference cases changed full-character similarity by -0.57 percentage points and answer-section similarity by -0.32 points relative to FP8. Neither paired 95% interval detected a significant loss. This is reference-output fidelity, not task accuracy, and the internal serving results are not claims about the public reproducer. #### Reproduction and evidence - Project: https://github.com/Nekofish-L/mxfp6_sm120 - Public vLLM reproduction: https://github.com/Nekofish-L/mxfp6_sm120/tree/main/examples/vllm - Public serving result: https://github.com/Nekofish-L/mxfp6_sm120/blob/main/benchmarks/results/qwen35_public_vllm_tp2.json - Benchmark methodology: https://github.com/Nekofish-L/mxfp6_sm120/blob/main/docs/benchmarks.md - Original MXFP6 format request: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/17837 - Existing format and emulation support: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/21166

## 🐛 Describe the bug ### What happens On a preempted request, `MooncakeStoreConnector` stores **KV that does not belong to the key**. Those bytes are later read back by another request as a prefix-cache hit, loaded into the KV cache and attended over, which silently corrupts that request's output. ### Why The store is asynchronous. During a step the worker only pushes the store request onto `KVCacheStoreSendingThread`'s queue and returns; reading the blocks off the GPU and issuing the PUT happens later, on the background thread. Freeing the blocks takes an entirely separate path: in a following step the scheduler preempts the request, and core returns its blocks to the free pool within that same step, after which another request overwrites them. There is no synchronization between the two — nothing constrains when a queued job reads device memory relative to when its blocks are handed to someone else. The preemption notice does not help either. The earliest it can reach the worker is on the next step's connector metadata (`MooncakeStoreConnectorMetadata.preempted_req_ids`), and core has already freed the blocks in the very step that builds that metadata. In other words the blocks can be fully overwritten before the notice arrives, and with async scheduling the scheduler runs further ahead still. The only protection today is `request_finished()` returning `delay_free_blocks=True`, which covers the **normal completion** path only. Preemption goes the other way: `build_connector_meta()` calls `reset()` on the tracker, the blocks are freed immediately, and nothing knows that queued jobs still have to read them. ### Consequences 1. **Silent wrong results.** The poisoned key holds another request's KV, so a request that hits it attends over KV that is not its own and its output drifts unpredictably, with no error anywhere. 2. **It does not heal.** A key names a fixed token range, so once wrong bytes land under a key, every later request that hits the same prefix keeps being fed them. Contamination grows with uptime rather than decaying. 3. The more memory-constrained the deployment and the more it preempts, the more often this fires — which is exactly the deployment that wants an external KV store. ### How to reproduce Preemption has to actually happen. Configuration: - 2x H20, TP2, Qwen3-32B-FP8 - `--num-gpu-blocks-override 1024` (shrink the GPU cache to force preemption) - mooncake store backend, started cold - load: 96 requests / 48 concurrent / ~400-word prompts / `max_tokens=192` This configuration produces 162 preemptions in a single run. Nothing is visible from the outputs alone (wrong KV makes the text drift, it does not raise), so the determination is made by instrumentation. Two independent signals: **(1) Content fingerprints.** A store key names a fixed token range, so the KV under it is uniquely determined. The patch takes an 8-byte `D_pre` on the GPU **before** `batch_put` (the blocks still hold that key's own KV at that moment) and `D_post` on the destination blocks **after** `batch_get`. A disagreement means the bytes in the store are not the KV that key names, and they are already in a real request's KV blocks, about to be attended over. **(2) A scheduler-side block reallocation detector.** Recorded independently on the scheduler side: whether the blocks a store job references were reallocated to another request while that job was reading them. This signal never looks at the store's contents. The instrumentation, the load and the analysis scripts are at (instrumentation only, no behaviour changes): the fingerprint patch (`probes/fingerprint_on_main.patch`, applies on `643c125fa`), the preemption-forcing server config (`load/ab_serve.sh`), the synthetic load (`load/synth_load.py`, random-gibberish prompts so nothing dedups in the store and every save is a real `batch_put`), the orchestration for one run (`load/ab_run.sh`: cold master, server, poll `/health`, send the load) and the two analysers (`analysis/analyze_evi.py` for totals, `analysis/bad_dist.py` to split poisoned keys by `save_seq`). ### Measured `643c125fa` plus the instrumentation above, one run against a cold store, all 96 requests returned, 162 preemptions: | | | |---|---| | keys written with a fingerprint | 16,770 | | of those, written twice with differing content (excluded as ambiguous) | 0 | | read-backs checked | 16,788 | | **fingerprint mismatches** | **155** | | poisoned keys | 155 | | **requests that read wrong KV** | **1 / 96** | | jobs the scheduler-side detector flagged as "blocks reallocated while being read" | 25 | | preemptions | 162 | All 155 poisoned keys come from a single store job (`save_seq=125`), and that job is one of the 25 the scheduler-side detector flagged independently — two unrelated signals point at the same job. ### Relation to #51637 / #51662 #51637 describes a **secondary** problem derived from the same preemption scenario: a request that is rescheduled after preemption keeps its original req_id, and the store thread's bookkeeping only checks whether the req_id matches, so a leftover job from the retired generation spends the new generation's credit. The live save is silently dropped, the counter goes negative, the entry can never retire, `finished_sending` is never emitted and the blocks are held until KV starvation. #51662 fixes that. This issue is about the block lifetime itself: it never covered the preemption path to begin with. ## Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug]: Client stop strings match inside the reasoning segment for think-in-prompt models, truncating CoT and yielding content=None
signals.text: ### Your current environment Reproduced on 0.21.1 and 0.25.2.dev (V1 engine), 2x DGX Spark GB10 TP=2, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 with `--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4` and `--reasoning-config '{"reasoning_parser":"deepseek_v4","reasoning_start_str":"<think>","reasoning_end_str":"</think>"}'`. The mechanism is model-agnostic for any think-in-prompt template (DeepSeek V4, Qwen3-style). ### 🐛 Describe the bug With think-in-prompt templates, generation begins INSIDE the reasoning segment. The V1 detokenizer evaluates client `stop` strings against the whole output stream, so a stop string that the chain-of-thought naturally restates fires mid-`<think>`: `</think>` never arrives, the reasoning parser cannot close the segment, and the response returns `content: None` with `finish_reason: stop`. This is easy to hit unintentionally at scale: lm-evaluation-harness sends `stop[:4]` (e.g. `"Question:"`) on every request, and CoT loves restating `Question:`. On GSM8K n=50 at temp 0.6 we measured 8-15/50 responses decapitated this way (score 0.66-0.84); with stops suppressed inside reasoning it dropped to 1/50 nulls (0.98). Hosted deployments of the same checkpoints are immune because they scope stops to content — that behavior gap is the bug. It also masquerades as a model failure ("the model returned nothing"), which cost the community significant misdiagnosis time (see tonyd2wild/DeepSeek-v4-Flash-0731-DSpark-1M-NVFP4-KV-2x-DGX-Spark issue #18, where ~30% of eval nulls traced to this). ### Repro sketch 1. Serve any think-in-prompt reasoning model with a reasoning parser configured. 2. Send a request whose prompt ends inside `<think>` (standard chat template behavior with thinking enabled) plus `stop: ["Question:"]` and a prompt the model will deliberate about. 3. When the CoT restates "Question:", the response truncates mid-reasoning: no `</think>`, `content: None`. ### Expected behavior Stop strings should stay dormant while the reasoning segment is open and be evaluated only against text FOLLOWING the reasoning end marker (matching hosted-API behavior). EOS and max_tokens unaffected; non-thinking requests untouched. One subtlety for spec decoding: `update()` receives up to k+1 tokens per step, so the chunk that carries the end marker also carries the reasoning that precedes it — on closing, the stop-check offset must advance past the marker or a stop in the last <=k reasoning tokens still fires. ### Existing community fix A per-request guard implementing exactly this (markers from `--reasoning-config` with `<think>`/`</think>` fallback, process-wide opt-out env var, spec-decode one-chunk handling) has been running in production in the DSpark community for 10+ days across vLLM 0.21.1 and a 0.25.2.dev port: patch at tonyd2wild/DeepSeek-v4-Flash-0731-DSpark-1M-NVFP4-KV-2x-DGX-Spark `patches/0005-suppress-stops-in-reasoning.patch` (and PR #32 there for 0.25.x trees). Happy to adapt it into a proper vLLM PR with tests if maintainers agree with the direction — main design question is whether the guard should be default-on (hosted-parity) or opt-in via a sampling/serving flag. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

### 🐛 Describe the bug A non-streaming request to `/inference/v1/generate` with `sampling_params.n > 1` returns **fewer than `n` choices**, non-deterministically. No error is raised and the response is a well-formed `GenerateResponse`, the completions are simply missing, so callers silently train on or serve fewer samples than they asked for. `/v1/completions` with the same `n` always returns `n`. ```python import collections, requests BASE, MODEL = "http://127.0.0.1:8123", "Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B" def n_choices(n, i, extra=None): sampling_params = {"max_tokens": 5, "temperature": 1.0, "n": n, **(extra or {})} body = {"request_id": f"r{n}-{i}", "model": MODEL, "token_ids": [9707, 1879, 11], "sampling_params": sampling_params} return len(requests.post(f"{BASE}/inference/v1/generate", json=body, timeout=180).json()["choices"]) for n in (2, 4, 8): print(n, dict(collections.Counter(n_choices(n, i) for i in range(10)))) ``` Observed (10 runs per `n`; expected `{n: 10}` in all three): ``` 2 {1: 6, 2: 4} 4 {2: 5, 3: 3, 4: 2} 8 {5: 2, 7: 5, 3: 1, 6: 2} ``` With multimodal input (`/v1/chat/completions/render` → `token_ids` + `features`, Qwen2.5-VL-3B), `n=4` returned 3 choices on 6/6 runs. ## Root cause `vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py::serve_tokens` sets `output_kind` only for streaming: ```python if request.stream: sampling_params.output_kind = RequestOutputKind.DELTA ``` so non-streaming requests keep the `SamplingParams` default, `RequestOutputKind.CUMULATIVE`. The OpenAI path does the opposite — `CompletionRequest.to_sampling_params` uses `FINAL_ONLY` when not streaming. Under `CUMULATIVE`, `serve_tokens_full_generator` keeps only the last streamed output: ```python async for res in result_generator: final_res = res # earlier per-sequence updates are discarded ... for output in final_res.outputs: # only the sequences updated in that last step ``` so sequences that finished earlier never reach `choices`. ## Suggested fix ```diff - if request.stream: - sampling_params.output_kind = RequestOutputKind.DELTA + sampling_params.output_kind = ( + RequestOutputKind.DELTA if request.stream else RequestOutputKind.FINAL_ONLY + ) ``` matching `CompletionRequest.to_sampling_params`. A regression test asserting `len(choices) == n` for `n > 1` would cover it; the existing scale-out tests only use `n=1`. ## Workaround Pass `output_kind` explicitly in `sampling_params`: ```python "sampling_params": {"n": 4, "max_tokens": 64, "temperature": 1.0, "output_kind": 2} # 2 = FINAL_ONLY ``` Verified 10/10 correct for `n=2/4/8` (text) and 6/6 for token IDs + multimodal features, with correct indices, distinct completions and logprobs intact. ## Context Found while moving TRL's RL trainers from their custom vLLM server onto `vllm serve`. `/inference/v1/generate` is the only endpoint that accepts pre-tokenized prompts together with multimodal features, which RL rollouts need, and RL generates with `n = num_generations`, so the bug hits the main path. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug] XPU qnorm/rope kernel: overlapping stores in one program corrupt the KV cache nondeterministically
signals.text: **File:** `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/xpu/xpu_qnorm_rope_kv_fp8_insert.py` **Confirmed present in v0.27.1** (tag `6e448d0ea9bf`) and on `main`. ## Summary In the KV branch, the kernel stores all 512 elements of `kv` — RoPE region included, still unrotated — and then overwrites that region with the rotated values at stride-2 addresses: ```python # lines 93-94 kv_full = tl.load(kv_base + offs) tl.store(kv_out_base + offs, kv_full) # writes the unrotated rope region ... # lines 106-107 tl.store(kv_out_base + even_offs, new_even) # overwrites it, stride-2 addresses tl.store(kv_out_base + odd_offs, new_odd) ``` Two stores to the same addresses within one program, with different lane-to-address mappings and no ordering between them. Nothing guarantees the rotated store wins. ## Evidence On MTT S5000 (MUSA), 4096 tokens × 64 heads, compared against FlagGems' fused kernel, which is byte-exact against the pure-torch reference on the same inputs: - **30 tokens** of 4096 have a cache RoPE region that differs - **29 of those 30** hold values exactly equal to the **unrotated** `kv` — i.e. the bulk store landed last - the remaining one is partially overwritten, consistent with a lane-granular race - a **second run on identical inputs gives 29, not 30** — nondeterministic Concretely, token 96: the cache holds `[1.023, 0.262, -1.516, -0.277]`, exactly the raw `kv` values, where the correct rotated values are `[-0.441, 0.961, 1.531, -0.132]`. ## Fix One line, and it is also cheaper — mask the bulk copy so the overlap never exists: ```python tl.store(kv_out_base + offs, kv_full, mask=offs < NOPE_DIM) ``` This skips 64 redundant stores per KV token as well. With it applied, output is byte-identical to the reference. ## Note XPU scheduling may simply never expose this, but the ordering assumption does not hold on any backend. We found it because MUSA schedules differently.

signals.title: [Feature]: Support NVFP4 DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 with FP4 KV cache + DSpark speculative decoding on SM121 (DGX Spark)
signals.text: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch ## Summary Requesting first-class support for serving **NVFP4** DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 checkpoints (e.g. `Rarri/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-NVFP4`) with **FP4 KV cache** (`nvfp4` / `nvfp4_ds_mla`) **and DSpark speculative decoding** on SM121 (NVIDIA GB10 / DGX Spark, 2-node TP=2). Today this combination does not work on vLLM main. We currently run it on a fork of jasl's branch (PR #41834) which serves the NVFP4 checkpoint but **cannot** do DSpark speculative decoding with it (draft loader fails with `KeyError: 'layers.0.ffn.experts.routed_experts.w13_input_scale'`). vLLM main v0.27.1 fails earlier at startup on SM121 with the DeepGEMM "Unknown SF transformation" error (see #51884). ## Environment - **Hardware**: 2× NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10), compute capability 12.1 / SM121, Linux ARM64, two-node TP=2 - **Model (NVFP4)**: `Rarri/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-NVFP4` - ModelOpt mixed-precision conversion: `producer: dsv4-nvfp4-experts-mtp-fallback` - `quant_method: fp8`, `quant_algo: MIXED_PRECISION`, `moe_quant_algo: NVFP4`, `group_size: 16`, `format: e4m3` - **Model (FP8)**: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` - **vLLM versions tested**: - v0.27.0 / v0.27.1 (main) — fails at startup on SM121 (DeepGEMM "Unknown SF transformation") - jasl fork branch `codex/ds4-sm120-min-enable` (PR #41834), image `vllm-jasl-41834:latest` — serves NVFP4 but no DSpark - **KV cache dtypes**: `fp8`, `fp8_ds_mla`, `nvfp4`, `nvfp4_ds_mla` - **Speculative decoding**: DSpark, 5 speculative tokens, `--speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}'` - **Serving config**: `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85`, `--block-size 256`, `MTP_NUM_TOKENS=5`, `MAX_MODEL_LEN=131072`, `MAX_NUM_SEQS=4` ## What we want 1. Serve the **NVFP4** DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 checkpoint on SM121 with **FP4 KV cache** (`nvfp4` / `nvfp4_ds_mla`). 2. Enable **DSpark speculative decoding** on top of that NVFP4 target (MTP draft), without the draft loader failing on missing NVFP4 scale tensors. 3. Have the DSpark draft built under its **own model/quant config** so an NVFP4 target does not corrupt the MXFP4 draft experts (see abandoned PR #49133). ## What fails today ### On vLLM main (v0.27.1, official `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1-aarch64-cu129`) Startup fails on SM121 with the DeepGEMM scale-layout error: ``` RuntimeError: Assertion error (/workspace/.deps/deepgemm-src/csrc/apis/layout.hpp:60): Unknown SF transformation ``` This is the same class of failure as #51884 / #51758 (DeepGEMM SM120/121 regression). Full report: #51884. ### On jasl's fork (PR #41834) — NVFP4 serves, but DSpark fails The NVFP4 checkpoint loads and serves, but enabling DSpark fails during draft weight loading: ``` KeyError: 'layers.0.ffn.experts.routed_experts.w13_input_scale' ``` The draft loader expects a scale tensor that is absent from the NVFP4 draft params, so speculative decoding cannot be enabled for the NVFP4 target. ## Related issues / PRs - **#51884** — DeepGEMM "Unknown SF transformation" on SM120/121 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash FP8 + DSpark (blocker on main) - **#51758** — v0.26→v0.27 DeepSeek-V4-Flash load regression (DeepGEMM SM120) - **#50720** — DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 + DSpark fails on SM120 (FlashInfer sparse MLA topk=256 dispatch) - **#49133** (PR, closed/abandoned) — "DSpark: build draft under its own model/quant config (NVFP4 target corrupts MXFP4 draft experts)". Closed by author with note: *"we have nvfp4 drafter for dsv4-nvfp4 now"* — but that drafter does not work for this checkpoint on SM121. - **#51835** (PR, open) — "Restore DeepSeek-V4 DSpark draft quantization" (restores `deepseek_v4_fp8` for the draft) - **#41834** (PR) — "Add SM12x support for DeepSeek V4 Flash with essential fixes" (jasl's branch we currently run) - **jasl/vllm#43** — our original issue on jasl's fork for this exact scenario ## Request Please add/validate end-to-end support for **NVFP4 DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 + FP4 KV cache + DSpark speculative decoding** on SM121, including: - Making the DSpark draft loader work with NVFP4 targets (missing `w13_input_scale` / NVFP4 scale tensors). - Building the DSpark draft under its own model/quant config (revive #49133) so NVFP4 targets don't corrupt MXFP4 draft experts. - Confirming the `nvfp4` / `nvfp4_ds_mla` KV cache path works with DSpark on SM121. Happy to test any branch / provide logs.

signals.title: [Bug]: 0.27.1 crashes in custom_all_reduce (illegal memory access) during CUDA graph capture on Hopper TP=4; identical config works on 0.26.0
signals.text: ### Your current environment <details> <summary>Environment</summary> ```text vLLM (failing) : 0.27.1+cu129 vLLM (working) : 0.26.0+cu129 PyTorch : 2.13.0+cu129 (0.26.0 env: 2.11.0+cu129) CUDA (torch built): 12.9 Python : 3.10.12 OS : Linux-5.15.0-94-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.35 GPU : NVIDIA H800, compute capability 9.0 (Hopper / SM90) Driver : 575.57.08 Parallelism : TP=4, single node, no PP, no DP, no EP Model : deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (FP8 checkpoint) KV cache dtype : fp8 ``` The two vLLM versions are installed in **separate virtualenvs** on the same host, so the comparison below changes exactly one variable: the vLLM version. </details> ### 🐛 Describe the bug A TP=4 configuration that has been serving reliably on **0.26.0** for weeks fails to start on **0.27.1**. The engine dies during CUDA graph capture with an illegal memory access originating in the custom all-reduce kernel: ``` Failed: Cuda error /workspace/csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh:164 'an illegal memory access was encountered' torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered ``` Immediately before the crash, 0.27.1 logs: ``` Auto-enabling VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1. Set VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 to opt out. VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH is set, disabling vLLM's torch.compile pipeline. Equivalent to -cc.mode=none. ``` followed by `Capturing CUDA graphs (PIECEWISE): 0%| | 0/51` and then the fault on all four ranks. #### Reproduction The command line is **copied verbatim** from the working 0.26.0 systemd unit — same model, same `--tensor-parallel-size 4`, same `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, same `--gpu-memory-utilization`, same environment variables. Only the interpreter (virtualenv) differs: ```bash vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --served-model-name deepseek-v4 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \ --enable-prompt-tokens-details \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8012 ``` - On **0.26.0**: starts normally, serves traffic. - On **0.27.1**: crashes as above, reproducibly, every attempt. #### What I ruled out I ran this twice with different configurations to isolate the cause: | Run | Config | Result | |---|---|---| | 1 | 0.27.1 **with** `--speculative-config` (DSpark), `gpu-mem-util 0.88`, `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"PIECEWISE"}'`, `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` | illegal memory access | | 2 | 0.27.1 **without** speculative decoding, no `expandable_segments`, parameters byte-for-byte identical to the working 0.26.0 unit | **same crash**, `custom_all_reduce.cuh:164` | So the failure is **not** caused by speculative decoding, not by the lowered memory utilization, and not by `expandable_segments` — run 2 has none of them and still crashes. The only remaining variable is the vLLM version itself. #### Possibly relevant `csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh` was heavily refactored between the two releases — `git diff v0.26.0..v0.27.1` shows **+20 / −296** for that file, with the implementation moved into a new `custom_collective_common.cuh`. Given the crash site, that refactor seems like a plausible place to look. #### Not a duplicate of I checked the closest-looking existing reports; none match this configuration: - **#51758** — same headline symptom ("upgrade 0.26.0 → 0.27.0, DeepSeek V4 Flash error"), but that environment is **RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120) + CUDA 13.0**, and the comments trace it to a DeepGEMM scale-factor layout regression missing the `arch_major == 12` branch. This report is **Hopper SM90 / cu129**, and the fault is in the all-reduce kernel, not DeepGEMM. - **#46253** — illegal memory access under `breakable_cudagraph`, but that is a **cross-node** GB10 setup where NCCL falls back to a host-staged transport without GPUDirect. This is a **single-node** TP=4 case. - **#45604** — same file, 4 GPUs, but the reported fault is `invalid argument` in the FlashInfer AllReduce **norm fusion** path with MXFP8. - **#42609** — `custom_all_reduce` IPC handles vs `expandable_segments`, requires DP>1 **and** TP>1; here DP=1, and run 2 does not set `expandable_segments` at all. #### Happy to help I have both versions installed side by side on the same host and can run additional diagnostics (`CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, `--enforce-eager`, `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0`, `--disable-custom-all-reduce`, compute-sanitizer) if that would help narrow it down — just say which would be most useful. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lengthy documentation-related questions.

signals.title: [Bug]: Intermittent streamed-text corruption with MTP speculative decoding — words dropped at quote/byte-merge boundaries (raw /v1/completions repro; non-streaming clean)
signals.text:
### Summary With MTP speculative decoding enabled (`--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}'`), **streamed** output intermittently drops words at quote-adjacent token boundaries. The same requests non-streaming return correct text, and the same server with speculative decoding disabled streams correctly. In the affected session the corruption reproduced on **every** request for ~15 minutes across `/v1/chat/completions` and raw `/v1/completions`, with and without `tools`, at `temperature: 0` and default sampling — so it is not a parser bug (raw completions bypasses the chat template, reasoning parser, and tool parser). ### Environment - vLLM 0.27.1 (wheel), torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, Python 3.12.3, Linux - 1× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation (96GB), FLASHINFER attention backend - Model: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (compressed-tensors NVFP4) + its bundled MTP drafter (`model_mtp.safetensors`) - Serve flags: `--max-model-len 262144 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --enable-chunked-prefill --enable-prefix-caching --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 --reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml --enable-auto-tool-choice --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}'` ### Observed (captured verbatim from the affected session, 2026-08-14 ~21:50-22:00 local) Prompt (chat, stream=true): `Write exactly this sentence back to me: The "implied" volatility is a "forward-looking" measure, and then add one more sentence about it.` Content deltas received (note the missing words *implied*, *volatility is*, *forward*): ``` 'The' ' "' '"' ' a "' '-looking"' ', and it' ' is' ' derived from the' ... ``` Rendered: `The " " a "-looking", and it is derived from the current market prices…` Raw `/v1/completions` (stream=true, temperature 0, **no tools, no chat template**), prompt `Copy this sentence exactly: The "implied" volatility is a "forward-looking" measure.
Copy: `: ``` '<think>' '
' 'The user wants' ' me to copy' … 'The "' 'plied"' ' is a "' 'forward-looking"' ' measure.

' … ``` (`im` of *implied* and the word *volatility* are missing between the quoted fragments.) Same requests with `stream: false`: full, correct text. Same requests after restarting with speculative decoding **off**: streamed text correct, e.g. deltas `'The' ' "' 'im' 'plied' '"' ' volatility' ' is' ' a' ' "' 'forward' '-looking' '"' ' measure' '.'`. ### Intermittency (important for triage) The corruption reproduced on ~every streamed request during one server session (first session after a host reboot). Later sessions with a **byte-identical** configuration stream correctly, including under targeted attempts to re-trigger: - cache-cold prompts (unique prefixes, prefix cache unhit) - 4-way concurrent streams - streams racing a 26K-token chunked prefill - temperature 0 / 0.7 / default; with and without `tools` So the failure appears state-dependent (initialization-order or first-session state), not config-dependent. During the affected session, multi-token step deltas were being emitted (speculative accepts), and the dropped text always sat at byte-merge boundaries (quote character + following subword) — consistent with the streamed-delta slicing over multi-token steps losing a merged surface segment, while the non-streaming path (full re-render) is unaffected. ### What I can provide Full SSE captures from both the corrupted and clean sessions, server logs for the affected window, and exact repro scripts. Happy to run instrumented builds — the host that showed the corruption is available and the model/config are pinned. ### Impact Silent partial-text loss for streaming clients (agents, chat UIs) while token counts and non-streaming benchmarks look perfectly healthy — we found it only because an agent's quoted strings kept arriving with words missing. Currently running MTP disabled (losing +52-84% decode throughput) as the workaround.

signals.title: [Bug]: qwen3_5_mtp fails to load at tensor-parallel-size >= 2 (drafter weight shape mismatch)
signals.text:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Collecting environment information... uv is set ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 15.2.0-16ubuntu1) 15.2.0 Clang version : Could not collect CMake version : version 4.2.3 Libc version : glibc-2.43 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.13.0+cu130 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ROCM used to build PyTorch : N/A XPU used to build PyTorch : N/A ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.13 (main, Apr 7 2026, 20:45:25) [Clang 22.1.1 ] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-7.0.0-29-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.43 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : 13.2.78 GPU models and configuration : GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 GPU 1: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 GPU 2: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 GPU 3: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 Ti GPU 4: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 GPU 5: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 GPU 6: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 Nvidia driver version : 610.43.03 ============================== CPU Info ============================== Architecture: x86_64 Vendor ID: AuthenticAMD Model name: AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 9955WX 16-Cores CPU(s): 32 NUMA node(s): 1 ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== [pip3] flashinfer-python==0.6.16.post3 [pip3] numpy==2.3.5 [pip3] torch==2.13.0 [pip3] torchvision==0.28.0 [pip3] transformers==5.15.0 [pip3] triton==3.7.1 ============================== vLLM Info ============================== vLLM Version : 0.27.1 GPU Topology (relevant pair): GPU0 <-> GPU1: NODE (PCIe, no NVLink) ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp",...}'` (equivalently `--spec-method qwen3_5_mtp`) fails to load at `--tensor-parallel-size >= 2` for a Qwen3.5-architecture dense model (`Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, `model_type: qwen3_5`) with a shape-assertion crash inside the MTP drafter's weight loader. It works fine at TP=1 (modulo a separate, likely-unrelated OOM covered at the bottom, on a 24GB GPU specifically). The crash reproduces with both the Qwen3.5-specific and the generic MTP method name, so the method name isn't the variable — it looks like the drafter (loaded via a code path separate from the main model, in `vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py`) ends up with an effective tensor-parallel/world size that's inconsistent with the main model's requested TP degree. **Model:** a Heretic-abliterated, NVFP4-quantized (via NVIDIA Model-Optimizer's `hf_ptq.py`, `--qformat nvfp4`) finetune of `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` (dense, `mtp_num_hidden_layers: 1`). The base model's config declares `mtp_use_dedicated_embeddings: false`. Not a MoE model, no `--quantization moe_wna16`/GPTQ/AWQ involved, so this isn't #39475's `moe_wna16` MTP KeyError, and I confirmed `packed_modules_mapping` in `qwen3_5_mtp.py` is correct (`["q_proj","k_proj","v_proj"]` / `["gate_proj","up_proj"]`), so this isn't #35031's `gate_up_proj` copy-paste bug either — those are the two closest prior issues I could find and neither matches. The checkpoint's own `mtp.*` tensors were preserved unmodified from the original release (spliced back in from the raw upstream checkpoint after an unrelated finetuning step dropped them — `transformers`' `Qwen3_5PreTrainedModel._keys_to_ignore_on_load_unexpected = [r"^mtp.*"]` means any `AutoModel.from_pretrained()` round-trip silently discards `mtp.*` weights, so they have to be reattached from the original checkpoint afterward). I want to flag this clearly in case it's relevant, but I don't believe it's the cause of the crash below — see the "ruled out" list. #### Repro ```bash vllm serve \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' ``` Also reproduces identically with `--spec-method qwen3_5_mtp --spec-tokens 3` in place of the JSON `--speculative-config` form. #### Observed ``` (Worker_TP1 ...) ERROR ... [multiproc_executor.py:912] param.weight_loader(param, loaded_weight, shard_id) (Worker_TP1 ...) ERROR ... [multiproc_executor.py:912] File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/linear.py", line 989, in weight_loader_v2 (Worker_TP1 ...) ERROR ... [multiproc_executor.py:912] param.load_merged_column_weight( (Worker_TP1 ...) ERROR ... [multiproc_executor.py:912] File ".../vllm/model_executor/parameter.py", line 175, in load_merged_column_weight (Worker_TP1 ...) ERROR ... [multiproc_executor.py:912] assert param_data.shape == loaded_weight.shape (Worker_TP1 ...) ERROR ... [multiproc_executor.py:912] AssertionError ``` Both `Worker_TP0` and `Worker_TP1` crash identically, on the first fused (`qkv_proj` or `gate_up_proj`) weight loaded for the MTP block's single decoder layer (`mtp.layers.0.*`). #### Diagnosis With `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG`, the MTP block's `mlp.down_proj` (a plain row-parallel weight, loaded through a different, less strict code path than the fused-column weights) loads *successfully* right before the crash, with logged shape `torch.Size([5120, 4352])`. The raw checkpoint's `mtp.layers.0.mlp.down_proj.weight` is `(5120, 17408)`. `17408 / 4352 = 4` — not `17408 / 2 = 8704`, which is what correct TP=2 row-parallel sharding should produce. That means the drafter is loading with an effective world size of 4 for at least this tensor, while the rest of the process (main model included) is correctly running at TP=2. The very next fused-column weight for the same MTP layer hits the strict `assert param_data.shape == loaded_weight.shape` in `load_merged_column_weight`, which — unlike `down_proj`'s loader — doesn't tolerate the inconsistency. I wasn't able to pin down exactly where inside `llm_base_proposer.py`'s model/parallel-config construction for `Qwen3_5MultiTokenPredictor` the world size diverges — didn't have a local vLLM checkout set up to add print statements at `get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size()` in the drafter's construction path specifically. The `down_proj` shape is solid, reproducible evidence of *that* the divergence happens; not *why*. #### Ruled out - **Not the method name / CLI form**: identical crash with `--spec-method qwen3_5_mtp` and with the generic `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp",...}'` form. - **Not an NVFP4-quant-exclusion config issue**: tested directly against `ModelOptNvFp4Config.is_layer_excluded()` in a Python shell with the checkpoint's real `hf_quant_config.json` — `mtp.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj` and all sibling MTP linear-layer names correctly resolve as excluded from NVFP4 quantization. The destination parameters are being allocated as plain unquantized `nn.Parameter`s, same as the main model's, so this isn't a quantization-format/exclude-list matching problem. - **Not an actual architecture incompatibility.** I initially assumed the checkpoint's `q_proj` being unusually wide (12288, which is 48 attention-heads'-worth against a nominal 24-head config) was the root cause. That's wrong: the *main* model's decoder layers have the identical `q_proj=(12288,5120)` shape (likely related to `attn_output_gate: true` in the config) and load/serve correctly at TP=2. `Qwen3_5MultiTokenPredictor.__init__` explicitly constructs its single layer via the exact same `Qwen3_5DecoderLayer` class the main model uses for its full-attention layers, so this shape is not MTP-specific and not the bug. - **Disappears entirely at TP=1** — all weight loading succeeds, including everything that crashes at TP=2. (At TP=1 on a single 24GB GPU I then hit a separate `torch.OutOfMemoryError` while constructing `Qwen3_5MTP`'s `ParallelLMHead`, which persisted even after cutting `--max-model-len` from 262144 down to 32768 with no change in the reported memory figures — suggesting the MTP drafter may be allocating its own dedicated `embed_tokens`/`lm_head` regardless of the checkpoint's `mtp_use_dedicated_embeddings: false`, though I haven't confirmed that with an actual memory snapshot at the crash site, just arithmetic that happens to line up — `vocab_size=124160, hidden_size=5120` gives ~1.27GB per duplicated embed/lm_head tensor. Flagging this separately since it may or may not be related; happy to open it as its own issue if it turns out to be unrelated to the TP crash above.)
