signals.title: [Bug]: disagg_epd_proxy encoder fan-out restarts round-robin per request, overloading first encoder
signals.text: ### Your current environment NA ### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Problem In `examples/disaggregated/disaggregated_encoder/disagg_epd_proxy.py`, encoder requests are distributed with: ```python # Round-robin over encode servers to distribute load a bit url_cycle = (e_urls[i % len(e_urls)] for i in range(len(mm_items))) ``` This is only round-robin within a single incoming request. Since `i` always starts at `0` for every request, `e_urls[0]` receives the first multimodal item of every request. If most requests contain one image/audio item, then all encoder traffic goes to the first encoder instance. If most requests contain fewer multimodal items than encoder instances, later encoder instances receive little or no traffic. ### Example With 3 encoder instances: ```text Request with 1 image -> E0 Request with 1 image -> E0 Request with 1 image -> E0 ``` With 2 images per request: ```text Request 1 -> E0, E1 Request 2 -> E0, E1 Request 3 -> E0, E1 ``` `E2` is never selected in the second case. ### Expected Behavior The proxy should distribute encoder sub-requests fairly across encoder instances over time, not restart from `e_urls[0]` for every incoming request. ### Possible Fixes One option is to maintain a global round-robin cursor, for example: ```python start = app.state.encoder_rr_idx app.state.encoder_rr_idx = (app.state.encoder_rr_idx + len(mm_items)) % len(e_urls) url_cycle = (e_urls[(start + i) % len(e_urls)] for i in range(len(mm_items))) ``` Because the proxy is async, this should probably be protected with an `asyncio.Lock` or replaced with another concurrency-safe strategy. Another simpler option is to choose an encoder randomly per multimodal item: ```python target_url = random.choice(e_urls) ``` This avoids hot-spotting `e_urls[0]`, although it is not deterministic round-robin. ### Affected File `examples/disaggregated/disaggregated_encoder/disagg_epd_proxy.py` ### Additional Context The current comment says “Round-robin over encode servers,” but the implementation is only per-request modulo assignment. This can lead to uneven encoder load in common single-image request workloads. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

Container image is a community build (`ghcr.io/spark-arena/dgx-vllm-eugr-nightly`), but the affected code is stock `vllm` under `/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/`, not anything the image itself patches. ### 🐛 Describe the bug The Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages` endpoint crashes whenever a client sends a `tool_result` content block whose `content` array includes an Anthropic `tool_reference` item. This happens organically with Claude Code sessions that have a large number of tools available (multiple MCP servers configured), where the Anthropic API's tool-search/dynamic-tool-discovery beta feature lets a tool result reference another tool by name instead of re-embedding its full definition. Once a `tool_reference` block appears anywhere in a conversation's history, every subsequent request in that conversation fails — the coding agent gets no further responses. **Root cause:** `_convert_user_tool_result` in [`vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py) converts every other known item type (`text`, `image`) into a template-safe OpenAI content item, but for `tool_reference` it appends the **raw, unconverted** Anthropic-shaped block instead: ```python elif item_type == "tool_reference": ref_name = item.get("tool_name") or item.get("name") if ref_name: tool_reference.append( {"type": "tool_reference", "name": ref_name} ) ... if tool_reference: openai_messages.append( { "role": "tool", "tool_call_id": block.tool_use_id or "", "content": tool_reference, # <-- raw Anthropic-shaped items, never converted } ) ``` That raw `{"type": "tool_reference", "name": ...}` dict is handed straight to the model's chat template as the `content` of a `tool`-role message. Most Jinja chat templates (including Qwen3's, confirmed here) only understand content items shaped like `{"type": "text", "text": ...}` or `{"type": "image"/"image_url", ...}`; anything else falls through to a catch-all `raise_exception(...)` branch, so the request fails regardless of which model is served. **Minimal reproduction** (isolates the chat-template layer directly — no server needed, just the model's own tokenizer, reproducing exactly the content shape vLLM's converter produces): ```python from transformers import AutoTokenizer import traceback tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4") # This is exactly the shape vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py's # _convert_user_tool_result() produces for a tool_result block containing # a tool_reference item: the raw Anthropic-shaped dict is passed straight # through as OpenAI-style chat message content, unconverted. messages = [ {"role": "user", "content": "What tools do I have available?"}, { "role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "toolu_01abc123", "content": [ {"type": "tool_reference", "name": "some_mcp_tool"} ], }, ] try: tok.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True) print("NO ERROR (unexpected)") except Exception: traceback.print_exc() ``` **Observed output** (run against the model on disk in this deployment): ``` Traceback (most recent call last): File "/tmp/repro_template.py", line 22, in tok.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True) File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py", line 3108, in apply_chat_template rendered_chat, generation_indices = render_jinja_template( ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/transformers/utils/chat_template_utils.py", line 581, in render_jinja_template rendered_chat = compiled_template.render( ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/jinja2/environment.py", line 1295, in render self.environment.handle_exception() File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/jinja2/environment.py", line 942, in handle_exception raise rewrite_traceback_stack(source=source) File "

signals.title: [Bug] Cross-node TP CUDA-graph replay deadlocks with NCCL 2.28.9 (fixed by NCCL 2.30.4) — watchdog "RPC call to sample_tokens timed out"
signals.text: ### Your current environment 2× NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, SM12.1), connected back-to-back over 200G RoCE. vLLM TP=2 across the two nodes, `mp` distributed executor backend. NCCL 2.28.9 (as shipped). DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731. ### 🐛 Describe the bug With CUDA graphs enabled, serving deadlocks within the first 2–3 requests: a CUDA-graph replay containing NCCL collectives hangs on the cross-node link. The engine watchdog eventually fires with: ``` RPC call to sample_tokens timed out ``` after which the server must be killed. With `--enforce-eager` the identical setup serves indefinitely, which isolated the hang to captured-graph NCCL collectives (not the collectives themselves — eager NCCL is fine under the same traffic). **Root cause / resolution data point:** upgrading NCCL 2.28.9 → **2.30.4** fixes the deadlock with graphs re-enabled; nothing else changed. So this is the NCCL graph-capture bug class, not a vLLM logic bug — but vLLM can save users days here. Related: #41725 (same watchdog signature). ### Suggestion - Document the NCCL ≥2.30.4 requirement for multi-node CUDA-graph capture over RoCE (or gate/warn: if `torch.cuda.nccl.version() < (2,30,4)` and world spans nodes and cudagraphs enabled, log a prominent warning suggesting `--enforce-eager` or an NCCL upgrade). - The watchdog message could surface "likely collective hang inside CUDA graph replay; try --enforce-eager" as a hint — `sample_tokens timed out` sends users to the sampler, which is innocent. _Checked before filing: #41725's thread has no NCCL-version discussion; this adds the missing root-cause data point. NCCL versions verified on both nodes: deadlock on 2.28.9, clean on 2.30.4._

signals.title: [Bug]: FlashInfer TRT-LLM bf16 MoE weight-conversion OOM recurs post-#45589 at TP2 (120B MoE, GB200) — cumem MemPool still doesn't reclaim under pressure
signals.text: ### Your current environment - vLLM: `v0.25.1` - GPU: 4× NVIDIA GB200 (184 GiB/GPU), TP=2, gen colocated with training via NeMo-RL - Model: `NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16` (MoE, BF16), 231 GiB total weights → ~115 GiB/GPU at TP2 - Driver: NeMo-RL, which enables vLLM sleep mode implicitly for weight refit between train/rollout (no explicit `--enable-sleep-mode` on the vLLM CLI — NeMo-RL sets it internally; log confirms `Enabling cumem allocator because sleep mode requires it.`) ### 🐛 Describe the bug Loading the model OOMs inside `convert_moe_weights_to_flashinfer_trtllm_block_layout` (FlashInfer TRT-LLM bf16 MoE block-layout conversion), before CUDA graph capture is reached: ``` torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.38 GiB. GPU 1 has a total capacity of 184.31 GiB of which 191.50 MiB is free. Including non-PyTorch memory, this process has 184.11 GiB memory in use. Of the allocated memory 179.12 GiB is allocated by PyTorch, with 60.38 GiB allocated in private pools (e.g., CUDA Graphs), and 7.44 MiB is reserved by PyTorch but unallocated. ``` This is the same failure signature as #43951 (which I filed and closed) and #48680: `torch.OutOfMemoryError` inside FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE weight conversion, with the bulk of allocated memory landing in cumem "private pools" rather than the normal caching allocator. ### Why I'm re-opening this class of bug instead of assuming #43951 is still fixed #43951 bisected the regression to #41268 (`max_split_size_mb=20` during model load — correct for dense models, catastrophic for MoE's varied-size per-expert transient buffers) and was closed after #45589 landed, which replaced the old `clone()` + Python-list + `torch.stack()` pattern in `convert_moe_weights_to_flashinfer_trtllm_block_layout` with a single pre-allocated output tensor written via `index_select(..., out=...)`. I confirmed **this run's traceback is inside #45589's post-fix code path** (the OOM is raised from the `torch.index_select(..., out=out)` call inside the local `_copy_permuted_expert_to_block_layout` closure, not the old `stack()` call) — so #45589 is present and active here, and the OOM still happens. #45589 reduced the transient-buffer multiplier (roughly 3x → ~1x original weight size), which is enough headroom at TP4 (58 GiB/GPU weights) but not at TP2 (115 GiB/GPU weights) — there simply isn't 60 GiB of slack left to absorb even a single pre-allocated block-layout output buffer plus whatever the cumem `MemPool` is holding onto from earlier in the load. This matches #43951's root-cause analysis: PyTorch's cumem `MemPool` (required for sleep mode, since `expandable_segments` is incompatible with it — pytorch/pytorch#147851) does not reclaim freed segments under memory pressure mid-load (pytorch/pytorch#159674, still open upstream), so transient conversion buffers accumulate in the private pool instead of being reused/released. #48680 (filed 5 days after I closed #43951, different reporter, different model/hardware) is independent confirmation that raising `max_split_size_mb` does not resolve this class of OOM — it's the MemPool's inability to reclaim under pressure, not fragmentation from the split-size cap. ### Workaround in use Forcing `moe_backend=triton` for the affected TP2/120B config bypasses `convert_moe_weights_to_flashinfer_trtllm_block_layout` entirely (Triton's MoE kernel uses weights in place, no block-layout conversion buffer). This avoids the OOM but forgoes the FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE kernel. ### Proposed direction (from #43951, not yet implemented) vLLM already has a snapshot-sweep that reclaims fully-free cumem segments, but it currently only runs at `use_memory_pool()` context exit. Lifting it to run **mid-load** — e.g. triggered from the cumem malloc callback as mapped bytes approach a high-water mark — would bound reserved memory for both dense and MoE models without branching on model type, and doesn't depend on the currently-open PyTorch fix (pytorch/pytorch#159674). Happy to prototype this against the TP2/120B repro above if there's interest. ### Related - #43951 — original bisection to #41268; closed after #45589, which mitigated but did not eliminate this class of OOM - #48680 — independent report that the OOM persists post-#45589, on different hardware/model - #41268 — introduced `max_split_size_mb=20` during model load (correct for dense, adversarial for MoE) - #45589 — reduced (but did not eliminate) the transient buffer multiplier in `convert_moe_weights_to_flashinfer_trtllm_block_layout` - pytorch/pytorch#159674 (open) — cumem `MemPool` does not reclaim freed segments under memory pressure - pytorch/pytorch#147851 — `expandable_segments` incompatible with `MemPool`

signals.title: [Bug]: hybrid Mamba + `--mamba-cache-mode align`: a request near the KV-pool ceiling is admitted, prefilled to 98.9 %, requeued, and re-prefilled forever with zero output tokens and zero preemption accounting
signals.text: ### Your current environment This is a **downstream fork build**, and I want that on the record before the trace, because it determines what I am and am not claiming (see *Scope of the claim* at the bottom). ```text vllm 0.11.2.dev280+gilded.gnosis.v20.vllm4d006a4.b12xcd3ce19.fi1ac6942.cu132.20260810.r34 (local-inference-lab/vllm @ dev/gilded-gnosis, upstream integration tree 4d006a43928cdee0…, base image built 2026-08-10) container image localhost/vllm:gg-r34-patched-apc sha256:16a936b877b90fc080181e842f47dbafc5cb8e62688799596836e34ba0b79218 (built FROM the published base docker.io/voipmonitor/vllm@sha256:820181fbbc975cd5291c411cda…, adding exactly one file: see next paragraph) torch 2.12.0+cu132, FlashInfer @ 1ac6942, python 3.12.3 GPU 1x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090, 32,607 MiB, SM 12.0, driver 610.57.04, CUDA UMD 13.3 host Ubuntu 24.04.4, kernel 6.8.0-137-generic, podman 4.9.3 rootless model Qwen3.8-27B (Qwen3.5 architecture: hybrid GDN linear-attention + full attention), EXL3-quantised weights, --kv-cache-dtype fp8 ``` **The scheduler in this image is upstream's own post-#51113 file.** `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` is the vendored r34 copy with exactly the two behavioural hunks of [#51113](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51113) (`c56f169d9ae4`) applied, `sha256 b431c1066dfee3ed56bfa7e71cc8606f9afadc300f22d7fc542c43835d1b22bf`; upstream's own `tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py` from that merge commit passes 20/20 against it and fails 14/20 against the unpatched copy. So this is **not** #43559 or #51113 resurfacing, and it is not the encoder-cap zero-collapse livelock of #51603 / #40757 either — see *Prior art* below. ### 🐛 Describe the bug On a hybrid Mamba model with `--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align`, a request whose length sits close to the KV pool is **accepted** by admission, prefilled to ~99 % of the pool, dropped back to the waiting queue with the pool freed to 0 %, and prefilled again — forever. The cycle has a fixed 30-second period. Prompt throughput pins at ~960 tok/s, generation throughput is `0.0` for the whole run, and **not one output token is ever produced**. The HTTP request never returns and the server never recovers. It is not wedged — it is busy — so it presents as a very slow request rather than as a hang, and a liveness probe on `/health` keeps passing. Two properties make this worse than a plain admission misjudgement: 1. **`vllm:num_preemptions_total` stays at `0.0`.** Nothing is preempted, because nothing is ever admitted to `running` for long enough to count. The only observable is `vllm:num_requests_waiting_by_reason{reason="capacity"} = 1`, which is indistinguishable from a healthy server that is momentarily full. There is no counter that says "this request was descheduled after partial prefill", so no alert can fire. 2. **The work is discarded, not published.** Over the run the engine logged **261,794 prefix-cache queries and exactly 0 hits**. The cache was consulted on every retry and had nothing to offer, so every retry costs full price and no retry can ever cost less. That is what converts a one-off admission error into an unbounded one. *I now believe property 2 is an instance of the already-reported #45238 rather than a new finding — see Prior art. I am keeping it in the trace because it is the reason the loop is stable, but I am not claiming it as new.* ### Observed cycle ```text INFO 08-16 05:37:17 [loggers.py:314] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 800.0 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Running: 1 reqs, Waiting: 0 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 98.9%, Prefix cache hit rate: 0.0% INFO 08-16 05:37:27 [loggers.py:314] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 959.9 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Running: 0 reqs, Waiting: 1 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 0.0%, Prefix cache hit rate: 0.0% INFO 08-16 05:37:37 [loggers.py:314] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 960.0 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Running: 0 reqs, Waiting: 1 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 0.0%, Prefix cache hit rate: 0.0% INFO 08-16 05:37:47 [loggers.py:314] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 799.9 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Running: 1 reqs, Waiting: 0 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 98.9%, Prefix cache hit rate: 0.0% INFO 08-16 05:37:57 [loggers.py:314] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 960.0 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Running: 0 reqs, Waiting: 1 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 0.0%, Prefix cache hit rate: 0.0% INFO 08-16 05:38:07 [loggers.py:314] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 960.0 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Running: 0 reqs, Waiting: 1 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 0.0%, Prefix cache hit rate: 0.0% INFO 08-16 05:38:17 [loggers.py:314] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 800.0 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Running: 1 reqs, Waiting: 0 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 98.9%, Prefix cache hit rate: 0.0% ``` 63 such lines. Stopped by the operator after 656 s; nothing in the trace suggests it would ever terminate. `/metrics` at the moment of teardown: ```text vllm:num_requests_running 0.0 vllm:num_requests_waiting_by_reason{reason="capacity"} 1.0 vllm:num_preemptions_total 0.0 vllm:prefix_cache_queries_total 261,794.0 vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total 0.0 ``` ### Reproduction One request, one server. `--max-num-seqs 1`, so there is no concurrency and no second request involved in the failure. Exact server argv as run (EXL3 quantisation flags are ours; the scheduler-relevant flags are the last eight): ```sh podman run --rm --device nvidia.com/gpu=all --ipc=host --network host \ -e PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True \ --entrypoint /opt/venv/bin/vllm localhost/vllm:gg-r34-patched-apc \ serve /models/ctx-repo/snapshots/c45c273b0d6ef2859cb2d85b36dd52253c80d878 \ --served-model-name m \ --quantization exl3 \ --quantization-config '{"linear":{"weight":"mxfp8"},"ignore":["re:.*visual\\..*","re:.*in_proj_a$","re:.*in_proj_b$","re:.*in_proj_ba$","re:.*mtp\\..*","lm_head"]}' \ --max-model-len 262144 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9585 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --max-num-seqs 1 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \ --mm-processor-kwargs '{"truncation":false,"max_pixels":8388608}' \ --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[4]}' \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --mamba-cache-mode align \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8251 ``` Startup banner confirms the flags took effect, so this is not a silently-ignored flag: ```text 'enable_prefix_caching': True 'mamba_cache_mode': 'align' Prefix caching in Mamba cache 'align' mode is currently enabled Setting attention block size to 1600 tokens Add 3 padding layers, may waste at most 6.25% KV cache memory Available KV cache memory: 9.39 GiB GPU KV cache size: 265,072 tokens Maximum concurrency for 262,144 tokens per request: 1.01x ``` Then one request: a 261,794-token text prompt (a "needle" document with a 10-digit code at depth 0.5), `max_tokens=16`, `temperature=0`. It never returns. The **shape** that matters, for anyone reproducing on stock vLLM with a Qwen3-Next / Qwen3.5-family checkpoint and no EXL3 involved: - hybrid Mamba/GDN model, `--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align` - speculative decoding on (`mtp`, or anything that makes `use_eagle()` true), `num_speculative_tokens ≥ 1` - `--gpu-memory-utilization` tuned so `GPU KV cache size` is a **few thousand tokens above** `--max-model-len` (here: pool 265,072 vs window 262,144, engine's own "Maximum concurrency" 1.01x) - one request whose prompt is within ~1 % of `--max-model-len` - `--max-num-seqs 1`, `--max-num-batched-tokens` well below the mamba block size, so the prefill is chunked and the failure lands on the final allocation rather than the first ### Why the startup check does not catch it, and the arithmetic `Setting attention block size to 1600 tokens` — the mamba page size forces the attention block size up from the default. With `align`, a request occupies **whole blocks**: | term | value | |---|---| | prompt | 261,794 tokens | | rounded to whole 1,600-token blocks | `cdiv(261794, 1600) = 164` blocks = 262,400 slots | | plus MTP-3 lookahead slots | `num_lookahead_tokens = 3` (`scheduler.py:238-262`) | | plus the mamba group's own running-state and speculative blocks | `1 + num_speculative_blocks` blocks, from the same pool (`single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:1532-1534`) | | plus `BlockPool`'s permanently reserved null block | 1 block (this is #47272's point) | | pool reported by the engine | 265,072 tokens | The pool *looks* like it has 3,278 tokens of slack over the rounded prompt, and the startup check passes. (Deliberately stated in tokens: `GPU KV cache size` on a hybrid model cannot be inverted into a block count — see the note below — so I am not claiming that slack is worth any particular number of blocks.) It is not enough once every term above is added, and the engine only discovers this at the **final** allocation of the prefill — after ~260 k tokens of work have already been done and thrown away. The asymmetry between the two formulas is visible in the source. The startup sizer's per-request bound for the attention group is: ```python # vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py:291-298 AttentionSpec.max_memory_usage_bytes return cdiv(max_model_len, self.block_size) * self.page_size_bytes ``` `cdiv(max_model_len, block_size)` pages and nothing else: no lookahead slots, no decode block, no null block. Runtime admission for the same request goes through: ```python # vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:958-959 (waiting queue) new_blocks = self.kv_cache_manager.allocate_slots( ..., num_lookahead_tokens=effective_lookahead_tokens, ...) # vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py:430-431 num_tokens_need_slot = min(num_tokens_main_model + num_lookahead_tokens, self.max_model_len) ``` and, for the mamba group in align mode, through: ```python # vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:1507-1509 num_required_blocks = cdiv(num_tokens, self.block_size) + self.num_speculative_blocks # :1532-1534, first prefill num_new_blocks = 1 + self.num_speculative_blocks + int(has_partial_hit) ``` **What I have proven and what I have not.** The behaviour above is measured. The exact term that tips the final allocation over is *not* proven by me: `GPU KV cache size` on a hybrid model is a derived figure (`num_blocks // len(kv_cache_groups) * min_block_size`, the subject of #40384), so I cannot recover the block-level counts from the log line, and the card this ran on is not available for an instrumented rerun. What I can say is that the startup bound omits at least the null block (#47272) and the lookahead slots, that admission demands both, and that at 1,600-token blocks each omitted page is 0.61 % of a 262 k window — which is precisely the size of the gap. **If a maintainer tells me which counters to dump, I will run an instrumented reproduction and post the block-level numbers.** ### Measured band, one engine start per row, identical flags otherwise | `--gpu-memory-utilization` | available KV | `GPU KV cache size` | max concurrency @262,144 | result | |---|---|---|---|---| | 0.955 | 9.28 GiB | — | — | **refuses to start**: needs 9.29 GiB, suggests max len 260,800 | | 0.9555 | 9.30 GiB | 262,144 | 1.00x | starts, then **deadlocks** mid-prefill, `reason="capacity"`, 0 tok/s | | 0.958 | 9.38 GiB | 263,608 | 1.01x | starts (no request sent) | | 0.9585 | 9.39 GiB | 265,072 | 1.01x | starts, then **livelocks**: 30 s re-prefill cycle, 0 output tokens | | 0.959 | 9.41 GiB | 265,072 | 1.01x | starts (identical pool) | | 0.96 | 9.44 GiB | 265,072 | 1.01x | starts (identical pool) | Two things fall out of the band: - The pool is quantised: 0.9585, 0.959 and 0.96 all yield the same 265,072 tokens. So on this card **there is no `--gpu-memory-utilization` that makes a 262,144-token request schedulable under align mode.** The configuration is unserviceable, and every value of the knob either refuses to start or livelocks. - The 0.9555 row (pool exactly `max_model_len`, "Maximum concurrency … 1.00x", then 0 tok/s) is, as far as I can tell, exactly the boundary case #47272 describes and fixes. The same build with `--max-model-len 256000` at 0.9585 (pool 264,777, 1.03x) serves a 254,964-token needle exactly in 179 s, then serves a second 254,967-token needle in the same process after the first is released. So the feature itself works; it is specifically the request-close-to-the-pool case that fails. ### Expected behaviour In rough order of value: 1. **Reject at admission.** A request whose rounded, lookahead-inclusive, null-block-inclusive requirement exceeds the *whole pool* can never be scheduled at any future time, no matter what else drains. It should fail with a 400-class error naming the maximum servable length — the same information `_check_enough_kv_cache_memory` already prints at startup — rather than being accepted and retried forever. #35541 asked for exactly this and was closed as stale. 2. **Make the startup bound and the admission bound the same function**, the way #40946 did for SWA/chunked-local by introducing `max_admission_blocks_per_request` on the spec and calling it from both `max_memory_usage_bytes` and `get_num_blocks_to_allocate`. The align-mode rounding, the lookahead slots and the null block belong in that one function, so the two paths cannot drift. Today a configuration that cannot serve one native-length request still boots. 3. **Account for it.** A request descheduled after partial prefill should increment a preemption or restart counter. `num_preemptions_total = 0.0` through 63 full re-prefills of a 261 k prompt is a monitoring blind spot independent of the allocation bug: the only signal is a `waiting` gauge that healthy back-pressure produces too. 4. Optionally, bound the retries: a request that has been descheduled from the same admission decision N times without gaining ground should be failed rather than retried. ### Prior art I checked, and how this differs Searched `vllm-project/vllm`, issues and PRs, open and closed (queries recorded in our receipt, linked below). - **#47272** *(open PR, "Reserve the KV null block when validating max_model_len")* — **the closest thing to a duplicate, for one of my six rows.** Its exact-boundary case ("passes the check, logs `Maximum concurrency … 1.00x`, is one usable block short at runtime, engine hangs at 0 tok/s") is my 0.9555 row. It does not cover align-mode whole-block rounding or the lookahead slots, and it does not address the retry loop or the missing accounting. I have posted the six-row band as a comment there: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47272#issuecomment-5307330064 . - **#35541** *(closed as not-planned/stale)* — asked for exactly recommendation 1 ("vLLM should abort requests that can never fit in the KV cache block pool with a clear error, rather than hanging indefinitely"). Different mechanism: there the request never starts (`allocate_slots` returns `None` immediately). Here it prefills to 98.9 % first, which is what burns the GPU. - **#45238** *(open)* — align mode registers only ~1–2 mamba block hashes per request, and `HybridKVCacheCoordinator` requires every group to hit, so a mamba miss vetoes the attention matches and the hit rate collapses to 0 %. I believe this **is** the explanation of my 261,794 queries / 0 hits, so I am *not* offering that as a new finding. - **#51603** *(merged)* and **#51582** / **#40757** / **#40707** — mamba-align livelocks where `_mamba_block_aligned_split` collapses a chunk to **zero** tokens because a multimodal encoder cap landed mid-block, so the request makes no progress at all. Different trigger (encoder cache, not the KV pool), different signature (0 tokens scheduled vs a full 260 k prefill each cycle), and text-only here — no multimodal item is in this request. #51603 is merged and is *not* in this build; it would not change this trace. - **#40946** *(merged)* — same *class* of defect (runtime admission and startup pool sizing using different formulas) for SWA/chunked-local, and the design I am pointing at in recommendation 2. - **#45387 / #45388** *(closed)* — permanent scheduler deadlock under KV-cache pressure, but the root cause is an unconditional `break` blocking `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` promotion with a KV offloading connector enabled. No connector is enabled here. - **#38516** *(closed as stale)*, **#50509** *(open)* — both about the startup check being unfriendly/overridable. Neither is about admission accepting what it cannot schedule. - Nothing found for: an accepted request being re-prefilled on a fixed period with zero output; `num_preemptions_total` staying at 0 across repeated partial prefills; or align-mode rounding being absent from the startup bound. ### Scope of the claim I can support this **on the fork build named above**, and I say plainly that I have **not** reproduced it on stock vLLM and do not claim it there. What I can say about the transfer: the scheduler file involved is upstream's own post-#51113 copy, the flags are upstream's, the `kv_cache_interface.py` / `kv_cache_manager.py` / `single_type_kv_cache_manager.py` lines quoted above are unmodified vendored upstream code in this image, and nothing in the mechanism touches EXL3 weights, this fork's kernels, or the quantisation path — the failure is a block-count decision taken before any kernel runs. So I would expect any hybrid-Mamba deployment running align mode with speculative decoding and a request near its pool ceiling to hit it, but that is an expectation, not a measurement. The card is a single physical RTX 5090 shared with other work; if a maintainer wants a stock-vLLM reproduction (BF16 Qwen3-Next at a window sized to its own pool), say so and I will schedule one. ### Evidence Full artefacts — the 63-line timeline, every per-probe engine banner, every launch argv, the seven server logs with their sha256s, and the `/metrics` scrape: `receipts/qualification-5090-apc.json` and `receipts/qual-apc-raw/` in <https://github.com/malaiwah/qwen38-27b-exl3>. The prior-art search log, with every query, is in `receipts/upstream-issue-sweep.json` in the same repository. The fork-side record of this trace is local-inference-lab/vllm#394. ### Before submitting a new issue… - [x] Searched for relevant issues (queries recorded and published; see *Prior art*).

### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Summary We found a numerical determinism issue in the Marlin MoE WNA16 path while investigating DeepSeek-V4-Flash. `moe_align_block_size()` may produce different legal orderings of `sorted_token_ids` within blocks assigned to the same expert. Those orderings are semantically equivalent: the same routed tokens are processed by the same experts. However, we observed that Marlin's W13 GEMM can produce slightly different BF16 outputs depending on that within-expert ordering. The numerical differences are very small, but they can propagate through subsequent transformer layers and eventually alter autoregressive generation. ### Isolation We isolated the behavior using a same-forward A/B experiment. Two calls to `moe_wna16_marlin_gemm` used identical: - hidden-state / A input - quantized weights and scales - `expert_ids` - `num_tokens_post_padded` - top-k weights - launch parameters Each call used separately zeroed output and workspace buffers. The only changed input was `sorted_token_ids`: 1. the raw legal ordering produced by the alignment path 2. a deterministic canonical ordering containing the same routed tokens within each expert Across 3 requests and 2 TP ranks, all 6 raw-vs-canonical comparisons produced different W13 output tensors. The geometry where we originally isolated the issue was: ```text M = 8192 K = 4096 N = 2048 top_k = 6 block_size_m = 64 global_num_experts = 256 local_num_experts = 128 ``` ### Numerical magnitude Further experiments localized the permutation sensitivity to the multi-threadblock split-K region. One representative raw-vs-canonical comparison produced: ```text differing BF16 values: 26 max BF16 ULP distance: 4 max absolute difference: 0.0078125 RMS difference: ~1.50e-5 non-finite values: 0 ``` A direct split-K comparison produced: ```text differing BF16 values: 20 max BF16 ULP distance: 4 max absolute difference: 0.00390625 RMS difference: ~6.81e-6 non-finite values: 0 ``` This does not appear to be memory corruption or a gross numerical correctness failure. The magnitude is consistent with ordinary floating-point reduction-order effects. The issue is that two semantically equivalent routed layouts can select different floating-point reduction orderings inside Marlin because their physical block positions differ. ### Expected behavior Equivalent within-expert routed layouts should either: 1. produce a stable result independent of their physical block ordering, or 2. be canonicalized before entering an execution path whose reduction tree depends on that ordering. ### Validated workaround We tested deterministic canonicalization of `sorted_token_ids` within each contiguous expert region after `moe_align_block_size()` and before invoking Marlin. With canonicalization: - expert assignment is unchanged - `expert_ids` are unchanged - `num_tokens_post_padded` is unchanged - expert-map semantics are unchanged - the captured W13 numerical divergence disappears - the downstream layer-0 divergence disappears We have also validated this workaround in our serving environment. We do not think the right characterization is that the split-K scheduler is broken. Our current interpretation is a determinism/contract gap between legal MoE alignment ordering and Marlin's reduction behavior. We can prepare a focused regression test and PR if this interpretation matches the intended Marlin contract. ### AI assistance disclosure AI tools were used during investigation and debugging. The experiments, measurements, and production patch described above were executed and validated on the target hardware. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Summary

Serving Kimi-K3 with TP16 across two 8× B200 nodes (EFA, no NVSwitch/MNNVL),any form of CUDA graph capture produces wrong output or crashes. enforce_eager is correct 100% of the time. Unlike #50147, this reproduces at batch=1 on the first request, with prefix caching disabled and no concurrency. I also tried TP=8 and PP=2, the issue persists

Critically, the FlashInfer fused all-reduce path is disabled on this topology, so the latent-MoE stale-residual fix in #50386 cannot apply here (details below).

Configuration

vllm serve flags:

  • -tensor-parallel-size 16 --trust-remote-code --load-format fastsafetensors
    --moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA
    --disable-custom-all-reduce --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune
    --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90

env: VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=0 VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM=0
VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM=0 NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0 NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0
VLLM_ENABLE_K3_LATENT_MOE_TAIL_FUSION=0

Prefix caching is OFF. All tests below are single-stream, temperature=0, max_tokens=64, identical prompt.

Failure matrix

cudagraph config | result -- | -- enforce_eager: true | Correct output, every time, across many deploys (TP16 and TP8+PP2) default (FULL_AND_PIECEWISE) | Fluent but semantically random multilingual text; host SIGSEGV in cuGraphLaunch / at::cuda::CUDAGraph::replay() on the 3rd request cudagraph_mode: PIECEWISE | No crash. Deterministic collapse to a single repeated token (@ @ @ ...) from the first request VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 | AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered, surfaced at torch.cuda.set_rng_state during Dynamo tracing

Performance impact

Eager decode is ~2.6 tok/s at batch=1 (64 tokens in ~25 s), closely matching the ~2.7 tok/s eager figure in #50147 against ~85 tok/s with graphs. DSpark speculative decoding recovers this to ~10 tok/s, still far below the graph-enabled figure. Eager is therefore not a viable workaround for latency-sensitive serving, which makes graph capture on this topology effectively blocking.

Questions

  1. Is CUDA graph capture expected to be supported for Kimi-K3 on multi-node TP without NVSwitch, where the FlashInfer fused all-reduce path is inactive and collectives fall back to NCCL over EFA? But I tried TP=8 and PP=2 the issue still persist.
  2. Are there other buffers allocated outside capture in the K3 MoE/KDA paths, analogous to the one fixed in #50386, that would be reached on the non-FlashInfer path?

Reproduction

Serve:

vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \ --tensor-parallel-size 16 --nnodes 2 --node-rank $RANK \ --trust-remote-code --load-format fastsafetensors \ --moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA \ --disable-custom-all-reduce --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \ --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 # env: # VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=0 VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM=0 # VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM=0 NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0 NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0 # VLLM_ENABLE_K3_LATENT_MOE_TAIL_FUSION=0 # Add --enforce-eager for the known-good control run.

Single request, greedy, no concurrency:

from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI(base_url="<http://localhost:8000/v1>", api_key="dummy", timeout=600.0) resp = client.chat.completions.create( model="moonshotai/Kimi-K3", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "can you write me a story about a cat"}], max_tokens=64, temperature=0, extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"thinking": False}}, ) print(resp.choices[0].message.content)

With --enforce-eager this returns a coherent story on every run. Without it, the first response is already corrupted. Send the same request 3+ times to reach the segfault under the default cudagraph mode.

signals.title: [Feature] Allow random dataset to use --dataset-path for realistic token sampling
signals.text: ## Motivation When benchmarking speculative decoding, the acceptance rate of draft tokens depends heavily on the token distribution of the input. Currently, the `random` dataset in `vllm bench serve` generates purely random token IDs, which do not represent real-world text distributions. This can understate the effectiveness of speculative decoding in production. On the other hand, the `sharegpt` dataset uses real conversation prompts but does not support `--input-len` to control input length, making it impossible to run benchmarks with a fixed input length using real text. SGLang's benchmark tool already supports this via `--dataset-name random --dataset-path <sharegpt.json> --random-input-len 8192`, which samples tokens from ShareGPT and truncates/repeats them to the requested length. ## Proposal Allow `--dataset-name random` to accept `--dataset-path`. When provided, the random dataset samples token IDs from the file and truncates/repeats them to fill `--random-input-len`. File format is auto-detected from the extension: - `.json` → ShareGPT format (conversations array) - `.jsonl` → one JSON object per line with a "prompt" field - `.txt` → plain text, one line per entry No new CLI arguments are needed. When `--dataset-path` is not provided, the random dataset behaves exactly as before (purely random token IDs). ### Usage ```bash vllm bench serve \ --dataset-name random \ --dataset-path /data/ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json \ --random-input-len 8192 \ --random-output-len 1024 \ --max-concurrency 32 \ --num-prompts 32 ``` ### Why not use existing options? - `--dataset-name random`: supports fixed length but uses purely random tokens, not realistic for speculative decoding benchmarks - `--dataset-name sharegpt`: uses real text but doesn't support `--input-len` - `--dataset-name custom`: requires pre-processing ShareGPT into a JSONL file with truncated/padded prompts, which is inconvenient - `--dataset-name sonnet`: requires a chat template, not compatible with all tokenizers (e.g. DeepSeek-V4)

signals.title: [Bug]: ModelOpt NVFP4 on SM120 dies or wedges under sustained load with CUDA graphs (not the NVFP4 GEMM backend)
signals.text: ### Your current environment <details> <summary>Environment</summary> - GPU: 2x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition (sm120, 96 GB), driver 595.71.05, ECC clean - Container: `vllm/vllm-openai` v0.26.0 (`sha256:ffb2d59b1c059a5bd8d781320c9f5189de8293693b7d95da54befddaa54abf52`) and v0.27.1 (`sha256:0a51ea5b4ae2dc5d81890e5173f54203d2a3ae0cfffe51b8fd2afd4391bfd967`), podman, `--ipc host` - CUDA 13.0.2, torch 2.11.0+cu130, flashinfer 0.6.14 - Model: Qwen3.8-27B quantized by ModelOpt 0.47.0.dev0 to `MIXED_PRECISION`. 193 layers NVFP4 (all 64 `mlp.{gate,up,down}_proj` plus `lm_head`), 208 layers FP8 (`linear_attn.*`, `self_attn.*`), `kv_cache_quant_algo: FP8`. Architecture `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` (hybrid GDN linear attention with full attention every 4th layer), hidden 5120, ffn 17408, vocab 248320, 64 layers. - vLLM resolves this to `quantization=modelopt_mixed` and selects `FlashInferCutlassNvFp4LinearKernel` for the NVFP4 GEMMs, `FlashInferFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` for FP8, and the `FLASHINFER` attention backend. </details> ### 🐛 Describe the bug Serving a ModelOpt-NVFP4 checkpoint on SM120 dies under sustained batch load, reliably, on two vLLM releases. The same base model quantized to FP8 and served from the same image with the same attention backend is stable. The failure is specific to the NVFP4 build. I have not isolated the mechanism, and two backends I suspected are now ruled out by measurement (see the update comment below). **One thing that is measured but is not the cause.** `flashinfer.mm_fp4` hands the CUTLASS FP4 GEMM a fixed 32 MiB shared workspace, and on SM120 the kernel asks for 34 MiB at every M from 1 to 256 for this model's fused gate/up projection (5120 → 34816). Every decode-sized call therefore takes a fallback branch in `csrc/fp4_gemm_cutlass_sm120.cu` that allocates a private workspace and releases it right after an asynchronous launch, including inside CUDA graph capture. That is filed as https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4549 with a fix in https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4550. Raising the shared workspace so the fallback never fires does **not** stop the crash: the patched build failed after 15.0 minutes against 16.5 for the unpatched one. Recording it here so nobody else spends the window I spent on it. **Symptoms, for searchability.** Two failure modes, both with CUDA graphs enabled: | vLLM | spec decode | time to failure | error | |---|---|---|---| | v0.26.0 | none | 16 min 35 s | illegal memory access | | v0.27.1 | none | 21 min 32 s | illegal memory access | | v0.26.0 | MTP, 3 tokens | not recorded | misaligned address | | v0.26.0 | none | 8 s, on a boot right after a prior fault | illegal memory access in `BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCache` | The exception always surfaces at an asynchronous synchronization point, so the reported frame is never the offending kernel: ``` File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 314, in get_output self.async_copy_ready_event.synchronize() torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered ``` The second mode is a wedge. The engine stops making progress without raising anything, `/v1/models` still returns 200 in about a millisecond, `/v1/chat/completions` never returns, and the GPU sits at 100% utilization. `py-spy` shows the engine thread blocked in a kernel launch that never returns, and the driver reports `Xid 8 ... GPU is probably locked` only much later. `dmesg` records MMU faults at wild addresses, `faulted @ 0x4_00000000` and `0xf_00001000`, both `FAULT_PDE`. **Differential.** The same base model quantized to FP8, same box, same image, same FlashInfer attention backend, CUDA graphs on, prefix caching on, `--max-model-len 262144`, logged 10,282 completions across 35 hours with no illegal-address or misaligned-address error. The NVFP4 build dies after roughly 570 completions. Both GPUs produce the NVFP4 fault and ECC is clean on both. `--enforce-eager` reduces the rate roughly tenfold without eliminating it. We also swept the NVFP4 GEMM for memory-safety problems and found none: every layer shape in the model, every M from 1 to 8192, all 32 SM120 CUTLASS FP4 tactics, under `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck` with `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1`, with both a zeroed and a randomly poisoned workspace. Those runs cannot catch this defect, because disabling the caching allocator turns every free into a synchronizing `cudaFree`. ### Workarounds available today from vLLM Either of these avoids the fallback path without a FlashInfer patch: 1. `VLLM_DISABLED_KERNELS=FlashInferCutlassNvFp4LinearKernel`, which falls through to vLLM's native `CutlassNvFp4LinearKernel`. On our workload that reached 0.65 completions per second against 0.67 for the FlashInfer kernel, and 50 deterministic classification prompts returned byte-identical answers, so the swap does not change results. Soak results below. 2. `--enforce-eager`, which reduces the failure rate roughly tenfold without removing it, and costs more than the kernel swap. Swapping to `CutlassNvFp4LinearKernel` does not fix the failure, so quarantining the FlashInfer kernel on SM12x would not be a fix either. Both workarounds above are partial.

NVIDIA_BUILD_ID=74957750 CUDA_DRIVER_VERSION=545.23.08 PYTORCH_BUILD_VERSION=2.2.0a0+6a974be CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=LAZY NVIDIA_REQUIRE_JETPACK_HOST_MOUNTS= NVIDIA_PYTORCH_VERSION=23.11 TORCH_ALLOW_TF32_CUBLAS_OVERRIDE=1 PYTORCH_NVML_BASED_CUDA_CHECK=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/torchinductor_nsml ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Summary For Python-only builds, vLLM resolves a precompiled-wheel variant before fetching wheel metadata. The [Python-only build documentation](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/getting_started/installation/gpu/) documents `VLLM_PRECOMPILED_WHEEL_VARIANT` as selecting a variant subdirectory such as `cu129` or `cu130`. If it is not set, the CUDA variant is auto-detected from the local environment using PyTorch or `nvidia-smi`. The [nightly wheel documentation](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/contributing/ci/nightly_builds/) describes the root index as the default variant and named subdirectories as variant-specific indices. If metadata for the selected variant cannot be fetched, [`precompiled_wheel_utils.determine_wheel_url()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/836aac92ffdaa337083934181cb6d00b64b2a1a6/setup.py) currently retries the root/default metadata: ```python try: wheels, repo_url = precompiled_wheel_utils.fetch_metadata_for_variant( commit, variant ) except Exception as e: logger.warning( "Failed to fetch precompiled wheel metadata for variant %s: %s", variant, e, ) try_default = True if try_default: print("Trying the default variant from remote") wheels, repo_url = precompiled_wheel_utils.fetch_metadata_for_variant( commit, None ) ``` The fallback is part of the current resolution order. The issue is that once it happens, the CUDA variant selected explicitly or detected from the local environment is no longer used to qualify the fallback wheel. The wheel filtering that follows checks the package name and target architecture: ```python if wheel.get("package_name") == "vllm" and arch in wheel.get( "platform_tag", "" ): ... ``` but does not check that the root/default artifact matches the CUDA variant selected earlier. I encountered a concrete case where PyTorch CUDA 12.9 selected `cu129`, the `cu129` metadata lookup failed, and the fallback selected a native artifact requiring CUDA 13. I propose keeping the selected CUDA variant for the rest of precompiled-wheel resolution: if its metadata cannot be fetched, propagate that lookup failure instead of retrying the root/default variant. ### Concrete reproduction I encountered this while reproducing a separate issue from the exact v0.27.1 source: ```text source: v0.27.1 6e448d0ea9bf3d88d898b65449ca6dc2aec170ac PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu129 torch.version.cuda: 12.9 ``` Using the documented Python-only precompiled installation path: ```bash VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto ``` with neither `VLLM_PRECOMPILED_WHEEL_VARIANT` nor `VLLM_PRECOMPILED_WHEEL_COMMIT` set, the CUDA detection path selected: ```text cu129 ``` The Python-only build selected the following precompiled base commit: ```text f5bb701fa270f5c801f1572e1478b56f292d8dfc ``` For that commit, metadata for `cu129` was unavailable: ```text https://wheels.vllm.ai/f5bb701fa270f5c801f1572e1478b56f292d8dfc/cu129/vllm/metadata.json -> 404 ``` The fallback then queried the root/default metadata: ```text https://wheels.vllm.ai/f5bb701fa270f5c801f1572e1478b56f292d8dfc/vllm/metadata.json -> 200 ``` The resulting path was: ```text PyTorch CUDA 12.9 -> select cu129 -> cu129 metadata unavailable -> retry root/default metadata -> select default wheel ``` ### Artifact verification I extracted `vllm/_C_stable_libtorch.abi3.so` from the wheel selected through the root/default fallback and inspected its ELF dependencies. The fallback artifact requires: ```text NEEDED: libcudart.so.13 ``` As a control, the published `cu129` artifact for the exact v0.27.1 commit is available at: ```text https://wheels.vllm.ai/6e448d0ea9bf3d88d898b65449ca6dc2aec170ac/cu129/vllm/metadata.json -> 200 ``` Its `_C_stable_libtorch.abi3.so` requires: ```text NEEDED: libcudart.so.12 ``` So in this reproduction, the resolver first selected `cu129`, then replaced that selection after the metadata failure with a root/default artifact requiring `libcudart.so.13`. The exact-v0.27.1 `cu129` artifact is only used here as a control for the native CUDA dependency of a published `cu129` wheel. I am not proposing any change to the existing base-commit selection behavior. The problematic transition happens after the base commit and CUDA variant have already been selected. ### Why the default fallback is unsafe The [nightly wheel documentation](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/contributing/ci/nightly_builds/) treats the root index as the default variant and named subdirectories as separate variants. It also notes that the default variant can have a named alias, and that not every variant is present on every commit. A missing `cu129` index therefore does not imply that the root/default wheel is an equivalent `cu129` replacement. The current fallback nevertheless changes: ```text selected: cu129 | | metadata lookup fails v fallback: root/default | | package + architecture filtering v selected wheel ``` There is no CUDA-variant check between the selected variant and the fallback artifact. This affects explicit selection as well as auto-detection. For example, a user setting: ```text VLLM_PRECOMPILED_WHEEL_VARIANT=cu129 ``` can currently receive the default variant if the `cu129` metadata lookup fails. The root/default CUDA variant also cannot be inferred safely from the current `VLLM_MAIN_CUDA_VERSION`. `VLLM_PRECOMPILED_WHEEL_COMMIT` can select a different or historical wheel commit, and the normal Python-only path can select a base commit from `main`. The default artifact for that commit may therefore reflect a different CUDA build configuration from the one selected in the current environment. With the current metadata and wheel filtering, there is no check that makes the root/default wheel a verified replacement for an already selected CUDA variant. ### Proposed fix For CUDA, once a variant has been selected, fetch metadata only for that variant. If: ```python fetch_metadata_for_variant(commit, variant) ``` fails, propagate that error instead of retrying: ```python fetch_metadata_for_variant(commit, None) ``` The behavior changes from: ```text current: select cu129 -> fetch cu129 metadata -> lookup fails -> fetch root/default metadata -> select by package name / architecture ``` to: ```text proposed: select cu129 -> fetch cu129 metadata -> lookup fails -> propagate the original lookup failure ``` A fallback could be kept if the resolver had enough information to verify that the default artifact is compatible with the selected CUDA variant. That check does not exist in the current resolution path, so doing that safely would require a broader metadata or compatibility-selection change. The proposed patch instead keeps the existing variant selection intact and fails at the variant-specific lookup when that artifact is unavailable. A root/default wheel may happen to be compatible in some cases, but the current resolver cannot distinguish those cases from the incompatible case reproduced above. The existing base-commit selection is unchanged, and the ROCm precompiled-wheel path is unchanged. Regression coverage checks both CUDA selection paths: - explicit `VLLM_PRECOMPILED_WHEEL_VARIANT`; - auto-detected CUDA variant. In both cases, a failed selected-variant lookup should propagate its original error without calling `fetch_metadata_for_variant(commit, None)`. ### Current `main` The same fallback is still present on `main` at [`836aac92ffdaa337083934181cb6d00b64b2a1a6`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/836aac92ffdaa337083934181cb6d00b64b2a1a6). I also reproduced the path independently of the current contents of `wheels.vllm.ai` with a metadata-fetch stub: ```text fetch(commit, "cu129") -> raises fetch(commit, None) -> returns default metadata ``` On the unmodified code, both explicit and auto-detected `cu129` make both calls and return the default wheel. The regression test for the proposed behavior expects the first lookup error to propagate instead. ### Context / related work The variant-specific lookup followed by the default fallback was introduced in #29838. #32948 later added CUDA variant auto-detection while retaining that fallback. Related reports cover different paths: - #42338 reports a similar CUDA 12.9 -> CUDA 13 result through package resolver/index selection. This issue concerns the Python-only precompiled-wheel fallback after a CUDA variant has already been selected. - #49683 concerns availability of `cu129` nightly artifacts. Missing variant-specific metadata can trigger the fallback described here, but artifact availability itself is a separate problem. - PR #34139 discussed native compatibility concerns when falling back across different nightly commits. Here the wheel commit stays fixed while the selected CUDA variant is replaced by that commit's default variant. I have a patch implementing the proposed behavior with regression coverage for both explicit and auto-detected CUDA variants, and will open a draft PR shortly. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug]: Qwen3.6-27B (dense Gated-DeltaNet) permanently hard-wedges the V1 engine — two reproducible modes (2 large images; long multi-turn text), possibly related
signals.text:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64), glibc 2.35 Python: 3.12.13 | platform Linux-6.17.0-1026-nvidia-x86_64 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 (CUDA build 13.0) vLLM Version: 0.23.0 CUDA available: True | CUDA runtime 13.0.88 | driver 595.71.05 GPU: 8× NVIDIA B200 [pip3] flashinfer-python==0.6.12 [pip3] transformers==5.12.0 [pip3] triton==3.6.0 env: VLLM_USAGE_SOURCE=production-docker-image, VLLM_ENABLE_CUDA_COMPATIBILITY=0, TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=7.5 8.0 8.6 8.9 9.0 10.0 12.0+PTX ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary vLLM **0.23.0**, **Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B** (dense FullAttn + Gated-DeltaNet), single GPU TP=1, `--attention-config TRITON_ATTN`, `--max-model-len 262144`, `--enable-prefix-caching`, `mamba_cache_mode=align`. The engine **permanently hard-wedges** (generation stops, `/health` still 200, only restart recovers) in two reproducible cases: - **Mode A** — a request with **two large images** → **fixed** by raising `--max-num-batched-tokens` 8192→32768. - **Mode B** — concurrent **long multi-turn (~180k-token) prefills** → **not** fixed by `--max-num-batched-tokens`. Reported together because both wedge the same GDN model and **we can't tell if it's one bug or two** (stacks and fix-behavior differ). Related to #40707 / #47738 (both env 0.18–0.23). ## Mode A — 2 large images (scheduler-admission wedge) Each request has **two distinct 3024×4032 images** (11,844 vision tokens each). At `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192` it wedges on the first batch: `running=1, waiting=11`, gen frozen, KV≈0.9%. py-spy MainThread is **idle in the scheduler** (`_process_engine_step`), admitting none. Single-variable bisection: **8192 → WEDGE, 32768 → CLEAN** (65 completed); `--max-num-seqs` 64/384 and `--mm-processor-cache-gb` 256/0 make no difference (still WEDGE). > **Our workaround (works for us):** setting **`--max-num-batched-tokens 32768`** eliminates Mode A entirely — the multimodal load that reliably wedged at 8192 runs clean at 32768. We are running with this as our interim fix. (It does NOT help Mode B.) Mechanism (arithmetic exact; causation inferred): `encoder_cache_size = max(max_num_batched_tokens, max_tokens_per_mm_item=16384)`. At 8192 → 16384 holds one 11,844-token image but not two (23,688); at 32768 → holds two. Matches #40707's precondition (item 1 pinned, item 2 can't load, gap < block_size 16 → `_mamba_block_aligned_split` truncates to 0 → request skipped). Consistent with #40707, though no mamba frame appears in the stack. ## Mode B — long multi-turn text ~180k-token prefill (GDN-forward wedge) Each request is one distinct ~180k-token multi-turn conversation, no images. Wedges after ~4 completions at **both** batched 8192 and 32768: `running=1–2, waiting=10–11`, gen+prompt frozen, KV≈0.1%, ≥5 requests hit the 1200 s timeout. py-spy MainThread is **active inside the model forward** — batched-32768 run unambiguously in the GDN kernel `qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py:1532 chunk_gated_delta_rule → qwen3_5.forward → cuda_graph → execute_model`; batched-8192 run in a compiled Triton launch of the same forward. Not the scheduler. Trigger: a large **one-shot prefill** hitting the GDN chunked-prefill path — in production this is the full re-prefill after the prefix cache for a long conversation is evicted; the synthetic reproduces that single long prefill directly. (Caveat: the two dumps 3 s apart hit different compiled submodules, so the forward is grinding but never returns within 1200 s — a genuine client-side wedge, but these dumps can't fully separate an infinite hang from a pathologically-slow non-returning forward.) ## Same bug? Unknown. Both involve the GDN/mamba hybrid path, so a shared cause is plausible, but the evidence differs: Mode A = idle in scheduler, fixed by `--max-num-batched-tokens`; Mode B = active in the GDN forward, not fixed. Flagging both for maintainers who know the GDN internals; not asserting either way. ## Relation - **#40707** (OPEN) — matches Mode A; here on dense 27B / TP=1. Fix **#40709 unmerged** (not in any release through v0.27.1). - **#47738** (CLOSED, Qwen3.6-27B two images) — referenced fix **#47771 closed unmerged**. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bugfix] Auto-configure TRITON_PTXAS_PATH for new GPU architectures
signals.text: ## Summary Triton bundles a ptxas binary from CUDA 12.8 that does not support GPU architectures sm_110a (Jetson Thor) or sm_121a (DGX Spark GB10). This causes Triton kernel compilation to fail with: ``` ptxas fatal: Value 'sm_121a' is not defined for option 'gpu-name' ``` This PR adds automatic detection of new GPU architectures and configures TRITON_PTXAS_PATH to use the system CUDA toolkit's ptxas when needed. ## Changes - Add `_configure_triton_ptxas_for_new_gpus()` function to `vllm/triton_utils/importing.py` - Uses Triton's native backend detection (`triton.backends.backends`) to get GPU architecture - Sets TRITON_PTXAS_PATH for GPUs with arch >= 110 (compute capability 11.0+) - Respects user-configured TRITON_PTXAS_PATH if already set - Fails gracefully if detection is unavailable - Add unit tests for the new functionality ## Testing Tested on NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark) with: - CUDA 13.0 (V13.0.88) - Triton 3.5.1 - PyTorch 2.9.1+cu130 Verified that: - Triton kernels compile and execute successfully with the fix - Triton kernels fail without the fix (expected ptxas error) ## Related Issues Fixes #31269 Fixes #32093 Related to #29469

signals.title: [GLM-5] Fix loading of appended NextN/MTP draft layers
signals.text: Tracked in #37113. This PR fixes model-side loading for the appended GLM NextN/MTP draft layers used by GLM NVFP4 checkpoints. ## Problem GLM checkpoints with appended NextN/MTP layers do not load those draft layers through the same path as the base model layers. The appended layers have their own draft-layer layout and must be mapped as draft layers, not as normal decoder layers. If those layers are silently skipped or loaded through the wrong path, speculative decoding can start from an invalid draft model state. ## What This PR Changes - Loads appended NextN/MTP draft layers through the correct draft-layer mapping. - Preserves the expected internal layer id and `is_nextn` behavior for those layers. - Validates that the appended draft layers were actually loaded. ## Scope - Model-side GLM NextN/MTP loading only. - No MTP runtime metadata reuse. - No DCP/MLA runtime changes. - No distributed/custom-allreduce changes. - No SM120 B12X backend-selection changes.

signals.title: [Bugfix] Raise ImportError early when xxhash is unavailable for prefix caching
signals.text: ## Summary Fixes #39785 (originally #39338). When `prefix_caching_hash_algo` is set to `"xxhash"` or `"xxhash_cbor"` but the `xxhash` package is not installed, `LLM.generate()` silently returns empty outputs for requests that trigger prefix caching — no exception is raised. **Root cause:** The `ModuleNotFoundError` in `vllm/utils/hashing.py` is raised at hash-computation time during request preprocessing, where it gets caught as a preprocessing failure and silently converted to an empty output. **Fix:** Validate xxhash availability in `CacheConfig.__post_init__` so the error surfaces immediately at engine construction time, consistent with how other optional-dependency configs (e.g. mamba stochastic rounding) are validated. Uses `ModuleNotFoundError` with `e.name == "xxhash"` check to avoid masking broken/outdated installations that raise different `ImportError` subclasses. ## Changes - `vllm/config/cache.py`: Add xxhash import check in `__post_init__` (+13 LOC) - `tests/v1/engine/test_xxhash_validation.py`: Parametrized test that mocks xxhash absence and verifies `ImportError` is raised (+25 LOC) ## Test plan - [x] New unit test: `test_xxhash_missing_raises_import_error` (parametrized for both `xxhash` and `xxhash_cbor`) - [ ] Verify manually: `pip uninstall xxhash && python -c "from vllm.config.cache import CacheConfig; CacheConfig(prefix_caching_hash_algo='xxhash')"` → `ImportError`

signals.title: [BugFix][ROCM] Align the block size of rocm_attn kernel in hybrid attention arch.
signals.text: ## [BugFix][ROCm] Fix block size alignment for hybrid (Mamba+Attention) models to prevent NaN corruption under FULL CUDAGraph ### Summary Hybrid models (Mamba + Self-Attention) on ROCm with FULL CUDAGraph mode can produce **non-deterministic garbage output** due to a block size misalignment in the Triton paged attention decode kernel. This PR fixes it by ensuring the kernel block alignment is `MultipleOf(32)` (instead of `MultipleOf(16)`) for hybrid models, so that `PHYSICAL_BLOCK_SIZE` is always evenly divisible by `TRITON_BLOCK_SIZE`. ### Bug Description **Symptoms:** - Hybrid model (e.g. Mamba-like architecture, Qwen35、Qwen3Next) with `PP=1, TP=8` on ROCm, FULL CUDAGraph enabled (resulting block_size like 528/784, which is multiple of 16, not 32) - Output degrades into garbage/repetitive tokens **non-deterministically** — the same input may succeed or fail across runs - Forcing `--block-size 1056` (a multiple of 32) eliminates the issue entirely - `PP=2, TP=4` is unaffected because it naturally computes `block_size=1056` ### Root Cause Chain The failure results from a 5-step causal chain: #### Step 1: CUDAGraph capture writes NaN into KV cache blocks During CUDAGraph warmup and capture, [`_warmup_and_capture`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py) calls `_dummy_run` with **dummy inputs** (e.g. `seq_lens=1`). For hybrid models, the Mamba/SSM layers receive meaningless hidden states, which can produce NaN values. These NaN values flow through K/V projections and get written into the KV cache blocks allocated for the dummy run. (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/35219, fp32 ssm block polluted bf16 attention block) #### Step 2: NaN blocks are NOT zeroed after capture After CUDAGraph capture, [`_zero_block_ids`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py) only zeros blocks listed in `scheduler_output.new_block_ids_to_zero` (i.e., freshly allocated blocks for real requests). **The blocks written during capture remain polluted with NaN.** #### Step 3: Block size misalignment creates cross-boundary Triton tiles For `TP=8`, [`_update_mamba_hybrid_block_size`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/platforms/interface.py) computes `block_size = 528` (= 16 × 33). The Triton decode kernel [`kernel_paged_attention_2d`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/attention/ops/chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py) uses a hardcoded [`TRITON_BLOCK_SIZE = 32`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/attention/ops/chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py) for non-power-of-2 block sizes. Since **528 % 32 = 16 ≠ 0**, some Triton tiles span across two physical blocks: ``` Physical Block N: tokens [512 ... 527] (last 16 tokens) Physical Block N+1: tokens [0 ... 15] (first 16 tokens) ↑ Triton tile j=16 reads BOTH blocks ``` #### Step 4: Out-of-bounds block_table read hits NaN-polluted block For the cross-boundary tile, the kernel computes [`l_block_idx`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/attention/ops/chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py) as a mix of `[N, N, ..., N, N+1, N+1, ..., N+1]`, and loads [`p_block_idx = tl.load(block_tables_ptr + ... + l_block_idx)`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/attention/ops/chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py). When the sequence hasn't actually filled Block N+1, `block_table[N+1]` contains a stale entry (typically `NULL_BLOCK_ID = 0`) pointing to **physical block 0** — which was written with NaN during CUDAGraph capture. #### Step 5: `0 × NaN = NaN` — IEEE 754 kills the softmax masking The kernel correctly applies a [seq_mask](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/attention/ops/chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py) to the QK scores (setting out-of-range positions to `-inf`), which produces `p = 0` after softmax for those positions. However, the V values loaded from the NaN block are **not masked**. The final [accumulation `acc += tl.dot(p, V)`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/attention/ops/chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py) computes `0 × NaN = NaN` (per IEEE 754), **not zero**. This NaN propagates into the attention output, then into Mamba's in-place `ssm_state` update, permanently corrupting all subsequent decode steps. ### Why Non-Deterministic? - The block allocator assigns physical blocks non-deterministically → whether the NaN-polluted block from capture coincides with the stale `block_table` entry varies across runs - Whether the model's dummy-run actually produces NaN (vs. large-but-finite values) depends on uninitialized memory state ### Fix In [`RocmAttentionBackend.get_supported_kernel_block_sizes`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/attention/backends/rocm_attn.py), return `MultipleOf(32)` instead of `MultipleOf(16)` when the model is hybrid: ```python from vllm.config import get_current_vllm_config_or_none config = get_current_vllm_config_or_none() if config is not None and config.model_config.is_hybrid: return [MultipleOf(32)] return [MultipleOf(16)] ``` This causes [`_update_mamba_hybrid_block_size`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/platforms/interface.py) to compute `kernel_block_alignment_size = 32`, which changes the block size from `528` (16 × 33) to `544` (32 × 17). Since **544 % 32 = 0**, every Triton tile stays within a single physical block — **no cross-boundary reads, no stale block_table access, no NaN corruption**. | Config | Before | After | |--------|--------|-------| | TP=8 | block_size=528, 528%32=16 ✗ | block_size=544, 544%32=0 ✓ | | TP=4 | block_size=1056, 1056%32=0 ✓ | unchanged ✓ | | Non-hybrid models | MultipleOf(16) | unchanged ✓ | ## Purpose ## Test Plan ## Test Result --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. - [ ] (Optional) Release notes update. signals.title: feat: support passing configuration to custom attention backends
signals.text: ## What's broken? Custom attention backends registered via `register_backend()` have no way to receive configuration. The `vllm.general_plugins` entry points are zero-argument callables, and `AttentionImpl.__init__` has a fixed constructor signature — there is no sanctioned injection point for plugin authors to pass config to their custom backends. Workarounds like class-level attributes are fragile and not discoverable. Ref: #40051 ## Who is affected? Anyone building custom attention backends (e.g. observability tools like [glassbox](https://github.com/dmaniloff/glassbox)) that need runtime configuration. Existing built-in backends and users not passing `backend_config` are **not affected** — this is fully backward-compatible. ## How did we fix it? Added a `backend_config: Any = None` parameter to `register_backend()` in `vllm/v1/attention/backends/registry.py`. The value is stored in new module-level dicts (`_ATTN_BACKEND_CONFIGS` / `_MAMBA_ATTN_BACKEND_CONFIGS`) alongside the existing `_ATTN_OVERRIDES`. **New public API surface:** - `register_backend(..., backend_config={"key": "value"})` — store config at registration time - `backend.get_config()` — enum method to retrieve config (returns `None` if not set) - `backend.clear_config()` — enum method to clear stored config - `get_backend_config(backend)` — module-level function (equivalent to `backend.get_config()`) **Usage example:** ```python # In your plugin's entry point: from vllm.v1.attention.backends.registry import ( AttentionBackendEnum, register_backend ) register_backend( AttentionBackendEnum.CUSTOM, "my.module.MyObservabilityBackend", backend_config={"log_level": "debug", "sample_rate": 0.1}, ) # In your backend class: from vllm.v1.attention.backends.registry import get_backend_config, AttentionBackendEnum class MyObservabilityBackend(AttentionBackend): def __init__(self, ...): config = get_backend_config(AttentionBackendEnum.CUSTOM) # config == {"log_level": "debug", "sample_rate": 0.1} ``` **Design choices:** - Pull-based pattern (backend reads config at init time) — matches how `_ATTN_OVERRIDES` already works - No changes to `AttentionImpl.__init__` signature — zero disruption to existing backends - Config is set per-process when the plugin loads — matches subprocess behavior documented in plugin docs - Works with both decorator and direct-registration forms of `register_backend()` ## How do we know it works? - 5 new unit tests added to `tests/test_attention_backend_registry.py`: - `test_register_backend_config_with_class_path` — config via direct registration - `test_register_backend_config_with_decorator` — config via `@register_backend` decorator - `test_register_mamba_backend_config` — config for `MambaAttentionBackendEnum` - `test_backend_config_defaults_to_none` — backward compat: no config = `None` - `test_backend_config_clear` — `clear_config()` removes stored config - All existing tests continue to pass unchanged - `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass ## Changes - `vllm/v1/attention/backends/registry.py`: Added `backend_config` param, config storage dicts, `get_config()`/`clear_config()` enum methods, `get_backend_config()` function - `tests/test_attention_backend_registry.py`: 5 new tests covering the config mechanism

signals.title: [Bugfix] Clamp NVFP4 MoE activation scales to prevent NaN from dead experts
signals.text: ## Summary Some NVFP4 checkpoints (e.g. `txn545/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-NVFP4`) have near-zero or denormal `float32` activation scales for dead MoE experts. In `make_nvfp4_moe_quant_config()`, these are inverted directly (`1.0 / a13_scale`, `1.0 / a2_scale`), producing `Inf`, which the FP4 quantization kernel propagates as `NaN` — corrupting the entire output batch. Fix: clamp both activation global scales from below at `torch.finfo(torch.float32).tiny` (~1.18e-38) before inversion. Dead experts contribute zero-weighted outputs regardless of their scale value, so this clamp is numerically safe. - This is not a duplicate of #31740 (which covers SM12.1 platform support); that PR does not touch `oracle/nvfp4.py`. ## Test plan - Loaded `txn545/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-NVFP4` on DGX Spark (SM12.1, CUDA 13.1) with vLLM v0.20.2 + this patch - Ran multi-turn chat completions — no NaN/Inf in outputs - Without the patch, outputs contain NaN tokens when dead experts are routed > AI assistance was used to help identify and describe this fix.

signals.title: fix(v1): enforce VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION in run_method
signals.text: Enforcement of the `VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION` flag was missing in the `run_method` function within the V1 engine's serialization utilities. While other parts of the codebase correctly check this environment variable before attempting to deserialize data using `pickle` or `cloudpickle`, `run_method` was performing an unconditional `cloudpickle.loads` when receiving bytes as the method argument. Consistent security posture across the V1 engine is achieved by adding this check. This ensures that users who explicitly disable insecure serialization by setting `VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=0` (the default) are protected from potential arbitrary code execution via serialized method bytes. ## Purpose Fix an inconsistency in security policy enforcement where `run_method` could bypass the `VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=0` setting. ## Test Plan Verification was performed by locally testing the `run_method` function with the environment variable set to `0`. A `RuntimeError` is now correctly raised when attempting to pass serialized bytes, matching the behavior of other serialization-related functions in the project. ## Test Result The logic was verified to raise the expected exception when insecure serialization is disabled, preventing the unintended execution of cloudpickle payloads.

signals.title: Release stale CUDA primary contexts inherited by forked workers
signals.text: ## Summary - Release inherited CUDA primary contexts for non-assigned devices in forked worker processes - When using fork multiprocessing (Linux default), child workers inherit the parent's GPU 0 context even when assigned to GPU 1+ - These stale contexts waste GPU memory and cause NVIDIA `cuda-checkpoint` restore failures ("invalid argument") - Add `_release_stale_cuda_primary_contexts()` that calls `cuDevicePrimaryCtxRelease()` via ctypes after device setup in `Worker.init_device()` Fixes #42873 ## Context Discovered while integrating NVIDIA cuda-checkpoint with vLLM for multi-GPU cold start optimization (related to RFC #34303). The stale inherited contexts cause `cuda-checkpoint --action restore` to fail because it tries to restore both the inherited GPU 0 context and the worker's actual GPU 1 context in the same process. ## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR Searched open PRs and issues - no existing fix for this. The existing `_maybe_force_spawn()` in `system_utils.py` forces spawn when CUDA is already initialized, but doesn't handle the case where fork is used intentionally or where contexts are inherited through other mechanisms. ## AI assistance disclosure AI assistance was used for code review and drafting. All changes reviewed and validated by the submitter. ## Test plan - [ ] `tests/cuda/test_stale_context_release.py` - verifies stale contexts are released while preserving the assigned device's context (requires 2+ GPUs) - [ ] Manually verified with cuda-checkpoint on H100 tp=2: checkpoint/restore cycle passes after fix, fails without it - [ ] Single-GPU systems: function is a no-op (no contexts to release) Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
