signal.title: [Metrics] Report shared-prefix tokens lost to a missing sparse-retention checkpoint
signal.text: ## Purpose For hybrid models running `mamba_cache_mode="align"`, the Mamba group retains only a sparse set of state checkpoints. When none of them lands inside a shared prefix, `HybridKVCacheCoordinator` intersects the per-group hits and the attention groups' matches are discarded. Prefix caching then reports a clean miss, which is indistinguishable from "these requests simply don't share a prefix" — there is no signal that reuse was found and then thrown away. The coordinator already computes the size of that loss (`num_uncached_common_prefix_tokens`) in order to pin the Marconi shared-prefix junction, and then drops it. This PR records it in the prefix cache stats and exports it as `vllm:prefix_cache_sparse_retention_misses`. This is observability only. Scheduling, allocation, lookup, and model output are unchanged. Relates to #45238. ### Why this matters more now - #50991 enabled Mamba prefix caching by default. - #52216 promotes `prefix_cache_retention_interval` to an argument and defaults it to `0`, i.e. sparser retention by default. Both increase how often a lookup can lose a match this way, and neither makes the loss visible. There is also a concrete remedy once the signal exists. `--prefix-match-unit` enables fine-grained partial Mamba hits, but its default is the GCD of the group block sizes; in align mode the attention block size is set equal to the Mamba block size, so the default GCD equals `block_size`, the `mamba.block_size > hash_block_size` gate in `enable_partial_hash_hits` is false, and the mechanism is inert unless an operator explicitly sets the flag. Measured on this branch with a 2-group align hybrid at `block_size=544`: | config | `hash_block_size` | partial Mamba hits | |---|---|---| | default (`prefix_match_unit=None`) | 544 | disabled | | `--prefix-match-unit 136` | 136 | enabled | So today an operator has the knob but no indication they need it. This counter is what tells them. ## Why this is not a duplicate - No open PR references #45238, and none exposes this quantity. Checked with `gh pr list --search "45238 in:body"`, plus keyword sweeps over `mamba prefix cache`, `mamba cache mode align`, `VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL`, and `prefix cache metric observability`. - #52216 and #50551 / #49574 change **which** checkpoints are retained. This reports the cost when none is reachable, so they compose rather than compete — as #52216 makes retention sparser by default, this signal becomes more useful, not redundant. - #51807 adds coverage for prefix-cache metric accounting under same-step Mamba deferral (that each request is counted once). It does not surface vetoed hits. - #47491 attempted to *fix* the veto by letting attention hits survive a Mamba miss and was closed as a correctness hazard (`has_initial_states` is derived from the scalar `num_computed_tokens`, so the resume boundary would have no valid state). This PR deliberately does not change hit semantics — it only reports the loss. ## Test plan ```bash uv venv --python 3.12 VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \ tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/ tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \ tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/metrics/stats.py vllm/v1/metrics/loggers.py \ vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \ tests/entrypoints/serve/instrumentator/test_metrics.py docs/design/metrics.md ``` ## Test result `348 passed, 1 failed`. The single failure is `test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders`, which fails identically on the unmodified base commit (`4d2a68d64`) — verified by checking out the base and running it in isolation. It is unrelated to this change. All `pre-commit` hooks pass, including `mypy`. Two unit tests are added to `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py`: one asserting the counter reports the lost tokens when an align-mode Mamba group holds no checkpoint at the shared-prefix junction, and one asserting it stays at zero on a hit every group agrees on. As a negative control, stubbing the computation to `0` makes the first test fail (expected 32, got 0), confirming it exercises the new path rather than passing vacuously. ### End to end `Qwen3.5-4B` (AWQ 4-bit), single GPU, `--enable-prefix-caching --enforce-eager`, `--max-model-len 8192`, concurrency 1, 32 prompts over 8 prefix groups. Engine selected `mamba_cache_mode="align"` and `block_size=528`, matching the geometry in #45238. Workloads are `vllm bench serve --dataset-name prefix_repetition`, differing only in where the 1584-token block boundary falls: | | 1600 / 600 (boundary inside shared prefix) | 1500 / 700 (boundary in unique tokens) | |---|---|---| | `prefix_cache_queries` | 70,400 | 70,400 | | `prefix_cache_hits` | 38,016 (54.0%) | 17,952 (25.5%) | | **`prefix_cache_sparse_retention_misses`** | **0** | **8,448** | | Mean TTFT | 245.95 ms | 300.25 ms | The counter stays at exactly zero on the healthy workload and reports 8,448 tokens (16 × 528, whole blocks) on the geometry-unlucky one, alongside a halved hit rate and a 22% TTFT regression that is otherwise unattributable. Note the unlucky case is 25.5%, not 0% — the Marconi admission policy (#37898) recovers most of it. The catastrophic case originally described in #45238 is genuinely fixed on current main; what remains is a real but silent residual loss, which is what this counter exposes. ## Model evaluation Not applicable. This PR adds a counter and does not touch scheduling, block allocation, cache lookup, or anything reaching the model, so it cannot affect output or accuracy. No eval was run for that reason. ## AI assistance This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude, Fable 5). The investigation, patch, and tests were AI-produced; I reviewed every changed line, ran the test commands above, and can defend the change end to end. cc @njhill (authored #47782, the Marconi retention pinning this reports against) and @tlrmchlsmth (#52216, which defaults retention to sparse).
signal.author: Sahil170595

signal.title: [Feature][DSpark]: Improve Adaptive DSpark Online Profiling
signal.text: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch The initial version does profiling at startup to estimate the verification step time by replaying the recorded CUDA graphs. This is known to have some drift, especially at higher batch sizes. Here are my results from initial study: We want to extend this to fully online profiling. However, there are some challenges that make this tricky: - Online profiling may lead to "dead spots": one-time latency spikes make a certain batch size appear unattractive, leading to the adaptive verifier to never select that batch size, which leads to negative feedback and stale data limiting our range of profiled values. Generally there is an "exploration vs exploitation" problem here, as well as a requirement for some way to detect and eliminate outliers (such as those caused by JIT compilation). - Variable sequence lengths make it hard to measure a single reliable estimate of execution time for a given number of tokens. In practice we will want some way to account for this: either tracking measured points in 2D (num_tokens, max_seq_len or mean_seq_len), or estimating the overhead added per-token of KV reads We should do a more comprehensive study on the drift across models, batch sizes, and sequence lengths. Then, we should design a fully-online solution that addresses the shortcomings, and evaluate the performance gain. We should also evaluate the "oracle" speedup with perfect timing prediction (retrospectively) to assess how much performance can be gained
signal.author: benchislett

signal.title: [Bugfix][Core] Fail requests the KV cache pool can never hold instead of retrying them forever
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52520. ### The symptom On a hybrid Mamba + full-attention model with `--mamba-cache-mode align`, a request whose length is near the KV pool ceiling is **accepted**, chunk-prefilled to ~99 % of the pool, descheduled when the last chunk cannot be allocated — and then never scheduled again. Zero output tokens, the whole prefill discarded, and the only observable is `vllm:num_requests_waiting_by_reason{reason="capacity"} = 1`, which is indistinguishable from a healthy server that is momentarily full. The HTTP request never returns. The engine boots happily into this state: `_check_enough_kv_cache_memory` passes. ### The mechanism Two bounds describe the same quantity — how many blocks one `max_model_len` request can hold at once — and they are computed by different code that does not agree. **Startup** sizes the pool from each spec's `max_memory_usage_bytes` (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:2189-2198`). For a hybrid Mamba model in align mode that is `cdiv(max_model_len, block_size)` blocks for the attention group plus `2 + num_speculative_blocks` for the Mamba group (`vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py:687-696`). It compares that against **all** the blocks the pool will have. But `BlockPool` permanently reserves one block as the null block (`vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py:188-191`), so only `num_blocks - 1` are ever available to a request. A pool built at exactly the startup minimum is one usable block short of one `max_model_len` request, and startup does not notice. **Runtime admission** (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py:475-491`, reached with `scheduler_reserve_full_isl` — default `True`) asks the coordinator for the same quantity, but through the per-step allocators. For the Mamba align group that path returns `1 + num_speculative_blocks` on a first prefill (`vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:1529-1540`), one block below the peak the spec itself states, because a later step allocates the next state block before `remove_skipped_blocks` retires the one from two steps ago. So admission asks for one block *less* than the pool is short by, and admits. The request then chunk-prefills until the final chunk needs the block that does not exist. It is the only running request, so it preempts itself (`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:676-688`): `num_computed_tokens` back to 0, all blocks freed, requeued. On the next step the same gate now also has to count the blocks the discarded prefill left in the prefix cache as evictable, so it refuses — and keeps refusing. The request is stuck, and the prefill is gone. Measured on unmodified `main` at `4d2a68d64d9e05921ed5c4099146e768a92d71d5`, CPU only, no model weights: hybrid full-attention + Mamba(align), `block_size=16`, `max_model_len=1024`, `num_speculative_blocks=3`, `max_num_batched_tokens=256`. The startup bound is `cdiv(1024,16)=64 + (2+3)=5 = 69` blocks, and `get_kv_cache_configs` accepts a 69-block pool: ```text pool of 69 blocks: startup check accepts=True (num_blocks=69) pool=69 blocks, free at start=68 (one block is BlockPool's null block) step 0 scheduled= 256 computed= 256 free= 48 status=RUNNING preemptions=0 step 1 scheduled= 256 computed= 512 free= 31 status=RUNNING preemptions=0 step 2 scheduled= 256 computed= 768 free= 15 status=RUNNING preemptions=0 step 3 scheduled= 240 computed= 1008 free= 0 status=RUNNING preemptions=0 step 4 scheduled= 0 computed= 0 free= 68 status=PREEMPTED preemptions=1 step 5 scheduled= 0 computed= 0 free= 68 status=PREEMPTED preemptions=1 ... 19 more identical steps ... VERDICT prompt=1023: finished=False computed=0 preemptions=1 status=PREEMPTED pool of 70 blocks: startup check accepts=True (num_blocks=70) step 3 scheduled= 240 computed= 1008 free= 1 status=RUNNING preemptions=0 step 4 scheduled= 15 computed= 1023 free= 0 status=RUNNING preemptions=0 VERDICT prompt=1023: finished=False computed=1023 preemptions=0 status=RUNNING ``` One block of headroom is the entire difference. Note that the prefill dies at exactly 1008 tokens, which is `(69 - 1 - 5) * 16` — the sequence length the pool can actually serve. ### The fix One function computes the bound, and it is the function the startup error message already uses: - `max_servable_num_tokens(vllm_config, kv_cache_groups, num_blocks)` in `kv_cache_utils.py` — the longest sequence a pool of `num_blocks` blocks can hold for one request. It is `_estimate_max_model_len_from_groups` (the helper behind "the estimated maximum model length" that `_check_enough_kv_cache_memory` prints) evaluated against `num_blocks - 1` blocks, i.e. against the capacity `BlockPool` will actually hand out. It returns `None` for group layouts that cannot be priced per block — exactly the layouts whose pool was not sized per block either — so it never invents a bound the startup check did not apply. - `Scheduler` evaluates it once at construction. When it is below `max_model_len` the configuration cannot serve its own window, which is logged at `ERROR` with the number the operator needs. A request past the bound can never be scheduled at any future time, however much drains, so `add_request` fails it immediately instead of queueing it: no prefill is spent, nothing is preempted, and the client gets a terminal response rather than a request that never returns. So there is one bound with two call sites, which is the point: `_estimate_max_model_len_from_groups` is called by the startup check (`kv_cache_utils.py:2234`, via `_check_enough_kv_cache_memory`) and now by `max_servable_num_tokens`, which is what the scheduler admits against. Neither side can grow its own formula without the other seeing it. The failure uses `RequestStatus.FINISHED_IGNORED`, which `vllm/v1/request.py` already documents as the status for "requests whose prompt lengths are longer than the model's length cap", mapping to `finish_reason="length"`. `FinishReason.ERROR` is documented as a *retryable* internal error always converted to a 500, which is the wrong contract here. Returning a literal 400 would mean exposing the pool-derived bound to `input_processor._validate_prompt_len`, where `max_model_len` is validated; happy to do that in a follow-up if maintainers prefer it — it is a frontend/engine-core plumbing change and I kept it out of this PR. Behaviour is unchanged whenever the pool covers `max_model_len`, which is every correctly-sized deployment: the bound is then `>= max_model_len`, `_is_unservable` short-circuits on the first comparison, and nothing is rejected. The 70-block row above is byte-for-byte identical before and after. ### Relationship to #47272 — scoped around it, not a duplicate I read #47272 ("Reserve the KV null block when validating `max_model_len`") before writing any code, and this PR is deliberately scoped around it. - **#47272 owns the capacity side.** It subtracts one block from the memory the startup check validates against, so a pool that cannot serve `max_model_len` is refused at boot with the existing message naming the estimated maximum model length. That is the right place for it and this PR does not touch that code path. Applied to the reproduction above, #47272 makes the 69-block pool illegal at startup — which is a better outcome than anything the scheduler can do, and is why I am not proposing an alternative to it. - **This PR owns the request side.** It makes the runtime bound the same function as the startup bound, and gives the engine an answer for a request it cannot serve other than retrying it. That is needed independently of #47272, because the scheduler currently has *no* concept of "this request can never be scheduled": it only distinguishes "not now". If #47272 lands, this PR's check becomes dormant on correctly-sized pools (bound `>= max_model_len`) and remains the backstop for the paths #47272 does not cover — notably `_auto_fit_max_model_len`, which runs before #47272's reservation and can still land on the boundary. - The two compose cleanly and neither subsumes the other. **Please do not merge this instead of #47272.** Other prior art I checked: **#40946** (merged) is the design precedent — it fixed the same class of defect (startup pool sizing and runtime admission using different formulas) for SWA/chunked-local by putting the bound in one method called from both sites, and this PR follows that shape. **#35541** (closed not-planned/stale) asked for "abort requests that can never fit in the KV cache block pool with a clear error rather than hanging indefinitely" — this is that, for the mechanism above. **#40384** is why the numbers here are stated in blocks and tokens rather than inverted from the `GPU KV cache size` log line, which on a hybrid model is `num_blocks // len(kv_cache_groups) * min_block_size`. ### Scope of the claim The field trace in #52520 came from a **downstream fork build** on a hybrid Qwen3.5 model (261,794-token request, `--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align`, MTP depth 3, pool within ~1 % of the window; 63 full re-prefills over 656 s with zero output tokens). The mechanism above is upstream code, and everything in this PR is demonstrated on **stock `main` at `4d2a68d64d9e05921ed5c4099146e768a92d71d5`** by the CPU-only unit test below — no GPU, no model weights, no fork code involved. One part of the original report I could **not** reproduce on `main` and am therefore not claiming: `vllm:num_preemptions_total` staying at `0.0` across the re-prefills. On `main` the self-preemption path does increment `request.num_preemptions` and record `EngineCoreEventType.PREEMPTED`, which `IterationStats` counts into `vllm:num_preemptions_total`. So there is no accounting fix here, and I am not filing one. (With this PR the point is moot for this defect: nothing is preempted, because nothing is admitted, and the operator gets two `ERROR` lines naming the limit.) ### The decode case, added in the second commit Review raised it and I measured it on the same stock-`main` harness: the admission gate bounds a request on `num_tokens + 1`, but a generate request grows to `prompt + max_tokens`. With `block_size` 16, `max_model_len` 1024 and the 69-block pool above (`max_servable_num_tokens` 1008), `prompt=1000, max_tokens=24` clears the frontend (`1000 + 24 <= 1024`, `vllm/renderers/params.py:210,442`) and clears admission (`1000 + 1 <= 1008`), and then reaches 1009 tokens at output token 9. On `main` it is preempted there, is now too long to re-prefill, and the next **3987 scheduler steps schedule zero tokens, produce no output and leave all 68 blocks free** — the same terminal state as the prefill case, reached through decode. Bounding admission on `num_tokens + max_tokens` would close it, but would refuse requests that stop well before the wall: on that same pool, `max_tokens=8` runs to completion in 12 steps. So the ceiling is applied where it belongs, as a length cap: `check_stop` takes `max_servable_num_tokens` instead of `max_model_len`. Those are equal on every pool that covers its window — `_estimate_max_model_len_from_groups` searches with `right = original_max` (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:1960`), and the scheduler falls back to `max_model_len` when there is no per-block bound — so the common path is unchanged. Where they differ the request stops on the ceiling and returns its tokens with `finish_reason: length`, exactly as if `max_model_len` had been set to what the pool can serve. That is one bound with three call sites: startup sizing, admission, and the length cap. The spec-decode lookahead can also reach past the ceiling, because the running path asks for `1 + len(spec_token_ids)` slots. Measured on stock `main` with drafts injected: it preempts twice and then finishes, because preemption clears `spec_token_ids` and the retry decodes into the cap. Bounded and self-correcting, so `sched/scheduler.py:605` is left alone. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_pool_unservable_requests.py # surrounding suite, unchanged behaviour: pytest tests/v1/core/ ``` `tests/v1/core/test_kv_pool_unservable_requests.py` is CPU-only (`pytestmark = pytest.mark.cpu_test`), built the same way as `tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py`: a real `Scheduler` over a hand-built hybrid `KVCacheConfig`, driven with `schedule()` / `update_from_output()`. No model weights, no GPU. Seven cases: 1. `test_max_servable_num_tokens_reserves_the_null_block` — the bound is `(69 - 1 - 5) * 16 = 1008` at the startup minimum, and `>= max_model_len` with one block of headroom. 2. `test_unservable_request_is_failed_not_prefilled_and_retried` — the regression test. A 1023-token request on the 69-block pool: nothing is scheduled, it is finished as `FINISHED_IGNORED`, `num_computed_tokens == 0`, `num_preemptions == 0`, and no unfinished request is left behind. 3. `test_request_at_the_bound_is_failed_because_it_needs_an_output_slot` — the bound is a sequence length, so a prompt of exactly 1008 is already too long (it was the one length that prefilled fully on `main` and then stalled on its first decode step). 4. `test_servable_request_at_the_same_pool_still_runs` — 1007 tokens on the *same* 69-block pool prefills fully, decodes, and finishes. The bound must not over-reject. 5. `test_pool_with_headroom_serves_the_whole_window` — 1023 tokens on a 70-block pool behaves exactly as before this PR. 6. `test_generation_stops_at_the_bound_instead_of_stalling_mid_decode` — the decode regression test. `prompt=1000, max_tokens=24` on the 69-block pool clears both length checks, then must finish `FINISHED_LENGTH_CAPPED` at 1008 tokens with `num_preemptions == 0` and nothing left unfinished. 7. `test_generation_is_not_capped_when_the_pool_covers_the_window` — the same request with one block of headroom must still produce all 24 tokens, so the length cap cannot silently truncate generation on the common path. ## Test Result The new file, checked out on top of unmodified `main` at `4d2a68d6` (the fix reverted, the test kept), fails: ```text $ git checkout HEAD -- vllm/ && pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_pool_unservable_requests.py -q FAILED test_max_servable_num_tokens_reserves_the_null_block - AttributeError: 'Scheduler' object has no attribute 'max_servable_num_tokens' FAILED test_unservable_request_is_failed_not_prefilled_and_retried - AssertionError: assert not {'0': 256} FAILED test_request_at_the_bound_is_failed_because_it_needs_an_output_slot - AssertionError: assert not {'0': 256} FAILED test_generation_stops_at_the_bound_instead_of_stalling_mid_decode - AttributeError: 'Scheduler' object has no attribute 'max_servable_num_tokens' FAILED test_generation_is_not_capped_when_the_pool_covers_the_window - AttributeError: 'Scheduler' object has no attribute 'max_servable_num_tokens' 5 failed, 2 passed, 14 warnings in 4.81s ``` `{'0': 256}` is `main` admitting the unservable request and scheduling the first 256-token prefill chunk of the sequence it will then throw away. The two that pass before and after are the two "must still work" directions — they are there to catch over-rejection and over-capping, and they must never have gone red. Reverting only the one-line length cap and keeping everything else isolates the decode case: ```text $ sed -i 's/self.max_servable_num_tokens)/self.max_model_len)/' <the check_stop call> $ pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_pool_unservable_requests.py -q FAILED test_generation_stops_at_the_bound_instead_of_stalling_mid_decode - assert <RequestStatus.PREEMPTED: 6> == <RequestStatus.FINISHED_LENGTH_CAPPED: 8> 1 failed, 6 passed, 14 warnings in 4.92s ``` With the fix: ```text $ pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_pool_unservable_requests.py -q ....... [100%] 7 passed, 14 warnings in 4.71s ``` Surrounding suite, same command on `4d2a68d6` and on this branch: ```text main @ 4d2a68d6 : 2 failed, 495 passed, 2 errors in 348.75s this branch : 2 failed, 502 passed, 2 errors in 375.92s ``` The same two failures and the same two setup errors occur on both, all environmental in my CPU-only sandbox and unrelated to this change: failures in `test_scheduler.py::test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders` and `test_reset_prefix_cache_e2e.py::test_reset_prefix_cache_e2e`, and setup errors on `test_concurrent_partial_prefill` and `test_prefix_cache_stats_is_recorded` — all four need a GPU-backed engine core. The +7 are the new tests. Two existing tests build a `Scheduler` with `object.__new__` and set its attributes by hand; they each gain one line for the new `unservable_reqs` set and one for `max_servable_num_tokens` (`tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`, `tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py`). Lint gates on the changed files: ```text $ ruff check <changed files> # 0.14.0, as pinned in .pre-commit-config.yaml All checks passed! $ ruff format --check <changed files> 5 files already formatted $ typos --force-exclude <changed files> (clean) $ python tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.12 <changed files> # mypy 1.20.2 Success: no issues found in 2 source files Success: no issues found in 3 source files ``` --- AI assistance was used to investigate and draft this change; every changed line was reviewed, and the reproduction, the tests and the lint gates were run locally as described above. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [x] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. — none needed: no new model, flag, or user-facing configuration. </details>

signal.title: Decode optimizations for NVIDIA confidential computing
signal.text:
## Background Confidential Computing (CC) is a feature of NVIDIA GPUs (Hopper and later) that protects workloads running in a confidential VM from infrastructure operators. It implements a range of security features on the GPU, including encrypted data transfers over PCIe and between GPUs. CC is designed to require no code changes for existing applications, albeit often at a performance penalty. Running vLLM under CC, we measured a significant degradation in both prefill and decode performance relative to non-CC operation. We traced the decode degradation to CUDA async memcpy behavior under CC's bounce-buffer encryption: a host<->device `cudaMemcpyAsync` on pinned memory becomes **host-synchronous** — the issuing thread blocks until the copy *and everything already queued on its stream* completes. This hurts the engine in two ways: 1. **H2D input copies** issued on the compute stream during `_prepare_inputs` block the scheduler thread for the duration of the in-flight forward pass (~one full step per copy), starving the GPU of work. 2. **The per-step D2H token readback** blocks the thread that issues it, delaying the next step's CUDA graph launch by roughly one decode step. ## Changes All changes are gated on CC detection and are no-ops otherwise; the non-CC code paths are untouched. - **CC detection** (`Platform.is_confidential_compute()`): auto-detected once via NVML, with a `VLLM_CONFIDENTIAL_COMPUTE=0/1` env override for testing and for hosts without NVML. - **Staged H2D input copies** (`StagedH2DCopier`, `prep_stream_ctx` in `vllm/v1/conf_compute_utils.py`): the H2D lands in a double-buffered device staging tensor on a dedicated prep stream — paying only its own ~tens-of-µs transfer instead of draining the in-flight forward — followed by a device-to-device copy on the compute stream (genuinely asynchronous under CC), ordered after the forward's reads of the reused input buffers. A round-robin pool of prep streams keeps consecutive copies within one `_prepare_inputs` from queuing behind each other. - **Async D2H output readback** (`AsyncD2HCopyWorker`): the still-blocking per-step sampled-token/logprobs readback is submitted to a dedicated daemon thread, which event-syncs on the producing forward+sample and performs the copies on its own stream. The copy remains synchronous under CC but no longer blocks the scheduler thread, restoring scheduling/compute overlap (mirrors TensorRT-LLM PR #8463). ## Test Plan Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, TP4, B300 (SXM6) with CC on (NVLE multi-GPU mode), fp8 KV cache, FlashInfer AR+RMSNorm fusion enabled on both sides (via the companion FlashInfer CC workspace fix), ISL/OSL 1024/1024, `vllm bench serve`; before/after = this PR's optimizations off/on. ## Test Result Concurrency | Output tok/s (before → after) | Median TPOT ms (before → after) | CC off -- | -- | -- | -- 4 | 306 → 404 (+31.8%) | 12.64 → 9.47 (−25.1%) | 434 8 | 548 → 713 (+30.1%) | 14.09 → 10.80 (−23.4%) | 754 16 | 925 → 1143 (+23.6%) | 16.74 → 13.46 (−19.6%) | 1287 32 | 1428 → 1701 (+19.1%) | 21.74 → 18.18 (−16.4%) | 2080 64 | 2186 → 2506 (+14.6%) | 28.41 → 24.76 (−12.8%) | 3314 128 | 3654 → 4079 (+11.6%) | 34.00 → 30.41 (−10.5%) | —

The last column is the non-CC reference: the same hardware, model, and benchmark configuration with CC disabled.

This brings decode performance under CC roughly on par with the non-CC baseline at low concurrency (93–95% of its throughput, up from ~71%), and to 76–89% at medium concurrency.

signal.title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Resolve tuned configs across device-name aliases
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes #50436. ROCm can report the same device under different names. This change keeps exact config lookup first, then falls back to a single equivalent device name after an exact miss. Empty or ambiguous matches still use the existing default path. If ROCm platform detection returns a non-string device name, configuration lookup falls back to `torch.cuda.get_device_name()` before applying the same resolver. Valid platform-provided string names remain unchanged. The shared resolver is used by the MoE, FlyDSL MoE, block INT8/FP8, and Mamba config loaders. Non-ROCm behavior and user-config priority are unchanged. ## Not a duplicate PR #44331 adds a gfx1151 config, and PR #44332 proposes a broader platform-name fallback. This PR keeps the fallback local to the tuned-config filename boundary and does not depend on #44332. ## Validation Validated on Radeon 8060S / gfx1151: - 11 focused platform/config tests and 6 existing Mamba config tests passed. - All six shipped Qwen3 W4A16 MoE configs matched the torch reference. - Tuned configs were 3.20x-4.52x faster than the current default. - Full-model Qwen3 A/B produced identical 32-token greedy output. - Ruff format/check passed. Commands: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/test_platform_utils.py \ tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba_ssm_configs.py -q changed=$(git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD -- '*.py') .venv/bin/ruff format --check $changed .venv/bin/ruff check $changed ``` ## AI assistance This change was prepared with GitHub Copilot assistance. The implementation, tests, and PR text were AI-assisted. Validation was executed on physical AMD hardware, and publication was explicitly approved after vLLM's AI contribution and accountability requirements were reviewed.

signal.title: [Quantization][ModelOpt] Serve modelopt_mixed checkpoints with FP8_PB layers
signal.text: ## Summary Serves `modelopt_mixed` checkpoints containing FP8_PB layers. Rebased onto #49381. FP8_PB and FP8_PB_WO are the same quantization scheme — per-block FP8 with dynamic per-token activation quant — resolving to the same QuantKey pair and the same block-FP8 kernel. They differ only in scale serialization: FP8_PB_WO exports ModelOpt's 4-D `weight_scale` [out_blk, 1, in_blk, 1], which requires every partition to be block-aligned; FP8_PB uses DeepSeek's 2-D `weight_scale_inv`, sized by ceiling division, so a partition may end in a partial block. GLM-5.2 needs the latter. `q_a_proj` (2048) + `kv_a_proj_with_mqa` (576) fuse to a 2624-wide `fused_qkv_a_proj`; `2624 % 128 = 64`, and the layer is replicated, so no TP degree makes it block-aligned. Previously this failed with `KeyError: '...weight_scale_inv'`. ## Design Since the layout can't live in the QuantKey, it rides on `CkptCtx.block_scale_deepseek` — the per-checkpoint carrier #49381 already provides — and `KFp8Block128` branches on it. `FormatScheme` is the wrong seam: it composes *around* the key schemes and can't replace what the weight scheme registers, and a secondpossible for the same key. Adding FP8_PB is one `LINEAR_ALGOS` row plus one `resolve()` row. No new sub-config — `resolve()` only reads `subcfg` for the NVFP4 LinearKernel` already reads whichever scale name is present, so no kernel change. `kFp8Static128BlockSym` is 128x128, so a checkpoint declaring another `group_size` is rejected at config time rather than silently m ## Two fixes to existing behavior 1. `ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig` never implems()`, which `VllmConfig` uses to enable `+quant_fp8`. Without it `QuantFP8` runs `forward_native`, emitting unpacked fp32 group scales where Dwants them UE8M0-packed into int32 — the model serves NaN logits. Resolving it per layer fixes FP8_PB_WO mixed checkpoints too, not just F 2. `deep_gemm_warmup` discovered layers via `ip8LinearMethod)` plus `block_quant`/`use_marlin`/`fp8_linear`. The generic `ModelOptLinearMethod` has none of those and keeps its kernel in `kernears were invisible to the warmup and DeepGEMM JIT-compiled during serving. Now probes the selected kernel and reads the block size from `layer.weight ## Validation B300 (sm103), `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4-V2` @ `57a4 FP8_PB layers. `tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py`: 43 passng hardcoded path). GSM8K, 1319 problems, 5-shot: | Config | exact_match | vs baseline | |---|---|---| | pre-rebase, TP8 (baseline) | 0.9431 / 0.9439 | this PR, DP8 | 0.9416 ±0.0065 | −0.16σ | | this PR, TP8 | 0.9484 ±0.0061 | +0.60σ | Throughput (random 1024/128, 256 prompts, c64)t tok/s, 256/256 successful. No regression against the best pre-rebase configuration (11.72–12.81 req/s). The warmup fix is load-bearing, not cosmetic. Controlled A/B on one container: | | req/s | Mean TTFT | Mean TPOT | |---|---|---|---| | old route | 12.81 | 968ms | 31.6ms | | new route, no warmup fix | 5.52 | 2479ms | 7 | new route + warmup fix | 11.72 | 1060ms | 34.6ms |

signal.title: [Spec Decode] Failing test: speculative max_model_len is silently ignored
signal.text: ## Purpose Draft. Adds a failing test for #52258 to pin down the behavior before fixing it, because the right scope is not obvious and I would rather agree on it than guess. `max_model_len` in the speculative config is accepted and validated, then has no effect. There are two separate reasons, depending on the method: **Draft-model methods (mtp, eagle, dflash).** The value reaches `draft_model_config.max_model_len` (`config/speculative.py:1127`), and nothing reads it: ``` $ grep -rn "draft_model_config" vllm/v1/ | grep max_model_len (no matches) ``` The two runtime sites that look like consumers read the **target** config: `v1/spec_decode/suffix_decoding.py:23`, and `v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/speculator.py:86-87` where `draft_max_seq_len` is assigned from `vllm_config.model_config.max_model_len`. **ngram.** `draft_model_config` is an alias of `target_model_config` (`config/speculative.py:834`) and the override never runs, so the value is dropped before it reaches the draft config at all. Confirmed the alias does not corrupt the target's own `max_model_len`. The existing `test_mtp_speculative_config_max_model_len` covers the config plumbing and passes, which is why this has gone unnoticed: the option looks wired up. The mechanism for skipping already exists in-tree. `suffix_decoding.py:59-62` does exactly what #52258 asks for, bounded on the target length: ```python if num_tokens >= self.max_model_len: # Skip requests that have already reached the max model length. draft_token_ids.append([]) continue ``` `ngram_proposer.py` and `step3p5.py` have the same guard. `eagle.py`, `dflash.py`, `draft_model.py`, `medusa.py` and `gemma4.py` have no `max_model_len` awareness at all. ## Scope question Three options, smallest first. This PR is only the test; I will implement whichever is preferred. 1. Warn or reject when `speculative_config.max_model_len` is set, so the option stops silently doing nothing. 2. Bound the existing skip on the draft's configured length, and extend the guard to the proposers that lack one. This restores the documented V0 behavior and reuses a pattern already in the directory. 3. Per-request speculative control, the broader ask in the issue, which probably wants an RFC. I would default to (2) but (1) is defensible on its own and is a prerequisite either way. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_max_len.py::test_ngram_speculative_config_max_model_len_is_respected -q ``` ## Test Result Fails as intended on `main` @ `6914d60b1e`, on a single RTX 4090: ``` FAILED tests/v1/spec_decode/test_max_len.py::test_ngram_speculative_config_max_model_len_is_respected 1 failed, 14 warnings in 3.58s ``` The assertion is `draft_model_config.max_model_len == 80`; the actual value is `200`, the target's. Config-only, so it needs no GPU work and runs in seconds. The rest of the file is unaffected: ```bash pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_max_len.py -q -k "not ngram_speculative_config" ``` No model evaluation results: this PR adds a test and changes no runtime behavior. If (2) is chosen I will include acceptance-rate numbers before and after, since that scope does affect output. ### Not a duplicate `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "52258"` returns nothing; the issue had no other claimants when I commented on it. ### AI assistance Developed with AI assistance (Claude). I reviewed every line, ran the tests myself, and can defend the change.

signal.title: [Bugfix][DCP] Handle sparse MLA metadata after DCP Manager refactor
signal.text: ## Purpose DCP Manager refactoring #50484 is focused on DCP for dense MLA, which does not handle sparse MLA properly. - `MLASparseMetadata` does not inherit `MLACommonMetadata`, thus `attn_metadata.decode` attribute access should be guarded by getattr - DCP query-gather assumes a decode query, so its workspace (direct_dcp_q_gather_workspace) is too small for prefill queries (which is passed via forced MQA codepath). - Forced MQA codepath must be considered in DCP Manager combine as well. signal.title: Bump setuptools to a CVE-2025-47273-fixed release across build/platform/test requirements
signal.text: ## Summary Several requirement files pin or permit setuptools releases below the `78.1.1` floor that fixes [CVE-2025-47273](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-47273) ([GHSA-5rjg-fvgr-3xxf](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5rjg-fvgr-3xxf)), a path traversal in setuptools' package-index/archive handling: - `pyproject.toml`'s PEP 517 `build-system.requires` and several `requirements/build/*.txt` files allow `setuptools>=77.0.3` with no lower bound at the fixed release - `requirements/build/cpu.txt` and `requirements/cpu.txt` pin the exact vulnerable `setuptools==77.0.3` - `requirements/tpu.txt` pins `setuptools==78.1.0`, one patch release short of the fix - The generated test locks `requirements/test/cpu.txt` and `requirements/test/cuda.txt` also resolve to `setuptools==77.0.3` This bumps every affected pin/lower-bound to `78.1.1`. Other parts of the repo (`docker/Dockerfile.ppc64le`, `build_vllm_ppc64le.sh`, `requirements/test/rocm.txt`, `requirements/test/xpu.txt`) already use a setuptools version at or above this floor, so this brings the rest of the requirement set in line with that existing practice. This is a MODERATE-severity supply-chain issue per the project's own [severity guide](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/SECURITY.md) (build-time, requires a malicious package index/archive to be exercised during a build step; no RCE or privileged-access path demonstrated), which is why this is a plain PR rather than a private security advisory. **Note on `requirements/build/cpu.txt` / `requirements/cpu.txt`:** the prior exact pin carried a comment that `setuptools==77.0.3` "can reuse CMake build dir". I don't have a way to independently confirm whether `78.1.1` preserves that specific behavior, so I've flagged it inline for maintainer judgment — if it doesn't, please pick another `setuptools` release `>=78.1.1` that does. ## Test plan - [x] Confirmed no remaining `setuptools==77.0.3` / `setuptools==78.1.0` / unbounded `setuptools>=77.0.3` reference anywhere in `pyproject.toml` or `requirements/` - [ ] Maintainer: confirm `setuptools==78.1.1` still supports the CMake build-dir reuse the prior pin's comment referenced - [ ] Maintainer: confirm the generated test locks (`requirements/test/cpu.txt`, `requirements/test/cuda.txt`) don't need a full `uv pip compile` regeneration instead of the direct edit here

TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/torchinductor_nsml ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Summary For Python-only builds, vLLM resolves a precompiled-wheel variant before fetching wheel metadata. The [Python-only build documentation](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/getting_started/installation/gpu/) documents `VLLM_PRECOMPILED_WHEEL_VARIANT` as selecting a variant subdirectory such as `cu129` or `cu130`. If it is not set, the CUDA variant is auto-detected from the local environment using PyTorch or `nvidia-smi`. The [nightly wheel documentation](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/contributing/ci/nightly_builds/) describes the root index as the default variant and named subdirectories as variant-specific indices. If metadata for the selected variant cannot be fetched, [`precompiled_wheel_utils.determine_wheel_url()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/836aac92ffdaa337083934181cb6d00b64b2a1a6/setup.py) currently retries the root/default metadata: ```python try: wheels, repo_url = precompiled_wheel_utils.fetch_metadata_for_variant( commit, variant ) except Exception as e: logger.warning( "Failed to fetch precompiled wheel metadata for variant %s: %s", variant, e, ) try_default = True if try_default: print("Trying the default variant from remote") wheels, repo_url = precompiled_wheel_utils.fetch_metadata_for_variant( commit, None ) ``` The fallback is part of the current resolution order. The issue is that once it happens, the CUDA variant selected explicitly or detected from the local environment is no longer used to qualify the fallback wheel. The wheel filtering that follows checks the package name and target architecture: ```python if wheel.get("package_name") == "vllm" and arch in wheel.get( "platform_tag", "" ): ... ``` but does not check that the root/default artifact matches the CUDA variant selected earlier. I encountered a concrete case where PyTorch CUDA 12.9 selected `cu129`, the `cu129` metadata lookup failed, and the fallback selected a native artifact requiring CUDA 13. I propose keeping the selected CUDA variant for the rest of precompiled-wheel resolution: if its metadata cannot be fetched, propagate that lookup failure instead of retrying the root/default variant. ### Concrete reproduction I encountered this while reproducing a separate issue from the exact v0.27.1 source: ```text source: v0.27.1 6e448d0ea9bf3d88d898b65449ca6dc2aec170ac PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu129 torch.version.cuda: 12.9 ``` Using the documented Python-only precompiled installation path: ```bash VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto ``` with neither `VLLM_PRECOMPILED_WHEEL_VARIANT` nor `VLLM_PRECOMPILED_WHEEL_COMMIT` set, the CUDA detection path selected: ```text cu129 ``` The Python-only build selected the following precompiled base commit: ```text f5bb701fa270f5c801f1572e1478b56f292d8dfc ``` For that commit, metadata for `cu129` was unavailable: ```text https://wheels.vllm.ai/f5bb701fa270f5c801f1572e1478b56f292d8dfc/cu129/vllm/metadata.json -> 404 ``` The fallback then queried the root/default metadata: ```text https://wheels.vllm.ai/f5bb701fa270f5c801f1572e1478b56f292d8dfc/vllm/metadata.json -> 200 ``` The resulting path was: ```text PyTorch CUDA 12.9 -> select cu129 -> cu129 metadata unavailable -> retry root/default metadata -> select default wheel ``` ### Artifact verification I extracted `vllm/_C_stable_libtorch.abi3.so` from the wheel selected through the root/default fallback and inspected its ELF dependencies. The fallback artifact requires: ```text NEEDED: libcudart.so.13 ``` As a control, the published `cu129` artifact for the exact v0.27.1 commit is available at: ```text https://wheels.vllm.ai/6e448d0ea9bf3d88d898b65449ca6dc2aec170ac/cu129/vllm/metadata.json -> 200 ``` Its `_C_stable_libtorch.abi3.so` requires: ```text NEEDED: libcudart.so.12 ``` So in this reproduction, the resolver first selected `cu129`, then replaced that selection after the metadata failure with a root/default artifact requiring `libcudart.so.13`. The exact-v0.27.1 `cu129` artifact is only used here as a control for the native CUDA dependency of a published `cu129` wheel. I am not proposing any change to the existing base-commit selection behavior. The problematic transition happens after the base commit and CUDA variant have already been selected. ### Why the default fallback is unsafe The [nightly wheel documentation](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/contributing/ci/nightly_builds/) treats the root index as the default variant and named subdirectories as separate variants. It also notes that the default variant can have a named alias, and that not every variant is present on every commit. A missing `cu129` index therefore does not imply that the root/default wheel is an equivalent `cu129` replacement. The current fallback nevertheless changes: ```text selected: cu129 | | metadata lookup fails v fallback: root/default | | package + architecture filtering v selected wheel ``` There is no CUDA-variant check between the selected variant and the fallback artifact. This affects explicit selection as well as auto-detection. For example, a user setting: ```text VLLM_PRECOMPILED_WHEEL_VARIANT=cu129 ``` can currently receive the default variant if the `cu129` metadata lookup fails. The root/default CUDA variant also cannot be inferred safely from the current `VLLM_MAIN_CUDA_VERSION`. `VLLM_PRECOMPILED_WHEEL_COMMIT` can select a different or historical wheel commit, and the normal Python-only path can select a base commit from `main`. The default artifact for that commit may therefore reflect a different CUDA build configuration from the one selected in the current environment. With the current metadata and wheel filtering, there is no check that makes the root/default wheel a verified replacement for an already selected CUDA variant. ### Proposed fix For CUDA, once a variant has been selected, fetch metadata only for that variant. If: ```python fetch_metadata_for_variant(commit, variant) ``` fails, propagate that error instead of retrying: ```python fetch_metadata_for_variant(commit, None) ``` The behavior changes from: ```text current: select cu129 -> fetch cu129 metadata -> lookup fails -> fetch root/default metadata -> select by package name / architecture ``` to: ```text proposed: select cu129 -> fetch cu129 metadata -> lookup fails -> propagate the original lookup failure ``` A fallback could be kept if the resolver had enough information to verify that the default artifact is compatible with the selected CUDA variant. That check does not exist in the current resolution path, so doing that safely would require a broader metadata or compatibility-selection change. The proposed patch instead keeps the existing variant selection intact and fails at the variant-specific lookup when that artifact is unavailable. A root/default wheel may happen to be compatible in some cases, but the current resolver cannot distinguish those cases from the incompatible case reproduced above. The existing base-commit selection is unchanged, and the ROCm precompiled-wheel path is unchanged. Regression coverage checks both CUDA selection paths: - explicit `VLLM_PRECOMPILED_WHEEL_VARIANT`; - auto-detected CUDA variant. In both cases, a failed selected-variant lookup should propagate its original error without calling `fetch_metadata_for_variant(commit, None)`. ### Current `main` The same fallback is still present on `main` at [`836aac92ffdaa337083934181cb6d00b64b2a1a6`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/836aac92ffdaa337083934181cb6d00b64b2a1a6). I also reproduced the path independently of the current contents of `wheels.vllm.ai` with a metadata-fetch stub: ```text fetch(commit, "cu129") -> raises fetch(commit, None) -> returns default metadata ``` On the unmodified code, both explicit and auto-detected `cu129` make both calls and return the default wheel. The regression test for the proposed behavior expects the first lookup error to propagate instead. ### Context / related work The variant-specific lookup followed by the default fallback was introduced in #29838. #32948 later added CUDA variant auto-detection while retaining that fallback. Related reports cover different paths: - #42338 reports a similar CUDA 12.9 -> CUDA 13 result through package resolver/index selection. This issue concerns the Python-only precompiled-wheel fallback after a CUDA variant has already been selected. - #49683 concerns availability of `cu129` nightly artifacts. Missing variant-specific metadata can trigger the fallback described here, but artifact availability itself is a separate problem. - PR #34139 discussed native compatibility concerns when falling back across different nightly commits. Here the wheel commit stays fixed while the selected CUDA variant is replaced by that commit's default variant. I have a patch implementing the proposed behavior with regression coverage for both explicit and auto-detected CUDA variants, and will open a draft PR shortly. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signal.title: [Bugfix] Keep top-level quantization_config when benchmark_moe descends via --model-prefix
signal.text: ## Purpose `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py --model-prefix` silently tunes the wrong kernel variant for quantized checkpoints with nested configs. HF checkpoints keep `quantization_config` at the top level of `config.json`, while the MoE parameters of VL MoE checkpoints live in a nested sub-config. `--model-prefix text_config` replaces the whole config object with the sub-config, so `get_weight_block_size_safety()` / `get_quantization_group_size()` no longer see the checkpoint's `quantization_config`: - block-FP8 checkpoints (e.g. `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8`, `weight_block_size: [128, 128]`) get tuned as the **per-tensor** FP8 variant, and `save_configs()` writes the result to a filename **without** `block_shape=[128,128]` — the serving-time lookup then never loads the tuned file, so hours of tuning are silently wasted; - int4 (AWQ/GPTQ) checkpoints fail outright with "Could not determine group_size". This was hit in practice in #44688 ("tuning requires a flattened config workaround — `--model-prefix text_config` drops the top-level `quantization_config`, silently producing the per-tensor variant instead of `block_shape=[128,128]`"); no fix was filed. #37068 adds `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration` support to `get_model_params()` but doesn't touch the quantization-config loss, and I found no other issue/PR covering it. The fix carries the top-level `quantization_config` over to the sub-config when descending (not overwriting one the sub-config already has), so dtype/block-shape/group-size detection matches the checkpoint regardless of `--model-prefix`. AI assistance (GitHub Copilot CLI) was used to prepare this PR. ## Test Plan On an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell with the `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` checkpoint (E=256, N=512 at TP=1, block-FP8 `[128,128]`): ```bash python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py --model <Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8> \ --model-prefix text_config --dtype fp8_w8a8 --tp-size 1 --batch-size 8 ``` before/after this change, plus the same command without `--model-prefix` (nested-config support from #37340 makes the prefix optional for this family) as the reference behavior. Edge cases checked with synthetic nested configs: AWQ `group_size` resolution through the prefix, a sub-config that already has its own `quantization_config` (must not be overwritten), and configs with no `quantization_config` at all (no attribute injected). `pre-commit run --files benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py` and `git diff --check`. ## Test Result Before (with `--model-prefix text_config`) — block shape lost, wrong filename probed, falls back to default config: ```text WARNING [fused_moe.py:1161] Using default MoE config. Performance might be sub-optimal! Config file not found at .../E=256,N=512,device_name=NVIDIA_RTX_PRO_6000_Blackwell_Server_Edition,dtype=fp8_w8a8.json ``` After — matches the no-prefix reference exactly and loads the committed tuned block-FP8 config: ```text INFO [fused_moe.py:1148] Using configuration from .../E=256,N=512,device_name=NVIDIA_RTX_PRO_6000_Blackwell_Server_Edition,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128,128].json for MoE layer. ``` Synthetic-config checks: AWQ `group_size=128` resolves through the prefix; existing sub-config `quantization_config` preserved (`[64, 64]` not overwritten by `[128, 128]`); no-quantization case unchanged (`None`, no attribute added). ruff/mypy/typos hooks and `git diff --check` pass. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Handle custom tool history in Responses API
signal.text: ## Purpose Fix Responses API multi-turn requests that resubmit `custom_tool_call` and `custom_tool_call_output` items. `ResponsesRequest` validates these input items into `ResponseCustomToolCall` Pydantic models. The non-Harmony message conversion handled function tool models but allowed custom tool models to fall through into the chat message list. On the next item, `_construct_message_from_response_item` called `.get()` on the previous `ResponseCustomToolCall`, causing: ```text AttributeError: 'ResponseCustomToolCall' object has no attribute 'get' ``` This change converts custom calls into the OpenAI chat message custom-tool representation and converts custom call outputs into tool messages. It preserves the custom tool name, freeform input, and call ID without coercing the call into a function tool. The regression test covers the public conversion path with a `custom_tool_call -> custom_tool_call_output -> user message` sequence. Duplicate checks searched open PRs for `ResponseCustomToolCall`, `custom tool history Responses API`, and `custom_tool_call_output Responses API`. No other PR addresses this history-conversion failure. Rechecked after #49724 and #49882: they address initial active custom-tool prompting and output classification on non-Harmony routes, choosing fail-fast rejection for unsupported tools; this PR handles resubmitted custom-tool history, so the scopes are complementary. #35905 concerns the ResponseStore abstraction, while #41834 only matched incidental model text and is unrelated. No documentation update is needed because this fixes existing Responses API input handling without changing the public interface. Model evaluation is not applicable. The change is a deterministic frontend protocol conversion and does not modify model weights, sampling, tokenization, tool parsing, or generated output. The focused conversion regression is the relevant validation. AI assistance was used to diagnose the failure, prepare the focused implementation and test, run duplicate checks, and draft this description. The human submitter is responsible for reviewing and validating the change. ## Test Plan Run the focused Responses utility regression test and frontend lint/format checks in a configured vLLM environment: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_responses_utils.py::TestResponsesUtils::test_construct_input_messages_with_custom_tool_history pre-commit run ruff-check --files vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/utils.py tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_responses_utils.py pre-commit run ruff-format --files vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/utils.py tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_responses_utils.py git diff --check ``` ## Test Result Before the fix, the minimized conversion path reproduced: ```text AttributeError: 'ResponseCustomToolCall' object has no attribute 'get' ``` After the fix, the same path produced the expected assistant custom tool call, tool result, and user message. ```text PASS: custom tool history converted to chat messages All checks passed! 2 files already formatted ``` After rebasing onto the current `main`, the complete Responses utility test file passed in a Python 3.12 `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=empty` environment: ```text 41 passed ``` Ruff check, Ruff format check, and `git diff --check` also passed. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [x] No documentation update is needed for this bug fix. </details>

signal.title: [Feature]: Restore length-based speculation skip (speculative max_model_len) or per-request speculative decoding control in V1
signal.text: ## 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch In V0, `--speculative-max-model-len` allowed sequences longer than a threshold to automatically skip speculation (documented in v0.6.x spec_decode docs). In V1, the config plumbing survives — `SpeculativeConfig.max_model_len` is still accepted and `_maybe_override_draft_max_model_len()` still overrides `draft_model_config.max_model_len` (its docstring even says "mainly used for testing that sequences can skip speculation") — but we could not find any runtime consumer under `vllm/v1/`, and empirically the field is a no-op. **Repro (vLLM 0.26.0, DGX Spark GB10, Qwen3.6-27B NVFP4 target + DFlash drafter):** ``` --speculative-config '{"method": "dflash", "model": "z-lab/Qwen3.6-27B-DFlash", "num_speculative_tokens": 10, "max_model_len": 12288}' ``` - Config validation accepts the field, engine boots normally. - A 19,853-token prompt still drafts normally (spec_decode_num_drafts_total +149 for a 150-token completion) — no skip. ## Use case Mixed workloads on a single engine: interactive short prompts get a real speculation win (we measure 1.6–1.8× decode with EAGLE-3/DFlash), but long-document summarization (20K–73K Chinese meeting transcripts) collapses to 5–8% acceptance, making speculation net-negative (decode drops below the no-spec baseline). With no per-request toggle in V1 and the dynamic schedule (`num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size`) keyed on batch size only, there is currently no way to keep speculation for short requests while disabling it for long ones on one engine — and unified-memory hardware (GB10 128GB) cannot co-load a second engine as a workaround. ## Ask Either: 1. Re-implement the V0 behavior: proposers skip drafting when the sequence exceeds the draft model's effective `max_model_len`, or 2. Expose a per-request control (e.g. a SamplingParams / request-level field to disable speculation), or 3. A length-keyed variant of the dynamic speculative schedule. Related: RFC #36657 (Dynamic Speculation Length / confidence-based early exit) addresses the per-step dimension but not the per-request/length dimension. ## Alternatives - Dual serve profiles routed by input length — not viable on unified-memory single-GPU hosts (cannot co-load two large models). - Batch-size-keyed dynamic schedule — wrong dimension for bs=1 long jobs. - Patching the sealed vendor image — not sustainable.

signal.title: [Core][V1] Support trace_decode_token_ids for deterministic decode replay
signal.text: Add inference trace-replay: a new SamplingParams.trace_decode_token_ids field that forces the v1 sampler to emit a predetermined sequence of decode token IDs, step by step, instead of sampling. Real logprobs and token ranks are still computed from the unmodified logit distribution. The sampler injects each trace token after sampling (so logprobs stay real); InputBatch tracks the trace per request in parallel with spec_token_ids; and EngineCore.add_request caps generation to the trace length / forces ignore_eos, falling back to normal sampling (with a warning) for incompatible modes (speculative decoding, n > 1). Tests cover the SamplingParams field, sampler injection (including async -1 placeholders and past-end-of-trace), and engine-core admission. A demo example script is added under examples/generate/. ## Purpose Add **inference trace-replay**: a new `SamplingParams.trace_decode_token_ids` field that forces the v1 sampler to emit a predetermined sequence of decode token IDs, step by step, instead of sampling. Real logprobs and token ranks are still computed from the unmodified logit distribution at each step. **Motivation.** The goal is to make a request follow a *fixed* token trace and return the logprobs the model assigns to that exact trace. This is useful for: - **Quantifying differences between settings/backends.** Replaying the same trace under different configs (dtype, quantization, attention/MoE backend, TP size, etc.) and comparing per-token logprobs gives a direct, apples-to-apples measure of numerical divergence on identical token sequences. - **RL training.** It lets you recompute logprobs for a rollout's exact tokens under the training engine, so the rollout↔train logprob gap can be measured and minimized — without re-sampling and drifting onto a different trajectory. **Why decode-replay and not prefill-only scoring?** Computing logprobs by prefilling the full (prompt + response) sequence does *not* faithfully reproduce the decode-time distribution: many models run **different operators / kernels in the prefill path vs. the decode path** (e.g. attention and MoE kernels differ between the two phases). To measure the logprobs a model would actually produce while *decoding*, the tokens must go through the decode path one step at a time — which is exactly what trace-replay does. ### How it works 1. Set `SamplingParams.trace_decode_token_ids` to the list of decode token IDs to force. 2. The sampler injects each trace token **after** sampling (`Sampler._inject_trace_tokens` in `vllm/v1/sample/sampler.py`), so logprobs stay real — they are computed from the original logits, before injection. 3. `InputBatch` tracks the trace per request in parallel with `spec_token_ids` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_input_batch.py`); the per-request step index counts real output tokens, skipping the trailing `-1` async-scheduling placeholder. 4. `EngineCore.add_request` caps generation to the trace length and forces `ignore_eos`, so EOS tokens inside the trace do not halt generation early. It falls back to normal sampling (with a warning) for incompatible modes (speculative decoding, `n > 1`). ### Not a duplicate No open PR addresses this — searched the repo for open PRs matching `trace_decode_token_ids` and `trace`/`replay` in title (0 results). The closest existing features are `logprob_token_ids` (only *scores* a fixed token set, doesn't force the output sequence) and `spec_token_ids` (speculative decoding, different purpose); neither forces a predetermined decode trace. ## Test Plan ```bash # Unit tests (CPU-only, no GPU required) .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/sample/test_trace_replay.py \ tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core_trace_replay.py -v # Lint / type-check as in CI pre-commit run --all-files pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --all-files --hook-stage manual ``` - `tests/v1/sample/test_trace_replay.py` — `SamplingParams` field defaults, clone preservation, and validation (empty / negative / non-int rejected); sampler injection covering step 0, mixed per-request steps, past-end-of-trace (no-op), the async `-1` placeholder, and the unset/none path. - `tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core_trace_replay.py` — engine-core admission: generation bounds capped to trace length + `ignore_eos` forced; fallback to normal sampling for speculative decoding and `n > 1`. - Demo: `examples/generate/trace_replay_offline.py` — greedy-generate to capture decode tokens, then replay them and assert a token-by-token match while printing per-token logprobs. ## Test Result ```text $ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/sample/test_trace_replay.py \ tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core_trace_replay.py tests/v1/sample/test_trace_replay.py .............. [ 82%] tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core_trace_replay.py ... [100%] ======================= 17 passed, 16 warnings in 0.14s ======================== ``` `pre-commit run --all-files` and `mypy-3.12` (CI hook stage) pass on the changed files (ruff-check, ruff-format, SPDX headers, forbidden-imports, etc.). > ⚠️ Unit tests were run on a CPU-only box; the end-to-end demo > (`examples/generate/trace_replay_offline.py`) should be run on a GPU to confirm > token-by-token replay before merge. > **AI assistance disclosure:** developed with AI assistance (Claude). The > submitter has reviewed every changed line and is responsible for the change > end-to-end. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [x] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Bugfix] Invalidate LazyDict cache on __setitem__
signal.text: ## Purpose `LazyDict` caches each value the first time its factory runs, but `__setitem__` only replaced the factory — it never dropped the cached value. So a key that was read before being overwritten keeps returning the old value, and the new factory is never called: ```python d = LazyDict({"a": lambda: "first"}) d["a"] # "first" (now cached in self._dict) d["a"] = lambda: "second" d["a"] # "first" <-- stale, expected "second" ``` Overwriting *before* the first read works correctly, which is what makes this easy to miss — the broken ordering is the one that looks harmless. ```python def __setitem__(self, key: str, value: Callable[[], _V]): self._factory[key] = value # _dict[key] left holding the old value ``` ## Fix Drop the cached entry when the factory is replaced, so the next access re-evaluates. Laziness and caching are unaffected: a factory still runs at most once per assigned value, and nothing is evaluated until accessed. ## Test Plan Added four tests to `tests/utils_/test_collection_utils.py`: - `test_lazy_dict_is_lazy_and_caches` — nothing evaluated until access; one factory call across two reads (guards against "fixing" this by dropping the cache entirely) - `test_lazy_dict_setitem_replaces_cached_value` — the regression; fails on `main` - `test_lazy_dict_setitem_before_access` — the ordering that already worked stays working - `test_lazy_dict_new_key_and_missing_key` — assignment of a new key, `len`/`iter`, and `KeyError` for a missing key ## Test Result ``` PASS test_lazy_dict_is_lazy_and_caches PASS test_lazy_dict_setitem_replaces_cached_value PASS test_lazy_dict_setitem_before_access PASS test_lazy_dict_new_key_and_missing_key ``` One disclosure on how these were run: I don't have a GPU, and `tests/conftest.py` imports `torch` at module scope, so I couldn't run the file through the repo's normal pytest entry point. I executed the four test bodies directly against `vllm/utils/collection_utils.py` instead, and confirmed the regression test fails without the one-line change. CI is the authority for the full suite.

signal.title: [ROCm][MoE] Split AITER CK and Triton MXFP4 W4A16 into separate backends
signal.text: # [ROCm][MoE] Split AITER CK and Triton MXFP4 W4A16 into separate backends ## Summary Split the overloaded `AITER_MXFP4_BF16` backend into two: - **`AITER_MXFP4_BF16`** → CK only (`AiterExperts`), behavior unchanged (gfx950). - **`AITER_TRITON_MXFP4_BF16`** (new) → aiter Triton `moe_gemm_a16w4` (`AiterW4A16ExpertsMonolithic`), available on gfx942 / gfx950 / gfx1250, selectable via `--moe-backend aiter_triton_mxfp4_bf16` and auto-selected for gpt-oss where CK is unavailable. On gfx942 this makes the Triton path the default for a16w4 (CK's `_supports_quant_scheme` returns False for `kMxfp4Static` off gfx950, so it declines and the next priority entry wins). On gfx950 CK still wins, so this is opt-in there. ## Not a duplicate No open PR splits the CK vs Triton MXFP4-BF16 backends. ## Test results Hardware: AMD MI300X (gfx942). Model: `openai/gpt-oss-120b`. ### Unit tests ``` pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py \ -k "rocm_mxfp4_moe_oracle or emulation_rounds_up or unsupported_reasons or preserves_native_tp_shard" → 9 passed, 2 skipped (AITER_MXFP4_BF16 / AITER_MXFP4_FP8, gfx950-only) ``` `ruff check` and `ruff format --diff` clean on all changed files. ### Accuracy `lm_eval` gsm8k (flexible-extract, TP1): `aiter_triton_mxfp4_bf16` = 0.903 vs `--moe-backend triton` = ~0.906 — parity. GPQA (low, temp 1.0) across TP, this PR vs `--moe-backend triton`: | TP | AITER Triton | OAI Triton | |---|---|---| | 1 | 0.6616 | 0.654–0.669 | | 2 | 0.6496 | 0.667 | | 4 | 0.6528 | 0.6502 | | 8 | 0.6660 | 0.67 | Note: gsm8k **cannot** detect the TP4 defect fixed here (it was 0.903 both ways); GPQA can. Anyone validating this path should use GPQA or watch the harmony non-terminal warning count. ### Performance `vllm bench serve`, random dataset, input 1024 / output 256, `--ignore-eos`, warmup = 2× concurrency (min 16), ≥200 prompts per point (1024 at c=128). Backends interleaved within each TP so machine drift is not confounded with the backend difference. **6720 requests per arm, 0 failed.** Geometric mean of ratios, AITER Triton vs OAI Triton: | metric | all 32 points | favors AITER | TP1 | TP2 | TP4 | TP8 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | Output throughput | **+55.7%** | 30/32 | +55.1% | +49.8% | +56.6% | +61.7% | | TPOT mean | **−39.6%** | **32/32** | −38.7% | −36.7% | −39.3% | −43.7% | | E2EL mean | **−35.8%** | 30/32 | −35.5% | −33.2% | −36.1% | −38.1% | Output throughput by point: | | c=1 | c=8 | c=32 | c=128 | |---|---|---|---|---| | TP1 | +141.7% | +68.3% | +52.6% | **−6.8%** | | TP2 | +141.7% | +63.3% | +48.3% | **−14.0%** | | TP4 | +154.5% | +72.4% | +17.6% | +16.6% | | TP8 | +112.1% | +76.4% | +30.6% | +39.7% | ## AI assistance This change was developed with AI assistance. Andy has reviewed every changed line and run the tests and evals reported above.

signal.title: [Feature] Allow random dataset to use --dataset-path for realistic token sampling
signal.text: ## Motivation When benchmarking speculative decoding, the acceptance rate of draft tokens depends heavily on the token distribution of the input. Currently, the `random` dataset in `vllm bench serve` generates purely random token IDs, which do not represent real-world text distributions. This can understate the effectiveness of speculative decoding in production. On the other hand, the `sharegpt` dataset uses real conversation prompts but does not support `--input-len` to control input length, making it impossible to run benchmarks with a fixed input length using real text. SGLang's benchmark tool already supports this via `--dataset-name random --dataset-path <sharegpt.json> --random-input-len 8192`, which samples tokens from ShareGPT and truncates/repeats them to the requested length. ## Proposal Allow `--dataset-name random` to accept `--dataset-path`. When provided, the random dataset samples token IDs from the file and truncates/repeats them to fill `--random-input-len`. File format is auto-detected from the extension: - `.json` → ShareGPT format (conversations array) - `.jsonl` → one JSON object per line with a "prompt" field - `.txt` → plain text, one line per entry No new CLI arguments are needed. When `--dataset-path` is not provided, the random dataset behaves exactly as before (purely random token IDs). ### Usage ```bash vllm bench serve \ --dataset-name random \ --dataset-path /data/ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json \ --random-input-len 8192 \ --random-output-len 1024 \ --max-concurrency 32 \ --num-prompts 32 ``` ### Why not use existing options? - `--dataset-name random`: supports fixed length but uses purely random tokens, not realistic for speculative decoding benchmarks - `--dataset-name sharegpt`: uses real text but doesn't support `--input-len` - `--dataset-name custom`: requires pre-processing ShareGPT into a JSONL file with truncated/padded prompts, which is inconvenient - `--dataset-name sonnet`: requires a chat template, not compatible with all tokenizers (e.g. DeepSeek-V4)
signal.author: wuhangxian

signal.title: [Bug]: draft_model speculative decoding crashes at init under TP>1 when draft hidden_size > target (TRT-LLM fused allreduce+RMSNorm workspace sized from target only)
signal.text: ### Summary With `draft_model` speculative decoding under tensor parallelism (`TP>1`), the engine crashes at init when the **draft model's `hidden_size` is larger than the target model's**. The `fuse_allreduce_rms` compilation pass builds the FlashInfer TRT-LLM fused allreduce+RMSNorm workspace with a token budget derived from the **target** model's `hidden_size` only. When the draft model then runs its own forward under TP, its larger `hidden_size` overflows that workspace and `check_trtllm_allreduce_fusion_workspace_metadata` raises, aborting startup. `draft_hidden < target_hidden` and `TP=1` both work; the crash is specific to **`draft_hidden > target_hidden` AND `TP>1`**. ### Environment - vLLM `v0.27.1`, V1 engine, `dtype=torch.bfloat16` - 2×H100 PCIe (80GB), `tensor_parallel_size=2` - `compilation_config.pass_config.fuse_allreduce_rms: True` (default), FlashInfer allreduce backend - Full raw server logs for all arms (`collect_env` included): https://github.com/seongyun1104/depthchart/tree/39b1557/draft_model_tp_bug ### Reproduction | Arm | target (TP) | draft | draft_hidden vs target_hidden | result | |-----|-------------|-------|-------------------------------|--------| | A | Qwen3-30B-A3B (**TP=1**) | Qwen3-4B | **2560 > 2048** | OK (acceptance 83.8%, normal) | | B | Qwen3-30B-A3B (**TP=2**) | Qwen3-4B | **2560 > 2048** | **CRASH** at init | | C | Qwen3-30B-A3B (TP=2) | Qwen3-0.6B | 1024 < 2048 | OK (acceptance 73.1%, coherent) | Arm A vs B isolates the trigger to **`TP>1`**: same `draft_hidden > target_hidden` pair, only the parallelism differs. Arm C shows the same TP=2 target is fine when `draft_hidden < target_hidden`. Arm B command (greedy): ``` vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --override-generation-config '{"do_sample": false}' \ --speculative-config '{"method": "draft_model", "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-4B", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}' ``` (Qwen3-4B `hidden_size=2560` as draft; Qwen3-30B-A3B `hidden_size=2048` as target.) ### Traceback (arm B, verbatim) ``` File ".../vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/allreduce_rms_fusion.py", line 265, in call_trtllm_fused_allreduce_norm ... check_trtllm_allreduce_fusion_workspace_metadata( File ".../flashinfer/comm/trtllm_ar.py", line 1026, in check_trtllm_allreduce_fusion_workspace_metadata raise ValueError(error_msg) ValueError: Workspace validation failed: - token_num (8192) * hidden_dim (2560) exceeds workspace max_token_num (8192) * hidden_dim (2048). This may cause Illegal Memory Access. ``` `hidden_dim (2560)` is the draft (Qwen3-4B); the workspace budget `hidden_dim (2048)` is the target (Qwen3-30B-A3B). ### Where it comes from The fused-allreduce workspace token budget is `max_token_num = max_size // (hidden_dim * element_size)`, and `hidden_dim` is taken from the target model config in the pass. The draft model's forward under TP issues the same fused allreduce with its own (larger) `hidden_size`, exceeding the target-sized budget. Note (not a proposed fix): patching the pass `__init__` to use `max(target_hidden, draft_hidden)` did **not** resolve it — the run still reports `hidden_dim (2048)` in the validation error, so the workspace metadata that is actually checked is created upstream of that pass field. A correct fix has to reach the workspace **creation** site so its stored `hidden_dim` accounts for the draft model. ### Relationship to #50877 / #50932 Same theme (FlashInfer allreduce workspace/buffer under a draft model that adds allreduce traffic), but a **distinct backend**: - #50877 / PR #50932 — the **MNNVL** path (`trtllm_mnnvl_ar`, Lamport buffer rotation); #50932 touches `flashinfer_all_reduce.py` / `fused_allreduce_gemma_rms_norm.py` and adds an `is_buffer_size_sufficient` admission guard. - This report — the **TRT-LLM fused allreduce+RMSNorm** compilation-pass path (`allreduce_rms_fusion.py` → `flashinfer/comm/trtllm_ar.py`), which #50932 does not touch. Filing separately so the TRT-LLM path is tracked; happy to fold into #50877 if maintainers prefer a single tracking issue.
