signal.title: [Kimi-K3][AMD] Return KDA and MLA projection outputs directly
signal.text: ## Purpose Kimi-K3's AMD attention paths copied each output projection into a caller-owned buffer even though the projection already returns a tensor with the required shape, dtype, layout, and lifetime. This PR removes that redundant post-projection allocation and copy from both attention families: - 69 KDA layers - 24 MLA layers - 93 post-attention-projection copies per model step in total The functionality from #50847 is now folded into this PR. #50654 is separate and complementary: it optimizes the earlier KDA recurrent/conv/RMSNorm path, while this PR removes the later copy after the output projection. ## Implementation - Return KDA output-projection storage directly from both the shared KDA implementation and the dedicated full-rank Kimi-K3 implementation selected by current `main`. - Return MLA output-projection storage directly. - Use one return-value contract in `KimiDecoderLayer` for KDA and MLA. - Preserve attention arithmetic, state updates, normalization, projection, tensor-parallel communication, and HIP-graph replay behavior. ## Validation ```text Targeted ownership tests: 3 passed Ruff 0.14.0 check: passed Ruff 0.14.0 format check: passed git diff --check: passed DCO: passed ``` The tests cover KDA dispatch ownership, the concrete full-rank Kimi-K3 KDA forward path, and MLA dispatch ownership. In each case, the returned tensor is the exact projection tensor and has the same `data_ptr()`. ## Fixed-cohort decode A/B ### Setup ```text GPU: 8 x AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950) Parallelism: TP8 Model: Kimi-K3, BF16 activations / MXFP4 weights Decode: non-speculative Prefix caching: enabled Prompt: 63,911-token shared prefix + 4,089-token suffix Output: 1,024 tokens per request, ignore EOS Concurrency: C16 and C24 fixed cohorts HIP graph: FULL, capture sizes 1/16/24 Sampling: greedy, seed 42 Runs: 1 warmup + 3 measured runs per concurrency and variant Success rate: 240/240 measured requests ``` Both variants used image `localhost/kimi-pp8-upstream-clean` (vLLM `beca88e59`, AITER `99733dc00`). The baseline was the unmodified image. The candidate mounted only this PR's AMD runtime files from `43d81ba3e`. The relevant AMD Kimi-K3 files in the image are identical to the rebased `main` baseline before this PR. ### Results Means over three measured runs. TPOT and ITL are end-to-end serving metrics, not the reviewer's pure-GPU trace period. | Cohort | Metric | Baseline | Combined PR | Delta | |---|---|---:|---:|---:| | C16 | Mean TPOT | 73.141 ms | 72.428 ms | **-0.713 ms (-0.97%)** | | C16 | Median ITL | 70.488 ms | 70.186 ms | **-0.302 ms** | | C16 | Output throughput | 193.575 tok/s | 195.555 tok/s | **+1.02%** | | C24 | Mean TPOT | 74.958 ms | 74.457 ms | **-0.501 ms (-0.67%)** | | C24 | Median ITL | 71.311 ms | 70.916 ms | **-0.396 ms** | | C24 | Output throughput | 278.245 tok/s | 280.452 tok/s | **+0.79%** | Mean-TPOT standard deviation across the three runs was 0.184 ms / 0.348 ms for baseline C16/C24 and 0.019 ms / 0.122 ms for candidate C16/C24. ### Interpretation The reviewer's trace found that the complete 93-copy group costs approximately 0.495 ms at C16 and 0.563 ms at C24. C16 is modestly larger, which is plausible because returning projection storage directly also changes allocator and lifetime behavior; the baseline's run-to-run variance is also higher. The absolute TPOT values should not be compared directly with the reviewer's 32.82/35.98 ms pure-GPU periods because TPOT includes serving and scheduling overhead. signal.title: [Bugfix] Pick the DeepSeek V4 eager cudagraph region per model runner
signal.text: #51430 narrowed the DeepSeek V4 eager cudagraph region, which corrupts MRV1 output, and #51768 responded by defaulting the model to MRV2 and rejecting MRV1 + PIECEWISE. That default costs ROCm, where MRV1 is still the faster runner for this model. Choose the region from the runner instead: MRV1 wraps the whole attention body in `_prepare_and_attn_eager`, restoring the pre-#51430 region it needs, while MRV2 keeps the narrow region and its shorter TTFT. The nested `_sparse_indexer_and_attn` break runs inline, since `add_eager` clears `_capturing` first. MRV1 + PIECEWISE is then correct on every platform, so drop the rejection. CUDA still defaults to MRV2; ROCm defaults to MRV1 until MRV2 is competitive there. Claude was used to help.

signal.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Keep EAGLE cache registration on the partial-hash-hit path
signal.text: ## Purpose `HybridKVCacheCoordinator.cache_blocks` decides once how far a request may be registered in the prefix-cache hash map. With fine-grained partial hash hits that bound is the raw token count, because a hit no longer has to land on a `scheduler_block_size` boundary. #50062 rewrote the EAGLE branch to re-derive its own bound from `num_finalized_computed_tokens` with an unconditional ```python // self.scheduler_block_size * self.scheduler_block_size ``` so the rounding comes back on the one path that had removed it. Registration is then capped at `floor(n / scheduler_block_size) * scheduler_block_size + manager.block_size` instead of `n`, and everything between the last aligned boundary and the tail stops being registered — `(n % scheduler_block_size) - manager.block_size` tokens per call, which is most of a segment whenever the group's own block is much smaller than the scheduler block. Only EAGLE-family groups take that branch, so a model without speculative decoding never sees it. This routes both bounds through one helper, `_align_cacheable`, so the exemption cannot be lost again by re-deriving it in a second place. **Reachability.** `enable_partial_hash_hits` requires a Mamba `"align"` group with `block_size > hash_block_size`, prefix caching, and `dcp_world_size == 1`. `mamba_cache_mode` is a `cache_config` knob rather than a model property, so any hybrid Mamba model served with `--mamba-cache-mode align` and an EAGLE-family drafter reaches this path; the remaining condition — every group's manager supporting fine-grained lookup — holds automatically for the full-attention + Mamba pair. A stock `dcp_world_size == 1` hybrid model with EAGLE-family speculative decoding is affected as written. We run that path under DCP > 1 through a local carry, which is why we hit it on every run. **Out of scope, flagged for a reviewer.** The soundness guard `scheduler_block_size >= num_prefill_lookahead` is justified in its comment by "hits land on scheduler-block boundaries", which holds only when `enable_partial_hash_hits` is off — `_cache_hit_alignment_tokens` returns `hash_block_size` when it is on. That guard predates this change and only matters for multi-module MTP on a hybrid Mamba model, a combination we do not run and cannot measure, so it is left alone rather than adjusted on a guess. ### Not a duplicate No open PR addresses this. The nearest neighbours, checked before opening: - #46384 — the partial prefix-cache hit feature itself - #45702 — its design RFC - #50438 — RFC: lookahead-aware prefix-cache hashing for EAGLE-style drafters, the closest in subject but a proposal for different hashing, not this bug - #49125 — a different bug in the same area (stale partial hash revival) ### AI assistance This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude). I reviewed every changed line, ran the tests below myself, and can defend the change end to end. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py -k eagle_group_registers_unaligned_tail pytest tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/ pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -k clamped_to_lcm pytest tests/v1/core/ # before/after, to check nothing else moves ``` End to end: Kimi-K3 MXFP4 (hybrid, 24 MLA + 69 KDA layers), 8x B300, TP8, DSpark speculative decoding with `num_speculative_tokens=7`, agentic replay workload, 60 minutes per point. ## Test Result The new test fails on the parent commit (`acb0f1dcdb`) and passes with the fix. The failure is the arithmetic above: the EAGLE group registers `floor(22/8)*8 + 2 = 18` tokens where it should register 22. ``` > assert recorded == [num_tokens] * len(coordinator.single_type_managers) E assert [18, 22] == [22, 22] E At index 0 diff: 18 != 22 1 failed, 24 deselected ``` ``` tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/ 25 passed tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -k clamped_to_lcm 1 passed ``` `tests/v1/core/` in full, same command on both trees: **+1 passed, −1 failed, no other test changes state.** The one that moves is the new test. My sandbox cannot import the compiled extensions, so a large fixed set of tests in that directory errors out identically on both trees and is not informative here; the targeted suites above are the ones that run clean. End to end, one 60-minute run per cell: | concurrency | before #50062 | with #50062 | with this fix | |---|---|---|---| | 8 | 5,146 tok/s/GPU | 4,767 (−7.4%) | **5,183** (+0.7%) | | 16 | 7,669 tok/s/GPU | 6,611 (−13.8%) | **7,654** (−0.2%) | GPU prefix-cache hit rate at concurrency 16: **86.3% → 77.4% → 86.2%**. The non-speculative arm of the same ladder is unaffected throughout (13 points from concurrency 1 to 78, all within −1.3% to +1.8%). The regressed pair was repeated and the two runs agreed to within 0.3%. ### Effect on output The change only widens which already-computed tokens may be registered in the hash map; it does not alter what is computed, what a hit returns, or the correctness conditions #50062 added (`num_reprefillable_tokens` still excludes re-prefillable tail tokens, and the EAGLE last-block drop is untouched). Output is bit-identical in the sense that no sampling path changes; the measured effect is throughput and prefix-hit rate only. No accuracy evaluation was run, and none is claimed. For scale on this model: `TOKENSPEED_MLA` sets `block_size=32` and the attention block is forced to 1536 to cover the mamba page. The unregistered part of a prefix tail is `(n % 1536) - 32`, so up to **1,503** tokens go unregistered per call — 1,472 when `n` is a multiple of 32.

signal.title: [ROCm][DSV4][Perf] Step 1/N: Port ATOM attention into vLLM: port single-node single-token-prediction case
signal.text: ## Purpose Step 1/N of porting AMD **ATOM**'s DeepSeek-V4 hybrid attention into vLLM on ROCm. This step vendors the ATOM DeepSeek-V4 attention subsystem and wires it into the existing in-tree ROCm DeepSeek-V4 model as an **env-gated** alternative (`VLLM_DSV4_USE_ATOM`, default on) to the current ROCm MLA attention path. **Scope of this step** (kept deliberately small; more to follow): - Single node, **TP=8 / EP=1** with DP-attention, gfx950, fp8 KV cache. - **Single-token prediction only** — no MTP / speculative decode, no prefill/decode disaggregation, no prefill context parallelism. **Integration.** The ATOM attention runs as a single vLLM proxy `AttentionBackend` / `AttentionLayerBase`: vLLM's pager owns the classical KV storage (via a `FullAttentionSpec`), and the bridge slices ATOM's unified SWA-ring + CSA/HCA compressed views out of that storage, re-deriving ATOM's V4 attention metadata from vLLM's `CommonAttentionMetadata` each forward. Only the per-layer attention module is swapped — vLLM's embeddings / MoE / head / weight loading are reused as-is. The vendored code is kept ATOM-native (imports repointed to the vendored root, not rewritten to vLLM conventions) so it can track upstream ATOM. Dead-for-this-scope paths (PCP, dual-stream MoE, other-model norm/linear variants) were trimmed. ## Test Plan The main env switch for ATOM attention path: `export VLLM_DSV4_USE_ATOM=1` - Model `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`, TP=8, fp8 KV cache, gfx950; served via the OpenAI-compatible server with `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` and async scheduling. - `lm-eval` GSM8K, comparing the ATOM path against the in-tree ROCm MLA path (`VLLM_DSV4_USE_ATOM=0`). ## Test Result

signal.title: [ROCm][Perf] Use AITER tgemm for DeepSeek V4 compressors
signal.text: ## Summary Use AITER tuned BF16 GEMMs for the DeepSeek V4 main and optional indexer `fused_wkv_wgate` compressor projections on `gfx950`. The optimized path is intentionally limited to FULL CUDA-graph execution with `M <= 4`, where `M` is the compressor projection row count. Larger shapes, PIECEWISE graphs, and eager execution retain the original FP32-output `torch.mm` path. This changes the two compressor score outputs from FP32 to BF16 only on that optimized path. AITER remains opt-in through `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`; users can retain the original compressor path with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_LINEAR=0`. ## Implementation - Cache hardware, AITER, compressor, and weight-dtype eligibility at initialization so non-dynamic predicates are not repeated per layer and forward pass. - Route eligible BF16 projections to AITER tgemm only during FULL graph capture/replay when `M <= 4`. - Check the dynamic row count before the CUDA-graph runtime mode so larger batches also skip that repeated context lookup. - Override only the existing `attn_gemm_parallel_execute` input-GEMM hook. Reuse its inherited path and existing attention boundary for `M > 4`, PIECEWISE graphs, and eager execution. - Reuse the shared DeepSeek V4 forward implementation; no ROCm-specific graph decorator, capture hook, or alternate attention forward is added. - Call the polymorphic `_fused_wqa_wkv_gemm()` helper so FP8 preshuffled projections remain correct. - Add focused coverage for runtime mode, row count, cached eligibility, input dtype, both compressor weights, and the inherited tuple contract. `M <= 4` is the range where the current DSV4 AITER table has tuned entries for both compressor projections. In the same-base serving sweep, unrestricted tgemm improved CONC=4, was neutral at CONC=8, and regressed throughput by 8.23%, 10.91%, and 7.61% at CONC=16, 32, and 64 respectively. The bounded path preserves the low-concurrency optimization without those larger-batch regressions. An earlier all-runtime-mode version was also evaluated and rejected. At CONC=4 it reached 154.462 output tok/s, 8.99% below its supplied 169.714 tok/s baseline, because PIECEWISE execution exposed 132 per-forward tgemm dispatches to the CPU. Keeping the optimization inside FULL graphs removes that repeated dispatch overhead. The unrestricted CONC=128 run also encountered an HSA memory-access fault when the indexer projection selected its M=128 ASM split-K kernel. Separately, [ROCm/aiter#4494](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4494) tracks an ASM split-K semaphore deadlock under graph capture. That upstream report supports avoiding the larger captured ASM path for now, but it does not prove that its reported deadlock caused the HSA fault observed here. ## Duplicate-work check No issue number was supplied, so an issue-specific lookup was not applicable. Open-PR searches for `DeepSeek V4 AITER tgemm`, `compressor tgemm`, and `DeepSeek V4 compressor ROCm` found no other PR implementing this change. The closest open work is materially different: - [#23712](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/23712) integrates AITER tgemm into generic linear layers; these compressor projections use direct `torch.mm` calls and are not routed through that integration. - [#46699](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46699) adds an opt-in HIP path that fuses the broader compressor, normalization, RoPE, quantization, and cache-storage pipeline; this PR only replaces two BF16 projection GEMMs. ## Tests - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py -q` — 49 passed. - `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/rocm.py tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py` — all hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy, and DCO sign-off checks. ## Performance and model evaluation The side-by-side comparison uses the branch's exact parent, `821717118fc26667dd474b9b0ab81d29259dfc5c`, as the baseline and `aaa3fee24014237015e6b9578f28c7f21b8034bc` as the PR revision. Both sides used fresh servers in the same refreshed container, editable environment, model weights, and server configuration. Settings: DeepSeek-V4-Pro, TP=8, `gpu-memory-utilization=0.8`, random 8K-input/1K-output requests, `random-range-ratio=0.8`, `seed=0`, `ignore-eos`, `2 * CONC` warmups, and `10 * CONC` measured requests. Each fresh server received one discarded CONC=4 preconditioning pass before its recorded sweep. The baseline and PR used pairwise-identical input/output token-length arrays. | CONC | Requests | Input / output tokens | Output tok/s, baseline → PR (Δ) | Mean TPOT ms, baseline → PR (Δ) | Mean TTFT ms, baseline → PR (Δ) | Mean E2E ms, baseline → PR (Δ) | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4 | 40 | 294,050 / 36,805 | 185.450 → 193.110 (+4.13%) | 20.566 → 19.729 (+4.07%) | 461.732 → 467.166 (-1.18%) | 19,366.683 → 18,600.765 (+3.95%) | | 8 | 80 | 584,809 / 74,069 | 318.593 → 321.202 (+0.82%) | 23.829 → 23.708 (+0.51%) | 755.531 → 711.015 (+5.89%) | 22,854.103 → 22,682.563 (+0.75%) | | 16 | 160 | 1,175,032 / 146,426 | 558.039 → 557.572 (-0.08%) | 26.960 → 26.986 (-0.09%) | 718.614 → 744.293 (-3.57%) | 25,388.323 → 25,433.095 (-0.18%) | | 32 | 320 | 2,352,062 / 296,143 | 832.600 → 839.829 (+0.87%) | 35.983 → 35.807 (+0.49%) | 1,300.083 → 1,188.915 (+8.55%) | 34,625.384 → 34,343.454 (+0.81%) | | 64 | 640 | 4,727,544 / 589,927 | 1,095.010 → 1,098.108 (+0.28%) | 54.877 → 54.966 (-0.16%) | 2,354.723 → 2,112.954 (+10.27%) | 52,980.846 → 52,827.137 (+0.29%) | | 128 | 1,280 | 9,454,961 / 1,177,736 | 1,340.538 → 1,404.579 (+4.78%) | 89.562 → 85.772 (+4.23%) | 4,231.753 → 3,707.103 (+12.40%) | 86,711.682 → 82,711.240 (+4.61%) | The output-throughput geometric-mean gain across the six concurrency points is **+1.78%**. CONC=128 completed all 1,280 requests without the HSA fault seen with unrestricted tgemm. For throughput, delta is `(PR / baseline - 1) * 100`; for latency, delta is `(baseline - PR) / baseline * 100`. Positive values therefore indicate improvement. Final-head GSM8K, 5-shot greedy, 1,319 examples: - strict match: **1,267/1,319 (96.0576%)** - flexible extract: **1,266/1,319 (95.9818%)** Both scores match the prior baseline exactly. ## AI assistance disclosure OpenAI Codex assisted with review-comment analysis, simplifying the implementation, running tests and model evaluations, benchmarking, and drafting this description. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and can understand and defend the change end-to-end.

signal.title: [Bug]: disagg_epd_proxy encoder fan-out restarts round-robin per request, overloading first encoder
signal.text: ### Your current environment NA ### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Problem In `examples/disaggregated/disaggregated_encoder/disagg_epd_proxy.py`, encoder requests are distributed with: ```python # Round-robin over encode servers to distribute load a bit url_cycle = (e_urls[i % len(e_urls)] for i in range(len(mm_items))) ``` This is only round-robin within a single incoming request. Since `i` always starts at `0` for every request, `e_urls[0]` receives the first multimodal item of every request. If most requests contain one image/audio item, then all encoder traffic goes to the first encoder instance. If most requests contain fewer multimodal items than encoder instances, later encoder instances receive little or no traffic. ### Example With 3 encoder instances: ```text Request with 1 image -> E0 Request with 1 image -> E0 Request with 1 image -> E0 ``` With 2 images per request: ```text Request 1 -> E0, E1 Request 2 -> E0, E1 Request 3 -> E0, E1 ``` `E2` is never selected in the second case. ### Expected Behavior The proxy should distribute encoder sub-requests fairly across encoder instances over time, not restart from `e_urls[0]` for every incoming request. ### Possible Fixes One option is to maintain a global round-robin cursor, for example: ```python start = app.state.encoder_rr_idx app.state.encoder_rr_idx = (app.state.encoder_rr_idx + len(mm_items)) % len(e_urls) url_cycle = (e_urls[(start + i) % len(e_urls)] for i in range(len(mm_items))) ``` Because the proxy is async, this should probably be protected with an `asyncio.Lock` or replaced with another concurrency-safe strategy. Another simpler option is to choose an encoder randomly per multimodal item: ```python target_url = random.choice(e_urls) ``` This avoids hot-spotting `e_urls[0]`, although it is not deterministic round-robin. ### Affected File `examples/disaggregated/disaggregated_encoder/disagg_epd_proxy.py` ### Additional Context The current comment says “Round-robin over encode servers,” but the implementation is only per-request modulo assignment. This can lead to uneven encoder load in common single-image request workloads. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

Container image is a community build (`ghcr.io/spark-arena/dgx-vllm-eugr-nightly`), but the affected code is stock `vllm` under `/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/`, not anything the image itself patches. ### 🐛 Describe the bug The Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages` endpoint crashes whenever a client sends a `tool_result` content block whose `content` array includes an Anthropic `tool_reference` item. This happens organically with Claude Code sessions that have a large number of tools available (multiple MCP servers configured), where the Anthropic API's tool-search/dynamic-tool-discovery beta feature lets a tool result reference another tool by name instead of re-embedding its full definition. Once a `tool_reference` block appears anywhere in a conversation's history, every subsequent request in that conversation fails — the coding agent gets no further responses. **Root cause:** `_convert_user_tool_result` in [`vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py) converts every other known item type (`text`, `image`) into a template-safe OpenAI content item, but for `tool_reference` it appends the **raw, unconverted** Anthropic-shaped block instead: ```python elif item_type == "tool_reference": ref_name = item.get("tool_name") or item.get("name") if ref_name: tool_reference.append( {"type": "tool_reference", "name": ref_name} ) ... if tool_reference: openai_messages.append( { "role": "tool", "tool_call_id": block.tool_use_id or "", "content": tool_reference, # <-- raw Anthropic-shaped items, never converted } ) ``` That raw `{"type": "tool_reference", "name": ...}` dict is handed straight to the model's chat template as the `content` of a `tool`-role message. Most Jinja chat templates (including Qwen3's, confirmed here) only understand content items shaped like `{"type": "text", "text": ...}` or `{"type": "image"/"image_url", ...}`; anything else falls through to a catch-all `raise_exception(...)` branch, so the request fails regardless of which model is served. **Minimal reproduction** (isolates the chat-template layer directly — no server needed, just the model's own tokenizer, reproducing exactly the content shape vLLM's converter produces): ```python from transformers import AutoTokenizer import traceback tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4") # This is exactly the shape vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py's # _convert_user_tool_result() produces for a tool_result block containing # a tool_reference item: the raw Anthropic-shaped dict is passed straight # through as OpenAI-style chat message content, unconverted. messages = [ {"role": "user", "content": "What tools do I have available?"}, { "role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "toolu_01abc123", "content": [ {"type": "tool_reference", "name": "some_mcp_tool"} ], }, ] try: tok.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True) print("NO ERROR (unexpected)") except Exception: traceback.print_exc() ``` **Observed output** (run against the model on disk in this deployment): ``` Traceback (most recent call last): File "/tmp/repro_template.py", line 22, in tok.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True) File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py", line 3108, in apply_chat_template rendered_chat, generation_indices = render_jinja_template( ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/transformers/utils/chat_template_utils.py", line 581, in render_jinja_template rendered_chat = compiled_template.render( ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/jinja2/environment.py", line 1295, in render self.environment.handle_exception() File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/jinja2/environment.py", line 942, in handle_exception raise rewrite_traceback_stack(source=source) File "

signal.title: fix: mask premature eos during reasoning
signal.text: PLEASE FILL IN THE PR DESCRIPTION HERE ENSURING ALL CHECKLIST ITEMS (AT THE BOTTOM) HAVE BEEN CONSIDERED. ## Purpose Addresses the premature EOS sub-issue in vllm-project/vllm-ascend#14031, where generation can stop while reasoning is still open. This PR adds an opt-in `ReasoningConfig.premature_eos_policy` with `mask_in_reasoning`. When enabled, vLLM masks the primary EOS token before sampling while the request is inside an unfinished reasoning span, and restores EOS after the natural reasoning end token is observed. The implementation reuses `ThinkingBudgetStateHolder` and also covers requests without `thinking_token_budget`. ## Test Plan ```bash git diff --check python -m py_compile vllm/config/reasoning.py \ vllm/v1/sample/thinking_budget_state.py \ tests/v1/logits_processors/test_correctness.py pytest tests/v1/logits_processors/test_correctness.py \ -k "eos_in_open_reasoning or unmasks_eos_after_reasoning_end or spec_rows_until_reasoning_end" ## Test Result - git diff --check: passed - py_compile: passed - Added focused unit coverage for: - masking EOS in open reasoning without thinking budget - unmasking EOS after reasoning end - spec-decode row-wise masking until reasoning end Local full pytest collection was blocked by environment dependency mismatch (openai.types.responses.NamespaceTool unavailable), not by the changed code.

signal.title: [Core] Keep client stop strings dormant inside the reasoning segment
signal.text: FIX #52393 ## Problem When a model emits reasoning inline in the same text stream (think-in-prompt deployments, e.g. DeepSeek-V4 with `--reasoning-parser deepseek_v4`), client-supplied `stop` strings are evaluated against the reasoning text too. A stop string that legitimately appears while the model is thinking (restating the user's question, quoting a delimiter) truncates the response inside the reasoning segment — the reasoning parser then never sees the end-marker, and the API returns `content: None` with the visible answer lost. Details and reproduction in #52393. ## Fix `BaseIncrementalDetokenizer` now arms a per-request guard (`reasoning_stop_guard`) when the request carries stop strings and the deployment has a reasoning parser with a known end marker. While armed: - stop strings stay dormant until the reasoning end marker (`</think>`) has been observed in the output stream; - once the marker lands, stop evaluation resumes from the character offset immediately after the marker (handles the marker and post-marker content arriving in one decode step, e.g. under speculative decoding); - requests without stop strings, or deployments without a reasoning parser, take the existing code path unchanged. `min_tokens` and EOS/token-id stopping are unaffected; only client stop-string matching is deferred. ## Testing - 4 new tests in `tests/v1/engine/test_stop_in_reasoning.py` (dormant-in-reasoning, one-chunk marker+content close, non-reasoning requests unchanged, marker split across decode steps) — all pass. - Logic additionally validated end-to-end against a GB10 two-node DeepSeek-V4-Flash deployment where the truncation reproduces; with the guard, hostile stop strings inside reasoning no longer truncate, and stops still fire in the visible answer. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: [Bug]: Client stop strings match inside the reasoning segment for think-in-prompt models, truncating CoT and yielding content=None
signal.text: ### Your current environment Reproduced on 0.21.1 and 0.25.2.dev (V1 engine), 2x DGX Spark GB10 TP=2, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 with `--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4` and `--reasoning-config '{"reasoning_parser":"deepseek_v4","reasoning_start_str":"<think>","reasoning_end_str":"</think>"}'`. The mechanism is model-agnostic for any think-in-prompt template (DeepSeek V4, Qwen3-style). ### 🐛 Describe the bug With think-in-prompt templates, generation begins INSIDE the reasoning segment. The V1 detokenizer evaluates client `stop` strings against the whole output stream, so a stop string that the chain-of-thought naturally restates fires mid-`<think>`: `</think>` never arrives, the reasoning parser cannot close the segment, and the response returns `content: None` with `finish_reason: stop`. This is easy to hit unintentionally at scale: lm-evaluation-harness sends `stop[:4]` (e.g. `"Question:"`) on every request, and CoT loves restating `Question:`. On GSM8K n=50 at temp 0.6 we measured 8-15/50 responses decapitated this way (score 0.66-0.84); with stops suppressed inside reasoning it dropped to 1/50 nulls (0.98). Hosted deployments of the same checkpoints are immune because they scope stops to content — that behavior gap is the bug. It also masquerades as a model failure ("the model returned nothing"), which cost the community significant misdiagnosis time (see tonyd2wild/DeepSeek-v4-Flash-0731-DSpark-1M-NVFP4-KV-2x-DGX-Spark issue #18, where ~30% of eval nulls traced to this). ### Repro sketch 1. Serve any think-in-prompt reasoning model with a reasoning parser configured. 2. Send a request whose prompt ends inside `<think>` (standard chat template behavior with thinking enabled) plus `stop: ["Question:"]` and a prompt the model will deliberate about. 3. When the CoT restates "Question:", the response truncates mid-reasoning: no `</think>`, `content: None`. ### Expected behavior Stop strings should stay dormant while the reasoning segment is open and be evaluated only against text FOLLOWING the reasoning end marker (matching hosted-API behavior). EOS and max_tokens unaffected; non-thinking requests untouched. One subtlety for spec decoding: `update()` receives up to k+1 tokens per step, so the chunk that carries the end marker also carries the reasoning that precedes it — on closing, the stop-check offset must advance past the marker or a stop in the last <=k reasoning tokens still fires. ### Existing community fix A per-request guard implementing exactly this (markers from `--reasoning-config` with `<think>`/`</think>` fallback, process-wide opt-out env var, spec-decode one-chunk handling) has been running in production in the DSpark community for 10+ days across vLLM 0.21.1 and a 0.25.2.dev port: patch at tonyd2wild/DeepSeek-v4-Flash-0731-DSpark-1M-NVFP4-KV-2x-DGX-Spark `patches/0005-suppress-stops-in-reasoning.patch` (and PR #32 there for 0.25.x trees). Happy to adapt it into a proper vLLM PR with tests if maintainers agree with the direction — main design question is whether the guard should be default-on (hosted-parity) or opt-in via a sampling/serving flag. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: [Kernel] Prefer fused A16WFP4 with cached MXFP4 emulation fallback
signal.text: ## Summary Add a three-level ROCm MXFP4 linear fallback while preserving the existing native backend priority: 1. existing native AITER A4W4 remains first; 2. on gfx950, if the FlyDSL fused A16WFP4 API from ROCm/aiter#4772 is available, preshuffle and retain packed E2M1 weights plus E8M0 scales once, apply activation QDQ, then run fused weight decode + BF16 MFMA; 3. otherwise cache the decoded BF16 weight once at model load, as in the original version of this PR. Set `VLLM_MXFP4_EMULATION_DEQUANT_AT_LOAD=0` to retain the original packed per-call dequantization path. Explicit `emulation` backend selection also remains explicit emulation. ## Motivation The generic MXFP4 emulation fallback otherwise repeats full weight dequantization for every linear invocation. Load-time BF16 caching removes that repeated work but increases device memory. When the optional fused A16WFP4 kernel is installed, the packed representation can remain resident and each tile is decoded transiently inside the GEMM. ```text native A4W4 available -> native A4W4 otherwise, gfx950 fused A16WFP4 available -> cache preshuffled packed MXFP4 -> activation QDQ -> fused BF16 MFMA otherwise -> cache decoded BF16 weight -> activation QDQ -> F.linear ``` The fused API is imported only after model workers are initialized, so old AITER installations and engine-core fork remain safe. Missing APIs, unsupported shapes, FP16 model parameters, and preparation errors fall back to cached BF16 rather than failing startup. ## Scope The generic MXFP4 kernel oracle makes this available to Quark, compressed-tensors, ModelOpt, online quantization, and other callers using dynamic MXFP4 activations. Native MXFP4 kernels and fused-MoE execution are unchanged. Kimi-K3 dense/shared linear scope: - layer 0 dense MLP: `gate_proj`, `up_proj`, `down_proj` - layers 1-92 shared experts: `gate_proj`, `up_proj`, `down_proj` - routed experts remain in the fused-MoE path - self-attention linears remain FP8 ## Validation - `41 passed`: focused CPU selection, lifecycle, QDQ, preshuffle, reshape/bias and fallback tests - `1 passed`: real gfx950 fused A16WFP4 correctness test - native A4W4 priority preserved - API/FlyDSL missing, FP16, alignment and preparation-failure BF16-cache fallback covered - packed per-call opt-out covered - Ruff, format, `py_compile`, and `git diff --check` passed AITER #4772 validation: 13 gfx950 tests passed. Against canonical MXFP4 weight decode + BF16 `F.linear`, relative L2 was 0.001118%-0.001776% and exact agreement was 99.9924%-99.9996%. The fused kernel was 1.75x-4.86x faster than the measured existing Triton path while packed weights plus scales used 73.44% less storage than cached BF16. ## Existing cached-emulation evidence Historical Kimi-K3 model-level measurements: - older runtime con1 TPOT: `402.43 ms` full emulation -> `90.97 ms` cached emulation - older runtime con4 TPOT: `177.14 ms` -> `109.98 ms` - newer ROCm/AITER runtime: `22.551 ms` cached shared/dense fallback vs `22.995 ms` BF16 (`-1.93%`) GSM8K 8-shot: - official emulation: `96.36%` flexible / `96.36%` strict - routed A8W4 plus cached dense fallback: `96.29%` / `96.36%` Observed cached-BF16 trade-off on Kimi-K3: - approximately `+1.5 GiB` resident dequantized-weight memory - approximately `3.43 GiB` less memory available for KV cache The fused A16WFP4 route avoids that persistent BF16 weight expansion by retaining the one-time preshuffled packed layout.

signal.title: [Core] Release NCCL communicator memory in sleep mode
signal.text: ## Replacement for #46234 This recreates #46234, which became unreopenable after its fork was detached. The original PR was not closed for a technical reason; all its review threads were resolved. ## What Sleep mode releases weights and KV-cache memory, but NCCL communicators retain their dynamic GPU buffers (~1 GiB/rank at TP4). This change releases that memory during sleep via NCCL's native `ncclCommSuspend(NCCL_SUSPEND_MEM)` / `ncclCommResume`, preserving communicator identity, topology, and connection state. Requires NCCL >= 2.29.7 (the vllm/vllm-openai image pins 2.30.7; the CUDA test lock 2.29.7). ## How (updated architecture) - `suspend()` / `resume()` hooks on `DeviceCommunicatorBase` (the generic surface requested in [#46234 review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46234#discussion_r3504640029), ready for FlashInfer comm suspension); `CudaCommunicator` delegates to PyNccl. - `PyNcclCommunicator.suspend/resume` are **idempotent** (`_suspended` state). - Orchestration lives in the shared worker dispatch layer (`gpu_worker.sleep/wake_up`) — the same placement #46234 was reviewed with — gated by a new `SleepModeBackend.requires_communicator_suspend()` capability (`cumem` → True; process-checkpoint mechanisms that cover NCCL themselves → False, avoiding double handling). PyNccl-level idempotence makes staged wakes safe: each communicator suspends and resumes exactly once, and the worker holds no extra state. This differs from the first push of this PR, which called the walkers from inside `CuMemBackend`. That shape had a layer inversion (allocator module importing `parallel_state`) and a reproducible crash: the staged RL wake (`/wake_up?tags=weights` → `/wake_up?tags=kv_cache`) called `ncclCommResume` twice, and the second call fails with `invalid usage`, killing the engine (`EngineDeadError`). Reproduced on GB200 TP4; fixed here by the PyNccl idempotence guard (unit-tested), with 7 edge scenarios (wake-without-sleep, double sleep, staged wake, mid-walk failure recovery, capability-off parity, XPU, TP=1) adversarially verified safe. ## Test - Unit: `tests/v1/worker/test_sleep_mode_backend.py` (9 passed) covers the capability contract and staged-wake single-resume ordering; `tests/distributed/test_pynccl.py::test_pynccl_suspend_resume_idempotent` covers the low-level guard. Pre-commit incl. mypy green. - E2E on 1×(4×GB200), vllm/vllm-openai:nightly, NCCL 2.30.7: full sleep/wake cycle and staged wake (weights → kv_cache), greedy 64-token output compared token-exact before/after. | Model | TP | NCCL freed/rank | Sleep L1 total freed/rank | Output preserved (full + staged wake) | |---|---|---|---|---| | Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking | 4 | 1152 MiB (2 comms: tp, ep) | 155.24 GiB | ✓ | | NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16 | 4 | 1152 MiB | 152.26 GiB | ✓ | Original #46234 validation (8×H200, TP2/4/8 ± EP/DP/PP, 958–1438 MiB/rank, output preserved) applies to the unchanged NCCL mechanism. **Additional GSM8K correctness pass, single-node TP4 and cross-node TP8** (vllm/vllm-openai:nightly, Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507, 200 questions/run, `--moe-backend TRITON`; checkpoint loaded from `/dev/shm` — Lustre client-side cache tops out well under this model's 56.87 GiB checkpoint, so `--safetensors-load-strategy prefetch` stalls at 0% indefinitely on a network filesystem for a model this size, unrelated to this PR): | Topology | Comm memory released (per rank, both sleep cycles) | `invalid_rate` | Errors/tracebacks | |---|---|---|---| | TP4, single node | `Sleep mode freed 155.22 GiB` then `152.82 GiB` | 0.0000 (600/600 answers parsed) | none | | TP8, cross-node (2×4×GB200) | `Sleep mode freed 151.51 GiB`, `CuMemAllocator: sleep freed 149.10 GiB` — consistent across all 8 ranks on both hosts | 0.0000 (600/600 answers parsed) | none | Both runs show baseline/post-full-wake/post-staged-wake accuracy within ±1 question (TP4) or ±9 questions (TP8, out of 200) of each other — expected batch-composition floating-point non-associativity for greedy decoding under concurrent load, not output corruption (zero invalid/unparseable answers, zero errors across both runs). The TP8 cross-node run also empirically confirms the FlashInfer limitation above: `Failed to initialize FlashInfer All Reduce workspace: CUDA error code=800 (CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED)` — a non-fatal warning, vLLM falls back cleanly and this PR's NCCL-only release is unaffected. Cluster caveat, unrelated to this PR's code: this rack is GB200 NVL72 with MNNVL (rack-scale NVLink fabric), but the site's Slurm/Pyxis container build has no device-injection option for the IMEX channel — confirmed by bind-mounting `/dev/nvidia-caps-imex-channels` into the container (visible via `nvidia-smi -L`, host IMEX daemon healthy) and still hitting `ncclCommInitRank`/NVLS proxy setup failure. The TP8 run above therefore exercises `ncclCommSuspend`/`ncclCommResume` over plain socket transport (`NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=0`), not the NVLink fabric path — both are the same NCCL communicator-suspend code this PR adds, but a rack with working IMEX container injection would be a stronger cross-node signal. ## Scope NCCL only. FlashInfer's all-reduce-fusion workspace (and MoE all2all workspace) GPU memory is **not** released during sleep in this PR. Investigated and deferred, not overlooked: - FlashInfer's `AllReduceFusionWorkspace` (MNNVL/TRTLLM) has no suspend/resume primitive analogous to `ncclCommSuspend`/`ncclCommResume` — only `checkpoint_prepare()`/`checkpoint_restore()` (added for #46877's separate checkpoint lifecycle, flashinfer >= 0.6.16). - Wiring `CudaCommunicator.suspend()`/`resume()` to call those checkpoint hooks directly (reuse, no new machinery) was tried and reverted: `checkpoint_prepare()`/`checkpoint_restore()` are reachable via `async_llm.checkpoint_prepare()`'s independent RPC path with no mutual exclusion against `sleep()`/`wake_up()`, so an interleaved call would double-release/rebuild the same workspace. Matches [galletas1712's #46234 comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46234#discussion_r3504640029) that "NCCL checkpoint and ncclCommSuspend are not really composable." - `DeviceCommunicatorBase.suspend()/resume()` (this PR) is the generic override point galletas1712 requested for future FlashInfer comm suspension; it's ready to host a real implementation once flashinfer exposes a dedicated suspend/resume primitive. ## Why this is not duplicate work No open PR implements `ncclCommSuspend`/`ncclCommResume`. #46877 is the separate process-checkpoint lifecycle (its hooks are deliberately no-ops for NCCL); #35934 tears down communicators for CRIU; RFC #52125 (L3 snapshot) references this PR as the ordinary-sleep counterpart. ## AI disclosure AI assistance (Claude, Codex) was used for the redesign analysis, implementation, and on-node validation; three candidate architectures were implemented and validated head-to-head before choosing this one. The submitter reviewed every changed line.

signal.title: [Bugfix][DSv4] Revert adaptive C128A metadata packing
signal.text: ## Summary Revert the adaptive C128A top-k width and packed persistent-buffer views introduced by #50004. The C128A metadata builder runs before FULL CUDA graph replay, but the sparse decode consumer is captured and reuses its capture-time row layout. With #50004, runtime metadata writes packed rows using a batch-dependent `active_topk_width`, while the captured consumer retained the capture-time row stride. Row 0 still started at offset 0, but later rows could be read from stale offsets. This change restores: - `c128a_max_compressed` as the metadata width - capacity-strided slices of the persistent decode and prefill buffers - each persistent buffer's `stride(0)` for Triton metadata writes - removal of the test that asserted the packed layout being reverted Fixes #52448. ## Validation ```text git diff --check .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py vllm/models/deepseek_v4/sparse_mla.py ``` All applicable hooks passed, including ruff, formatting, typos, mypy, SPDX, lazy-import, and forbidden-import checks. The full revert was also evaluated with the exact #52448 request on 2x NVIDIA GB300 using `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` revision `7872f01b1d1fe23eabc4c98b48bffcef5a386062`, TP=2 plus expert parallelism, DSpark-7, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, `max_model_len=70000`, concurrency 32, and `max_tokens=16384`: - 256 priming requests plus 256 measured requests - 0/256 issue-signature hits - 0 request errors and 0 `length` finishes - 253 `tool_calls` finishes and 3 `stop` finishes - 8.445 s median measured latency ## Contribution notes - Not a duplicate: `52448 in:body` found no other open PR. The open C128A/sparse-MLA keyword matches (#48805, #41836, and #41834) address warmup, prefill, or model enablement rather than reverting #50004. This updates the existing #51318 instead of opening another PR. - AI assistance was used for investigation, patch preparation, validation, and this PR update. The submitting human must review every changed line and be able to defend the change before merge.

signal.title: [ROCM][Bugfix] Deferring to TRITON_ATTN backend for Prefix lm models instead of ROCM_ATTN and fixed minor bug in Gemma3 Multimodal code
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes incorrect attention behavior for prefix-LM multimodal models (e.g., Gemma3) on ROCm. This is a correctness fix. **Root cause:** Both `RocmAttentionBackend` and `RocmAiterUnifiedAttentionBackend` overrode `supports_mm_prefix()` to return `True`, but neither backend actually implements the `mm_prefix_range_tensor` passing required for bidirectional image-token attention during prefill. As a result, prefix-LM multimodal models on ROCm were silently falling through with wrong attention masks and image tokens were not attending to each other bidirectionally as required by models like Gemma3. **Changes:** 1. **`rocm_attn.py` / `rocm_aiter_unified_attn.py`**: Removed the incorrect `supports_mm_prefix() -> True` overrides. Both backends now inherit the base-class default (`False`), causing the attention backend selector to correctly defer to Triton unified attention for prefix-LM models on ROCm. 2. **`gemma3_mm.py`**: Explicitly sets `config.text_config.is_mm_prefix_lm = True` in the multimodal constructor, since the text-only Gemma3 path does not set this flag but the multimodal path requires it for correct image-token attention. 3. **`rocm.py`**: Ports the `disable_chunked_mm_input` guard from the CUDA platform path to ROCm. For prefix-LM multimodal models, chunked prefill can split a multimodal item and break the intended bidirectional attention pattern; this ensures ROCm disables it automatically, matching CUDA behavior. 4. **`tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_attention_selector.py`**: Adds a regression test asserting that both ROCm backends do not claim `mm_prefix` support, guarding against this being re-introduced silently. ## Test Plan **Unit test (ROCm):** ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_attention_selector.py \ -v -k test_rocm_backends_do_not_support_mm_prefix ``` lm-eval benchmarks ran are as follows: Text-only tasks (lmeval) - HellaSwag, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, PIQA, BoolQ, WinoGrande (Gemma3 4B and 12B): ```bash # 4B python -m lm_eval \ --model vllm \ --model_args "pretrained=google/gemma-3-4b-it,dtype=bfloat16,max_model_len=2048,tensor_parallel_size=1,gpu_memory_utilization=0.85" \ --tasks hellaswag,arc_easy,arc_challenge,piqa,boolq,winogrande \ --batch_size 16 # 12B python -m lm_eval \ --model vllm \ --model_args "pretrained=google/gemma-3-12b-it,dtype=bfloat16,max_model_len=2048,tensor_parallel_size=1,gpu_memory_utilization=0.95" \ --tasks hellaswag,arc_easy,arc_challenge,piqa,boolq,winogrande \ --batch_size 16 ``` Multimodal task - `MMMU-val`: ```bash # 4B python -m lm_eval \ --model vllm-vlm \ --model_args "pretrained=google/gemma-3-4b-it,dtype=bfloat16,max_model_len=4096,max_images=1,tensor_parallel_size=1,gpu_memory_utilization=0.85" \ --tasks mmmu_val \ --batch_size 4 \ --apply_chat_template # 12B python -m lm_eval \ --model vllm-vlm \ --model_args "pretrained=google/gemma-3-12b-it,dtype=bfloat16,max_model_len=4096,max_images=1,tensor_parallel_size=1,gpu_memory_utilization=0.95" \ --tasks mmmu_val \ --batch_size 4 \ --apply_chat_template ``` ## Test Result No regression observed here. Hardware used was `AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700` ### Text benchmarks **Gemma3-4B**: ### Text benchmarks **Gemma3-4B**: | Task | Baseline (before fix) | With fix | Delta | |------|:---------------------:|:--------:|:---:| | arc_challenge | 0.5341 ± 0.0146 | 0.5324 ± 0.0146 | -0.0017 | | arc_easy | 0.8249 ± 0.0078 | 0.8237 ± 0.0078 | -0.0012 | | boolq | 0.8410 ± 0.0064 | 0.8407 ± 0.0064 | -0.0003 | | hellaswag | 0.5583 ± 0.0050 | 0.5591 ± 0.0050 | +0.0008 | | piqa | 0.7644 ± 0.0099 | 0.7639 ± 0.0099 | -0.0005 | | winogrande | 0.6969 ± 0.0129 | 0.6938 ± 0.0130 | -0.0031 | **Gemma3-12B**: | Task | Baseline (before fix) | With fix | Delta | |------|:---------------------:|:--------:|:---:| | arc_challenge | 0.6092 ± 0.0143 | 0.6118 ± 0.0142 | +0.0026 | | arc_easy | 0.8342 ± 0.0076 | 0.8350 ± 0.0076 | +0.0008 | | boolq | 0.8746 ± 0.0058 | 0.8743 ± 0.0058 | -0.0003 | | hellaswag | 0.6270 ± 0.0048 | 0.6271 ± 0.0048 | +0.0001 | | piqa | 0.8036 ± 0.0093 | 0.8003 ± 0.0093 | -0.0033 | | winogrande | 0.7451 ± 0.0122 | 0.7482 ± 0.0122 | +0.0031 | ### Multimodal benchmark (MMMU-val) | Model | Baseline (before fix) | With fix | Delta | |-------|:---------------------:|:--------:|:---:| | Gemma3-4B-IT | 0.4067 ± 0.0157 | 0.4133 ± 0.0158 | +0.0066 | | Gemma3-12B-IT | 0.4856 ± 0.0159 | 0.4922 ± 0.0158 | +0.0066 | ### **Edit: 24 July 2026** #### Reproducing the benchmarks **Additional multimodal tasks (lmms-eval)** - DocVQA, InfoVQA, AI2D, ChartQA, VQAv2 (Gemma3 4B and 12B): ```bash # 4B python -m lmms_eval eval \ --model vllm \ --model_args "model=google/gemma-3-4b-it,dtype=bfloat16,max_model_len=4096,tensor_parallel_size=1,gpu_memory_utilization=0.85" \ --tasks ai2d,chartqa,docvqa_val,infovqa_val,vqav2_val \ --batch_size 8 \ --limit 1000 \ --seed 0 # 12B python -m lmms_eval eval \ --model vllm \ --model_args "model=google/gemma-3-12b-it,dtype=bfloat16,max_model_len=4096,tensor_parallel_size=1,gpu_memory_utilization=0.95" \ --tasks ai2d,chartqa,docvqa_val,infovqa_val,vqav2_val \ --batch_size 8 \ --limit 1000 \ --seed 0 ``` > > Note: the `lmms-eval==0.7.2` wheel ships **without** the `_default_template_*_yaml` task templates, so install it editable from the tag: > `git clone --branch v0.7.2 https://github.com/EvolvingLMMs-Lab/lmms-eval && pip install -e ./lmms-eval --no-deps && pip install decord Levenshtein` > #### Multimodal benchmarks (lmms-eval) Multimodal accuracy improves on every text-in-image task. **Gemma3-4B**: | Task | Baseline (before fix) | With fix | Delta | |------|:---------------------:|:--------:|:---:| | ai2d (exact_match) | 0.6750 ± 0.0148 | 0.7280 ± 0.0141 | +0.0530 | | chartqa (relaxed_overall) | 0.2850 ± 0.0143 | 0.3480 ± 0.0151 | +0.0630 | | docvqa_val (anls) | 0.5938 ± 0.0143 | 0.7124 ± 0.0131 | +0.1186 | | infovqa_val (anls) | 0.3462 ± 0.0139 | 0.4046 ± 0.0144 | +0.0584 | | vqav2_val (exact_match) | 0.5720 ± 0.0148 | 0.5799 ± 0.0147 | +0.0079 | **Gemma3-12B**: | Task | Baseline (before fix) | With fix | Delta | |------|:---------------------:|:--------:|:---:| | ai2d (exact_match) | 0.7810 ± 0.0131 | 0.8030 ± 0.0126 | +0.0220 | | chartqa (relaxed_overall) | 0.4040 ± 0.0155 | 0.4470 ± 0.0157 | +0.0430 | | docvqa_val (anls) | 0.6995 ± 0.0134 | 0.7857 ± 0.0120 | +0.0862 | | infovqa_val (anls) | 0.4456 ± 0.0145 | 0.5123 ± 0.0148 | +0.0667 | | vqav2_val (exact_match) | 0.6397 ± 0.0143 | 0.6270 ± 0.0145 | -0.0127 |
